components.accessibility: Radix-backed native buttons expose expanded state and labelled panels. Arrow Up/Down and Home/End navigate enabled headers within the current accordion; Enter/Space toggle. Disabled items are skipped. Headings default to h3 and can follow the document hierarchy. Closed panels are inert during animation and unmounted afterward; forceMount retains hidden, inert content. Reduced motion is respected.
notes: `Accordion` and `AccordionGroup` from the package root are the items-based convenience API. Use `AccordionRoot` for compound composition. The named `Accordion` from the `core/Accordion` subpath remains the compound root for compatibility.
Give every item a stable, unique, non-empty string value. Single mode uses a string; multiple mode uses an array. An explicit undefined controlled value collapses every panel.

The group opens the first enabled item by default. Use `defaultValue={null}` for a collapsed single group or `defaultValue={[]}` in multiple mode. AccordionRoot starts closed unless a default is supplied.
Existing render-function children and explicit `isOpen` / `onClick` composition remain supported. New compound usage manages state and ARIA associations automatically.
Leading content and badges must be noninteractive. Put links, inputs, and action buttons inside AccordionContent. Provide an appropriate headingLevel for nested sections.
forceMount preserves form state but does not omit closed inputs from native form submission. Consumers own persistence, validation, and submission scope.

components.readme:
# Accordion Stacked sections whose headers expand and collapse their content. Use it for FAQs, settings groups, and long reference content that readers scan before opening one part. For a single show-more toggle, use `Collapsible`. ```jsx import { AccordionGroup, Icon, Pill } from '@gaudi/design-system'; import '@gaudi/design-system/global.css'; , badge: New, content:

Account settings content.

} ]} /> ``` ## State and variants - `type`: `single` (default) or `multiple`. - `value` / `onValueChange`: controlled state. Single close emits `undefined`; multiple changes emit an array. Explicit `value={undefined}` keeps a controlled single root collapsed. - `defaultValue`: initial uncontrolled state. A group opens the first enabled item by default, including as an array in multiple mode. Pass `null` (single) or `[]` (multiple) to start closed. `AccordionRoot` starts closed by default. - `collapsible={false}`: keep the current single panel open until another is selected. - `disabled`: disable all root items; item `disabled` disables a single trigger. - `variant`: `outline` (default), `flush`, `separated`, `solid`, or `framed`. - `indicator`: `chevron` (default), `plus-minus`, `arrow`, a React node, `({ isOpen }) => ReactNode`, or `null`. Override on an individual item/trigger. - `indicatorPosition`: logical `start` or `end` (default). `dir='rtl'` sets both layout and navigation direction. - `highlight`: accent background for an expanded header. - `headingLevel`: 2–6; defaults to 3. Override at root, item, or trigger. Give each item a unique, nonempty string `value`. An item's `title` and `content` accept React nodes. `leading`, `description`, and `badge` enrich the trigger. `className`, `triggerClassName`, and `contentClassName` customize each group item; native props and refs pass through the compound primitives. `AccordionContent` applies `className` to its padded inner body and its remaining native props/ref to the animated region. ## Composition ```jsx import { AccordionRoot, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent, Input } from '@gaudi/design-system'; Profile ``` The package-root `Accordion` remains an alias for `AccordionGroup`. Use `AccordionRoot` for unambiguous compound composition. The existing named `Accordion` export from `@gaudi/design-system/core/Accordion` remains the compound root. Legacy render-function children receive `{ currentValue, setValue, type }`; explicit `isOpen`, `onClick`, `contentId`, `id`, and `labelledBy` wiring remains supported. ## Accessibility and content lifecycle Each header is a native button inside a heading, with unique IDs associating the trigger and content. Header descriptions are separate accessible descriptions; decorative icons/avatars do not duplicate names. Choose heading levels to fit the page. Keep header slots noninteractive and place links, buttons, and form controls inside content. Tab follows the normal document order. Enter/Space toggles a header. Arrow Up/Down navigates enabled headers with wrapping; Home/End moves to the first/last. Nested groups maintain separate navigation. Disabled items are skipped. Open/close height and indicator motion respects reduced-motion preferences. Closed content is inert during its exit animation, then unmounted. `forceMount` retains content while hiding it visually and from keyboard/screen-reader navigation, preserving form drafts. Hidden retained inputs still participate in native form submission: applications own validation and submission scope. Avoid unnecessary region proliferation in very large multiple-open groups; set `role={undefined}` on compound content when appropriate.

components.readme:
# Attachment

A file row, compact pill or image tile with media, a name, a status line and actions. Use the same parts for images, documents, audio, video, links, source files and spreadsheets in composer trays, upload queues and messages. `state` drives the idle, uploading, processing, done and error styling.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Attachment, AttachmentAction, AttachmentActions, AttachmentContent, AttachmentDescription, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentTrigger } from '@gaudi/design-system';
import { RegistryIcon } from '@gaudi/design-system/icons';

const file = { id: 'cover', name: 'campaign-cover.jpg', type: 'image/jpeg', previewUrl: '/uploads/campaign-cover.jpg' };

<Attachment>
  <AttachmentMedia file={file} />
  <AttachmentContent>
    <AttachmentTitle title={file.name}>{file.name}</AttachmentTitle>
    <AttachmentDescription>Image · ready to send</AttachmentDescription>
  </AttachmentContent>
  <AttachmentTrigger aria-label={`Preview ${file.name}`} onClick={() => openPreview(file)} />
  <AttachmentActions>
    <AttachmentAction aria-label={`Remove ${file.name}`} onClick={() => remove(file.id)}><RegistryIcon lucide='X' /></AttachmentAction>
  </AttachmentActions>
</Attachment>
```

The host supplies `previewUrl` for a thumbnail or video poster. It is an image source, not a playable media URL. Without it, `AttachmentMedia` chooses an icon from the MIME type or filename extension; `kind: 'link'` chooses a globe. A failed thumbnail falls back to the file icon. File content, image previews, audio/video playback and download destinations stay with the host.

Explicit children still support custom artwork, progress or state feedback:

```jsx
<AttachmentMedia><RegistryIcon lucide='TriangleAlert' /></AttachmentMedia>
<AttachmentMedia file={file} variant='icon' />
```

The second form deliberately shows the file icon even when a preview URL exists.

## Parts

| Part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `Attachment` | `state`, `size` (default, sm, xs) and `orientation` (horizontal, vertical). |
| `AttachmentMedia` | Optional `file={{ name, type?, mediaType?, kind?, previewUrl? }}` provides a file icon or supplied thumbnail. MIME type takes precedence over the filename extension; `kind='link'` identifies links. Explicit children take precedence over automatic media. `variant='icon'` suppresses the thumbnail; `variant='image'` supports composed image children. |
| `AttachmentTitle`, `AttachmentDescription` | File name and status line; both truncate. |
| `AttachmentActions`, `AttachmentAction` | Icon buttons built on Button (`size='icon-xs'`, ghost by default). |
| `AttachmentTrigger` | A full-card button or link, for selectable tiles. |
| `AttachmentGroup` | A horizontally scrolling strip. |

## Layouts and examples

- [Mixed media · detailed rows](?path=/story/core-attachment--mixed-media) places full-width Attachment rows in a labelled list. It includes a local image, PDF, audio, video, a supplied poster, a link, code and a spreadsheet, with selection, removal, reset and failed-thumbnail recovery.
- [Mixed media · wrapping pills](?path=/story/core-attachment--compact-pills) uses `size='xs'` inside a `flex flex-wrap` list for compact inline attachments. Each pill stays within its parent width and retains its own remove action.
- [Images · thumbnail grid](?path=/story/core-attachment--image-grid) uses `orientation='vertical'` inside a two-column grid that expands to three columns at `sm`. Selecting a tile displays its local image preview.

Use a labelled `ul` with one `li` per attachment for wrapping pills, grids or detailed lists. `AttachmentGroup` remains useful when horizontal scrolling is intentional. The examples reuse local artwork; audio, video, document and link entries are explicitly sample metadata with no fake player or download destination.

## Accessibility

Name every icon-only action after its file ("Remove report.pdf") so a list of buttons stays distinguishable. Keep `AttachmentTrigger` and `AttachmentActions` as siblings so the full-card action never nests a remove button. The filename names the automatic decorative media; a full preview needs descriptive alternative text. Keep focus on an available control after removal, and announce selection or attachment-count changes with a concise status.

components.readme:
# Avatar

A person, workspace or source shown as a photo, initials or an icon, with an optional presence badge. `Avatar` and `AvatarGroup` are built on the `AvatarRoot`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarFallback` and `AvatarBadge` parts.

Image examples use Gaudi's own illustrated avatars bundled with Storybook (`/avatars/person-20.svg`, generated deterministically from a seed) with fictional demo identities, so examples never load images from the network. The same avatars appear in sizes, account menus, presence badges, reviewer rosters and other component examples. Initials, color surfaces, workspace marks and broken-image states remain explicit fallback demonstrations. These URLs are fixture data; applications supply their own `src`. See the [portrait reference](../../../../.storybook/public/avatars/README.md).

```jsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Avatar
  name='Mei Castellanos'
  src={person.photoUrl}
  shape='circle'
  indicator={{ label: 'Online', tone: 'success' }}
/>

<AvatarGroup avatars={people} max={3} size='md' label='Review team' />
```

| Prop | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `src` | Remote, local or data image URL. Pending, missing and failed images show fallback content; changing the source resets loading. |
| `name` / `label` | Name generates Unicode-aware initials from the first and last words; a single word uses up to two characters. The 16px `2xs` size shows only the first initial so it stays legible at the `text-xs` step. Label preserves explicitly supplied initials. |
| `alt` | Overrides the accessible identity; `alt=''` makes the avatar decorative beside visible text. |
| `fallback` | Custom text or noninteractive artwork; `true` renders the guest silhouette. Empty names show `?`. |
| `size` | `2xs`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`: 16, 20, 32, 40, 56 and 80px. Existing sizes retain their dimensions. |
| `shape` | `square` (default), `circle`, `tile`. Image and fallback inherit the same shape. |
| `surface` | `solid` (default, selected tone), `tinted`, `plain` or `bare`. Plain/bare default to `contain`; solid/tinted use `cover`. |
| `tone` | Existing gray, neutral, blue, teal, green, amber, yellow, red, rose and indigo colors. |
| `fit` / `grayscale` | Image crop (`cover` or `contain`) and optional grayscale treatment. |
| `indicator` | `{ label, tone?, icon?, position?, className? }`. Label is required; status is always supplied by the application. |
| `children` | Additional noninteractive `AvatarBadge` content. Provide its meaning in the root `aria-label`. |
| `onLoadingStatusChange` | Receives `loading`, `loaded` or `error` for host-owned feedback. |
| `imageProps`, `imageClassName`, `fallbackClassName` | Native image attributes and per-layer appearance. Identity alt text is owned by the root. |
| `ref`, native attributes | Forwarded to the root span. Wrap Avatar in Button, Tooltip or DropdownMenu for interaction. |

Indicators support `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `neutral` and `primary`, and `top-start`, `top-end`, `bottom-start`, `bottom-end` positions. Logical positions follow reading direction. Presence remains separate from loading or failure. The face retains its rounded crop while badges remain outside its bounds.

## Groups

`AvatarGroup` continues to accept compound children. Pass `avatars` for data-driven composition: each entry contains a unique stable `id` plus Avatar props. `max` defaults to four; positive fractions round down to at least one, and zero/negative/non-finite values show all. Empty lists have no overflow count. Supply surrounding empty-state copy where appropriate.

`size`, `shape` and `label` apply to the group. `renderAvatar(avatar, person)` and `renderOverflow(count, overflow)` wrap the supplied elements with existing buttons, tooltips or dialogs. `formatOverflow(count)` supplies translated overflow text. Large groups scroll within their own bounds. Compound APIs remain available as `AvatarRoot`, `AvatarImage`, `AvatarFallback`, `AvatarBadge` and `AvatarGroupCount` from this owner and the package root.

components.readme:
# Banner

A banner is a full-width strip for a site-wide message: a release, maintenance, or a billing problem. For a message inside the page, next to the content it is about, compose `Alert`.

```jsx
import { Banner } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Banner title='Gaudi 2.0 is out' href='/changelog' tone='accent' variant='solid'>
  New tokens and a faster docs site.
</Banner>
```

- `tone` carries meaning (`neutral`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `attention`, `discovery`); older hue names still work.
- `variant`: `solid` for the one announcement that matters most, `soft` or `outline` for routine notices. `size` sets the padding.
- With `href` the whole message is one link; without it the banner is announced as a status.

## Alert

`Alert`, `AlertTitle`, `AlertDescription` and `AlertAction` build an inline message with an icon, text and actions. `variant` is `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `invert`. `AlertRoot` and the `*Primitive` names are aliases of the same parts.

components.readme:
# Breadcrumb

A trail of links from the site root to the current page. Use it on nested pages (docs, categories, settings) so readers can see where they are and step back up a level.

```jsx
import { BreadcrumbTrail } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<BreadcrumbTrail
  items={[
    { href: '/', label: 'Home' },
    { href: '/blog', label: 'Blog' },
    { label: 'Design systems' }
  ]}
/>
```

`BreadcrumbTrail` (the default export) renders a labelled `nav`, an ordered list, router-aware links for ancestors and `aria-current="page"` on the last item (or the item marked `current`). `label` names the landmark.

For icons, collapsed paths or menus in the trail, compose the parts: `Breadcrumb`, `BreadcrumbList`, `BreadcrumbItem`, `BreadcrumbLink`, `BreadcrumbPage`, `BreadcrumbSeparator` and `BreadcrumbEllipsis`. The convenience names are the same parts with a labelled landmark and Gaudi `Link` for internal routes; `BreadcrumbLinkPrimitive` and friends are the raw parts (`asChild` on the link accepts a router link).

components.readme:
# Button

A button starts an action: submit a form, save a draft, open a dialog. Pass `href` to get a link that looks like a button.

```jsx
import { Button } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Button variant='outline' tone='neutral'>Cancel</Button>
<Button>Publish article</Button>
```

- `variant` sets the hierarchy: `solid` for the one primary action, `outline` or `soft` for supporting actions, `ghost` and `subtle` for low-emphasis ones.
- `tone` carries meaning (`accent`, `neutral`, `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `attention`, `discovery`). Pick it by intent, not colour.
- Sizes share heights with inputs and selects: `xs` 24px, `sm` 28px, `md` 32px, `lg` 36px. Icon-only buttons use `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`, `icon`, `icon-lg` and need an `aria-label`.
- `href` renders an internal link, or a new-tab anchor for external URLs. `disabled` works on both buttons and links.
- `asChild` passes the button styles to your own element, such as a router link.

components.readme:
# ButtonGroup

A button group joins related buttons into one control: a toolbar, a split button, a pager, or an input with its action.

```jsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup, ButtonGroupSeparator } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ButtonGroup aria-label='Reply'>
  <Button>Reply all</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <Button size='icon' aria-label='More reply options'>…</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

- Give each group an `aria-label` so assistive tech announces what the buttons do together.
- `orientation='vertical'` stacks the buttons; turn any `ButtonGroupSeparator` to `horizontal` with it.
- `ButtonGroupText` holds a label or value (such as "Page 2 of 26") inside the group.
- Groups can hold inputs and selects, and can nest to keep a small gap between sets.

components.readme:
# Calendar

A month grid for picking one date, several dates or a range. Use it inline or inside a Popover for a date field; use `DateSelector` when people filter by day, month, quarter, half-year or year.

```jsx
import { Calendar } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Calendar mode='range' selected={range} onSelect={setRange} numberOfMonths={2} disabled={{ before: new Date() }} />
```

- `mode` is `single`, `multiple` or `range`. `disabled` takes dates, ranges or matchers, and `footer` shows a summary under the grid.
- `captionLayout` switches the header between a label and month or year dropdowns; `showOutsideDays`, `showWeekNumber` and `numberOfMonths` shape the grid.
- Day cells are squares of `--cell-size` (32px, 40px on touch screens). Set the variable on the calendar to fit custom day content; the month never stretches to fill its container.
- `CalendarDayButton` is the default day cell, for custom `components.DayButton` renderers.

## DateSelector

`DateSelector` combines an is/before/after/between filter, period tabs and a calendar or period grid, with optional typed input. Pass `value` / `onChange` and translate every string with `i18n`.

The period grid shows `yearRange` years (10 by default) around `baseYear`, or the current year when omitted. Pass both `minYear` and `maxYear` to supply an explicit inclusive year window.

An empty `value` clears a previous selection, including a cancelled draft in an overlay that is still closing. Hosts keep committed and draft values separate when using Apply and Cancel.

## Accessibility

Days are buttons in a grid with the full date as their name. Arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, and disabled days cannot be picked.

## Implementation ownership

`Calendar` owns the DayPicker bridge. DateSelector formatting, labels, state and context are separate from its private day/period views and controls. All supported exports remain available from the Calendar entry.

components.readme:
# Carousel

Shows one item at a time, or a scrolling rail of cards, with previous and next buttons, dot indicators, and arrow-key navigation. Use it for featured content that readers browse in order; use a grid when every item should be visible at once.

```jsx
import { Carousel } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Carousel
  ariaLabel='Featured articles'
  loop
  items={[
    { id: 'graphs', title: 'An Introduction to Knowledge Graphs', eyebrow: 'Knowledge Graphs', image: '/images/art/2.svg', href: '/blog', action: 'Read article' }
  ]}
/>
```

- `variant='standard'` shows one slide with its call to action. `variant='rail'` shows snapping cards; selecting a card opens its `content` in a dialog.
- `loop` wraps navigation at the ends. `controls={false}` hides the previous and next buttons; the indicators stay.
- `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the maximum width and slide height; `radius` sets the corners.

## Parts

`Carousel` is built on the `CarouselRoot`, `CarouselContent`, `CarouselItem`, `CarouselPrevious`, and `CarouselNext` parts. Compose them directly for custom layouts such as thumbnails, multiple slides per view, vertical carousels, or autoplay (pass Embla `opts` and `plugins` to `CarouselRoot`). `useCarousel` exposes the Embla API inside the root.

# Cascader

Pick a value from a nested tree: a help topic, a folder, a region and its markets. Use it when options only make sense within their parent; use a Select for a flat list.

```jsx
import { Cascader, CascaderTrigger, CascaderValue, CascaderContent, CascaderPanel, CascaderList, CascaderItems } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Cascader items={topics} onValueChange={setTopic}>
  <CascaderTrigger aria-label='Topic'><CascaderValue /></CascaderTrigger>
  <CascaderContent>
    <CascaderPanel>
      <CascaderList><CascaderItems /></CascaderList>
    </CascaderPanel>
  </CascaderContent>
</Cascader>
```

- `items` are `{ value, label, children?, description?, icon?, disabled? }`. `mode` shows the tree as a drill-down list, Miller columns (`CascaderColumns`) or an expanding tree.
- `selectable='any'` lets branches be picked, not only leaves; `multiple` adds checkboxes and chips.
- `inline` renders the panel in the page instead of a popup. `CascaderInput`, `CascaderBreadcrumb`, `CascaderEmpty`, `CascaderStatus` and `CascaderFooter` add search, a path, empty and async states, and footer actions.
- `useCascaderLoader` fetches children on demand; `CascaderVirtualItems` windows long levels.
- `readOnly` preserves selection across active and background columns; `disabled` also disables navigation and dims every row. Both constraints follow prop changes.

## Accessibility

The trigger is a combobox. Up and Down move through a level, the inline-end and inline-start arrow keys open and leave a branch, and Enter picks. A live region announces changes, and every visible or announced string comes from `labels`.

## Implementation ownership

`Cascader` coordinates the controlled state and contexts. Owner-local hooks manage prepared rows, announcements, navigation and the Combobox callback contract. Trigger/chip and panel rendering live in private `components/` modules; the loader remains responsible for asynchronous children.

# Checkbox

A box people tick to turn one option on or off, or to pick several options from a list. Use a Switch instead when the change applies straight away.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Checkbox } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Checkbox label='Email me when someone replies' defaultChecked onCheckedChange={setReplies} />;
```

`Checkbox` pairs the box with a clickable label. For descriptions, cards, nested groups or the indeterminate state, compose `CheckboxRoot` with the Field parts (`Field`, `FieldLabel`, `FieldContent`, `FieldDescription`).

## Accessibility

The box is a `checkbox` with `aria-checked` (`mixed` when indeterminate), toggled by Space or a click on its label. A disabled checkbox dims its label too.

components.readme:
# CodeBlock

Render source code, streaming code, diffs or prepared highlighted lines with optional line numbers, wrapping, selection and folding. Compose a header and actions through the same CodeBlock context.

```jsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockTitle
} from '@gaudi/design-system/core/CodeBlock';

<CodeBlock code={source} language='javascript' showLineNumbers>
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTitle>example.js</CodeBlockTitle>
    <CodeBlockCopyButton />
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockContent />
</CodeBlock>
```

`highlight={false}` renders plain source immediately. `wrap` / `onWrapChange`, `expanded` / `onExpandedChange`, `selectedLines` / `onSelectedLinesChange`, and `folded` / `onFoldedChange` support host-controlled state. Folding uses source line numbers; supplied `foldRegions` can replace indentation-based discovery. Copy and download actions use the current source.

## Implementation ownership

The root owns document state and highlighting. `CodeBlockContext.jsx` shares that state with private line, surface, header and control modules under `components/`. `codeBlockFolding.js` contains the independent fold model; `CodeBlockHighlight.jsx` owns highlighting and source parsing. Consumers use the public owner entry.

Selectable code uses a single focusable grid of source-line rows. Arrow keys, Home and End move the active line; Space or Enter toggles selection, and Shift extends it. Line actions remain real buttons inside a grid cell so their own Enter/Space behavior is preserved.

`CodeBlockCopyButton` announces copy success and failures in a polite live region. A failed attempt stays available as **Retry copy** until the next successful attempt. Override `labels.copy`, `labels.copied`, `labels.retry`, and `labels.error` for translated feedback; `onCopyError` lets the host react to a blocked clipboard.

components.accessibility: The canvas supports mouse, pen, and touch. Its two keyboard stops adjust saturation and brightness with visible thumb focus; hue and opacity also support arrows and Home/End. Presets expose selection with a checkmark and pressed state. Invalid drafts have associated errors.
notes: Hex/CSS text commits on Enter or blur; Escape restores the current color. Invalid drafts never change the selection. RGB and HSL use Gaudi NumberField.

With opacity controls shown, three- or six-digit hex preserves opacity; four- or eight-digit hex sets alpha explicitly. Screen sampling always preserves opacity. CSS names and other color spaces are unsupported.

components.readme:
# ColorPicker

An inline color editor with a saturation/brightness canvas, hue and opacity sliders, HEX/RGB/HSL/CSS entry, screen eyedropper, and optional preset swatches. Its layout follows the [shadcn.io Color Picker](https://www.shadcn.io/components/color-picker), composed with Gaudi's Slider, Input, NumberField, NativeSelect, and Button primitives.

```jsx
import { ColorPicker } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ColorPicker';

<ColorPicker
  label='Accent color'
  name='accent'
  value={color}
  onValueChange={setColor}
  swatches={['#2563eb', '#16a34a', '#f59e0b', '#e11d48']}
  description='Used for links and primary actions.'
/>
```

Use `defaultValue` (default `#2563eb`) for uncontrolled state. Values accept three-, four-, six-, or eight-digit hex with an optional `#`, plus numeric `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, and `hsla()` values. RGB percentages, percentage alpha, and space/slash forms are supported; CSS names, variables, and other color spaces are not. Callbacks and form values use lowercase six-digit hex when opaque, or eight digits when translucent. Alpha is quantized to an 8-bit channel. Invalid supplied values fall back to `#2563eb`; invalid and duplicate swatches are omitted.

`defaultFormat` selects the initial editor (`hex`, `rgb`, `hsl`, or `css`). Changing format does not change the selected color. RGB and HSL offer labelled numeric channels; CSS accepts a color expression and displays `rgba()`. Hex and CSS edits commit on Enter or blur. Invalid drafts show an associated error without changing the selection; Escape cancels the draft. A host color change discards pending text permanently. Controlled values remain authoritative, even when the host refuses a change.

`showAlpha` (default `true`) shows the opacity slider and percentage field. Hiding these controls preserves existing alpha; the hex field then includes alpha when present. With opacity controls visible, three- or six-digit hex edits preserve current opacity. Four- or eight-digit hex explicitly replaces alpha. The eyedropper always preserves current opacity; selecting a preset adopts that preset's alpha. `showEyeDropper` (default `true`) shows the sampling button; it is disabled when the browser lacks the EyeDropper API or a secure context. Sampling starts only on a click. Cancellation is silent, failures can be retried, and changing the color, disabling the picker, making it read-only, or hiding/unmounting the eyedropper aborts pending sampling.

`name` submits the current valid color. Form reset clears drafts, restores the initial uncontrolled color, and calls `onValueChange` if it changes. Controlled resets leave the host value intact. `disabled` prevents interaction and form submission. `readOnly` keeps values selectable and submitted; format switching remains available for inspection.

The visible `label` names the group and every control. The canvas uses pointer capture for mouse, pen, and touch; its two keyboard stops reuse Gaudi Slider for saturation and brightness. Arrow keys adjust values, Home/End jump to bounds, and the visible canvas thumb shows keyboard focus. Hue is retained when selecting black or gray. Presets expose selection with a checkmark and `aria-pressed`. Text and numeric editors inherit InputConfigProvider. `description` explains the picker and is associated with its canvas keyboard controls and text editor. `id` targets the hex/CSS input; remaining DOM props and `className` apply to the root group.

The canvas fills its container. At a container width of 20rem (320px at the default root font size) or narrower, the value editor moves below the toolbar; RGB, HSL, and CSS always use a full-width second row. Swatches wrap within the component. No native color popup or additional runtime dependency is required.

components.readme:
# Commander

The site-wide command launcher: navigation, full-text search across posts, projects, thoughts, publications and tags, contact links and a theme switch. Open it from a visible trigger such as `MenuSearch`, or with ⌘K / Ctrl+K.

## Usage

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Commander, MenuSearch } from '@gaudi/design-system';

const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
const navigation = [{ id: 'library', title: 'Library', href: '/library' }];
const posts = [{ id: 'release', title: 'Release notes', href: '/articles/release-notes' }];

<MenuSearch setOpen={setOpen} />
<Commander open={open} setOpen={setOpen} navigation={navigation} posts={posts} />
```

## API

| Prop                                            | Type                     | Contract                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open / setOpen`                                | boolean / function       | Controlled visibility; ⌘K / Ctrl+K toggles it through `setOpen`.      |
| `navigation`                                   | Array                    | Prepared destinations; defaults to an empty list.                    |
| `posts / projects / thoughts / publications / tags` | Array                | Each non-empty collection adds a page and full-text results.          |
| `social`                                        | Array                    | Contact entries; defaults to the links in the site metadata.          |
| `restoreFocusRef`                               | Ref                      | Where focus returns when the element that opened the launcher is gone. |

Each destination or collection entry supplies a stable `id` (`slug` is a fallback), a `title`, and an explicit `href` or `onClick`. `disabled` prevents selection and `closeOnSelect={false}` keeps the launcher open for an action. Prepared titles, categories, subtitles, IDs and destinations are preserved, including empty and zero values. Collection names group entries; they do not construct routes. Home, Blog and About links must be supplied through `navigation` when the application uses those destinations.

## Composition

Commander is built on the Command parts it exports: `Command`, `CommandInput`, `CommandList`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandItem`, `CommandEmpty`, `CommandSeparator`, `CommandShortcut`, `CommandFooter` and `CommandDialog`. Use them for inline palettes or your own command dialog; `CommandInput` renders its children at the end of the search row. Pass a button as `CommandDialog`'s `trigger` to connect opening, expanded state, and focus restoration to the same control, including when the dialog opens through a keyboard shortcut.

## Accessibility

The search field is a combobox that controls a listbox. Arrow keys, Home and End move the selection, Enter runs it, and Escape leaves a sub-page before it closes the launcher. Focus returns to the trigger on close.

Inline and popover `Command` compositions use the semantic surface, text, border, and selected-item colors. A surrounding Popover or Dialog owns its outer frame. `CommandDialog` and `Commander` retain the dedicated launcher palette.

components.name: DataTable
components.title: Core/DataTable
components.description: DataTable is a TanStack table with a compact data anatomy: shared headers that preserve label casing, hairline rows, synced column and row hover, a tinted wash for selected rows, and declarative column alignment, width and pinning. It adds search with a live count, single or multi-column sorting, selection with bulk actions, expandable rows, row action menus, pinned rows, grouped bands, a totals footer, sticky headers, automatic virtualization, pagination or load-more, CSV export, and loading, refreshing, empty and error states. Sorting, selection, expansion and pinning work controlled or uncontrolled.
decisionRules: Use DataTable for actual tabular comparison, not card grids or definition lists.
Keep filtering predicates in the host: pass FilterBar state through your own match function and give DataTable the visible rows.
Right-align numeric columns with align: right so figures line up in tabular numerals.
Pin at most the identifying column and one summary column; pinning releases on narrow screens so every column stays reachable.
Pin rows for references readers compare against, such as a goal or the current item; pinned bands stop sticking when they would crowd out the scrolling rows.
Give long lists a maxHeight (or let virtualize="auto" pick one) so the header and pinned rows stay in view; use stickyHeader="page" when the table should scroll with the page under app chrome.
Prefer pagination or load-more for remote collections; client virtualization suits a few thousand rows that are already loaded.

For workspaces people shape themselves, compose the DataGrid view controls: DataGridViewOptions, DataGridLayouts with useDataGridLayouts, DataGridCardView, DataGridStatusTabs, header column stats and DataGridColumnPicker (see the CRM workspace and Shipment exceptions examples).

components.readme:
# DataTable

A table for client collections up to a few thousand rows: search with a live count, single or multi-column sorting,
row selection, column visibility, paging or load-more, grouped and expandable rows, row actions, pinned rows and
columns, sticky headers, automatic virtualization, CSV export, a totals footer, and loading, refreshing, empty and error
states. The convenience table and DataGrid share TanStack Table v9 and the same feature registry. It composes the DS Button, Input, Checkbox, DropdownMenu, Skeleton, Loader and
EmptyState.

```jsx
import DataTable from '@gaudi/design-system/core/DataTable';

<DataTable
  caption='Article library'
  columns={[{ key: 'title', header: 'Article' }, { key: 'words', header: 'Words', align: 'right' }]}
  rows={articles}
  searchable
  sortable
  selectable
  pagination
  pageSize={10}
  density='compact'
/>
```

- Columns take `key`, `header`, `render`, `accessor`, `align`, `width`, `sticky` (`start` or `end`; `left` and `right` are aliases that mirror in RTL), `footer`,
  `exportValue(value, row)` and `export: false`, and `sortable`, `searchable` or `hideable` set to `false` to opt out.
- Text follows the surrounding reading direction by default. Set `align` to `left`, `center`, or `right` for an explicit physical alignment.
- State is controlled or uncontrolled: `sorting` / `defaultSorting` / `onSortingChange`, `selection` /
  `defaultSelection` / `onSelectionChange`, `expanded` / `defaultExpanded` / `onExpandedChange` (row IDs) and
  `rowPinning` / `defaultRowPinning` / `onRowPinningChange` (`{ top, bottom }`). A controlled host can refuse a change by
  not applying it, or replace it with something else.
- `multiSort` adds Shift-click sorting by more than one column; headers show their sort order.
- `pinnableRows` adds Pin to top, Pin to bottom and Unpin to each row menu. Pinned rows stay in view through sorting,
  search and pages, and stick under the header while the region scrolls; they stop sticking when the bands would
  crowd out the scrolling rows.
- `getRowActions` opens one menu from the overflow button, a right-click, Shift+F10 or the Menu key, and returns focus to
  where it was. `canActivateRow(row)` leaves some rows inert while `onRowClick` activates the rest.
- `maxHeight` scrolls rows inside the region with a sticky header. `stickyHeader='page'` keeps the header under page
  chrome (`stickyOffset`) while the page scrolls; in that mode the table fits its container, and a table too wide
  for it falls back to scrolling sideways in place.
- `virtualize='auto'` (the default) renders only the rows in view above `virtualThreshold` rows (100) and gives the
  region a 32rem height unless `maxHeight` is set. Grouped and paged tables are not virtualized.
- `onLoadMore`, `hasMore` and `loadingMore` add a Load more action; `loadMoreOnScroll` asks for the next batch as the last
  row comes into view.
- `exportable` (or `{ filename, scope, label, delimiter, onExport }`) adds Export CSV: visible columns, the current
  search and sort, and only the selected rows when there is a selection. Formula-like text is neutralised so spreadsheets
  show it as text.
- Filtering predicates, remote fetching and persistence stay in the host; pair it with `FilterBar` for facets.

## Shared table appearance

The primitive Table, DataTable, DataGrid and article Table use the same header typography and semantic colours. Labels preserve supplied casing. Density changes padding and header height, not typography or colour.

`DataTable` uses `headerVariant='muted'` by default; choose `'plain'` for a surface-coloured header. DataGrid uses the same default through `tableLayout.headerBackground=true`; setting it to `false` selects the plain treatment. Its `dense` flag maps to the shared compact density. Both treatments keep an opaque background for sticky headers.

## DataGrid parts

Use the `DataGrid` parts (`DataGrid`, `DataGridContainer`, `DataGridTable`, `DataGridPagination`, …) for resizable,
draggable, virtualised, editable or server-driven grids.

- **Grouping and aggregation.** `dataGridFeatures` registers grouping and aggregation. Set `grouping` state (or turn on
  `tableLayout.columnsGroupable` for a "Group by this column" header action) and give columns an `aggregationFn`:
  `sum`, `count`, `mean`, `min`, `max`, `extent`, `median`, `unique`, `uniqueCount`, `first`, `last`, or a custom
  `constructAggregationFn({ aggregate })`. Group bands collapse, count their records and render aggregates with the
  column's `aggregatedCell` (or a formatted value). `column.getAggregationValue()` returns grand totals for a footer.
- **Narrow containers.** DataTable and DataGrid release fixed column positioning when pinned columns would use at least three quarters of the scroll viewport. The host’s pinning state and column order stay intact; pinning resumes when the container grows.
- **Editing.** With `tableLayout.cellSelection`, a column edits through `meta.cellEdit`:
  - `control`: `text`, `textarea`, `number`, `select`, `combobox`, `date`, `checkbox` or `switch`. Enter, F2, typing or a
    double-click opens the editor over the cell (the Gaudi Select, Combobox, Calendar); checkbox and switch cells flip with
    Enter, Space or a click and render with `DataGridCellToggle`. `options` (`[{ value, label }]`, strings or
    `(row) => options`) feed select and combobox; `step`, `min` and `max` the number editor (ArrowUp/Down steps, Shift
    by ten); dates are stored as `yyyy-MM-dd` and shown with `displayFormat` (`MMM d, yyyy`).
  - Each built-in control brings a `parse(raw, row)` and `format(value, row)` pair, so paste, fill and clipboard copy
    read the same values the editors write. A column's own `parse`, `format`, `clearValue` or `setValue(row, value)`
    wins.
  - `required`, `min`, `max` and `validate(value, row)` (a message string, `false`, or nothing when valid) mark a cell
    invalid. The grid shows the error inline through `getCellError(row, columnId)`: the cell sets `aria-invalid`,
    points `aria-describedby` at its message, tints red and shows a tooltip while hovered or focused.
- **Undo and redo.** `useDataGridHistory({ onApply, limit })` records each `onCellsChange` batch (an edit, paste, fill,
  clear or cut) as one step and replays its inverse through `invertDataGridCellsChange`; `record({ undo, redo, source })`
  adds custom steps. Pass `gridProps` (`onCellsChange`, `onUndo`, `onRedo`) to `DataGrid` for Mod+Z, Shift+Mod+Z and
  Ctrl+Y, and `DataGridHistoryControls history={…}` adds toolbar buttons with their shortcuts.
- **Pending changes.** `useDataGridEditing({ data, columns, getRowId, onSave, onReject })` keeps a working copy of
  `data`: give the table `editing.rows` and spread `editing.gridProps` onto `DataGrid` for dirty, new and invalid
  status, inline errors and history. `insertRow`, `duplicateRow(rowId, copy)` and `removeRows(ids)` are undoable;
  `pending`, `pendingCount`, `errors` and `firstError` describe the state, `save()` calls `onSave({ rows, updated,
  added, removed })` (return `false` or throw to keep the changes) and `discard()` reverts everything. Text that cannot
  be parsed stays visible as a cell error instead of a toast. `DataGridSaveBar editing={…} apiRef={…}` shows the count,
  the cells that need attention (Show focuses the first) and Discard and Save; Save is blocked while errors exist. It
  floats at the bottom like `DataGridSelectionBar`; to show both, wrap them in one sticky row and pass
  `className='static mx-0'` to each.
- **Per-row edit mode.** `useDataGridRowEditing({ columns, onSave, onCancel })` turns one row at a time into a draft:
  spread its `gridProps` onto `DataGrid` and render `DataGridRowEditActions row={row} label={name}` in an actions column.
  Editable cells of the draft render `DataGridCellInlineEditor`; Enter saves, Escape cancels, other rows stay
  read-only (spreadsheet edits pause too), and messages appear once a field is touched or after a save attempt.
  `start(row, { isNew: true })` opens a new row; `onCancel({ rowId, isNew })` lets the host remove it again.
- **Labels.** The editing parts read `undo`, `redo`, `unsavedChanges(count)`, `invalidCells(count)`, `showInvalidCell`,
  `saveBlocked`, `save`, `saving`, `discard`, `editRow(name)`, `saveRow` and `cancelRowEdit` from `i18n.labels`.
- **Lazy children.** `useDataGridLazyRows({ data, expanded, getRowHasChildren, loadChildren, onChildrenLoad })`
  loads a parent's children the first time it opens. Spread its `tableOptions` into `useTable` and pass the hook to
  `<DataGrid lazyRows={lazy}>`: the table shows a skeleton row under a pending parent and an error row with Retry when
  the promise rejects. Results are cached (`invalidate(id)` drops one); `onChildrenLoad` merges them into host data,
  which always wins over the cache. Mark the tree column with `meta.treeColumn` so status rows line up with it.
- **Tree drag and drop.** `DataGridTableTreeDnd` is a body whose rows drop before, after or into another row
  (`canDropInside(row)`, default: rows that can expand), drawn with the Tree's drop line. A row never drops into
  itself or its descendants, a closed folder opens after a short hover, and reordering pauses while the grid is sorted.
  `DataGridTableTreeDndHandle` is the grip; Enter or Space on it starts a keyboard move (arrow keys choose the place,
  Enter drops, Escape cancels), announced through a status region.
- **Row moves.** Drag and drop, the keyboard and `DataGridTableRowMoveItems` (Move up, Move down, Move to top, Move to
  bottom for a row menu) all report through `<DataGrid onRowMove>` with `{ id, parentId, index, targetId, position }`.
  `moveDataGridRow(data, move, { childrenKey })` applies a move to nested or flat data. Alt+Arrow and Alt+Home/End on
  either drag handle move the focused row among its siblings. `useDataGridRowOrder(rows)` keeps a flat manual order with
  `moveRow`, `handleDragEnd`, `reset` and `isReordered`. Pass an `emptyMessage` node for the DnD body's empty state.
- **Tree selection.** `DataGridTableTreeRowSelect` and `DataGridTableTreeRowSelectAll` cascade: checking a parent
  checks every descendant, a parent reads checked when all of its children are and mixed when some are, and children
  that load under a checked parent arrive checked. `DataGridSelectionBar` counts every selected row at any depth.
- **Rollups.** Give a column `meta.rollup: true` and an `aggregationFn`: tree parents show the aggregate of their
  deepest loaded descendants (an unloaded parent keeps its own value), formatted by `meta.rollupCell({ value, row,
  scope })`. `DataGridTableTreeTotals` adds a grand-total footer row; `getDataGridRollupValue` and
  `getDataGridTreeTotal` return the numbers. `DataGridTreeExpand` offers Expand all, Collapse all and Expand to level N
  (pass `levels` when deeper levels have not loaded yet).
- **Banded sections.** `DataGridTableSections` renders a grouped grid as one section per group: a tinted band with the
  title, a count, a collapse toggle, `selectable` select-all for the section and an optional `onSectionAdd` action,
  followed by its own column headers. Sort, selection and columns stay shared, sections scroll sideways together, and
  `sections={[{ value, label, tone, description }]}` orders the bands and keeps empty ones visible. Tones are
  `neutral`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `attention` and `discovery`. Hide the grouped column
  (`columnVisibility`) and set `groupedColumnMode: false`; `DataGridTableSectionSelectAll` and `useDataGridSection()`
  work inside a section's headers and cells.
- **Export.** `DataGridExport` saves the grid's visible columns, filters, sort and selection as CSV; `meta.exportValue`
  formats a cell and `meta.export: false` skips control columns. `toCsv`, `tableToCsv` and `downloadCsv` are exported for
  custom flows.

### View controls

```jsx
import {
  DataGrid, DataGridCardView, DataGridColumnPicker, DataGridLayouts, DataGridStatusTabs, DataGridTable,
  DataGridViewOptions, DataGridViewToggle, createDataGridColumnRegistry, dataGridEqualsFilter, useDataGridLayouts
} from '@gaudi/design-system/core/DataTable';

const layouts = useDataGridLayouts({ table, density, onDensityChange: setDensity, storageKey: 'deals-layouts' });

<DataGrid table={table} recordCount={rows.length} tableLayout={{ dense: density === 'compact', headerSticky, rowsPinnable: true }}>
  <DataGridColumnPicker registry={registry} value={addedIds} onAdd={(id) => setAddedIds((ids) => [...ids, id])} />
  <DataGridLayouts layouts={layouts} />
  <DataGridViewOptions density={density} onDensityChange={setDensity} headerSticky={headerSticky}
    onHeaderStickyChange={setHeaderSticky} onReset={layouts.resetLayout} />
  <DataGridViewToggle value={view} onValueChange={setView} />
  <DataGridStatusTabs columnId='stage' options={stages}>
    {view === 'table' ? <DataGridTable /> : <DataGridCardView aria-label='Deals' />}
  </DataGridStatusTabs>
</DataGrid>
```

- **View settings.** `DataGridViewOptions` is one popover for density (`density` / `onDensityChange`, `comfortable` or
  `compact`), the sticky header (`headerSticky` / `onHeaderStickyChange`), extra `toggles` (`{ id, label, checked,
  onCheckedChange, description? }`) and the column list: a checkbox per hideable column plus Move up and Move down
  (or Alt+Arrow keys), with pinned columns held in place. `onReset` adds Reset layout. Pass `children` to compose
  `DataGridViewOptionsSection`, `DataGridViewOptionsDensity`, `DataGridViewOptionsSwitch` and
  `DataGridViewOptionsColumns` yourself. `getDataGridColumnOrder(table)` and `moveDataGridColumn(table, id, delta)` are
  the ordering helpers.
- **Table or cards.** `DataGridCardView` renders the same row model as the table (sorting, filters, pagination, pinned
  rows first) as a responsive card grid (`minCardWidth`, default `16rem`), and selection is shared. Columns choose
  their card slot with `meta.card`: `title`, `subtitle`, `media`, `badge`, `actions`, `field` or `false`
  (`meta.cardLabel` renames a field). `renderCard({ row, slots, table, isSelected })` replaces the default card.
  `DataGridViewToggle` switches `'table'` and `'cards'`.
- **Saved layouts.** `useDataGridLayouts({ table, density?, onDensityChange?, defaultLayout?, layouts?,
  defaultLayouts?, onLayoutsChange?, storageKey? })` snapshots column order, sizing, visibility and pinning (and
  density when `onDensityChange` is given) into named layouts `{ id, name, layout }`. Saved layouts are controlled or
  uncontrolled; `storageKey` also keeps them and the current layout in localStorage, restored after hydration. It
  returns `layouts`, `activeLayout`, `isDefault`, `saveLayout(name)`, `applyLayout(id)`, `deleteLayout(id)` and
  `resetLayout()` (back to `defaultLayout`, else the table's initial state). `DataGridLayouts` is the menu for it;
  `getDataGridLayout`, `applyDataGridLayout` and `isSameDataGridLayout` work on any table.
- **Column stats.** A header with `stats` (or a column with `meta.stats`) adds a labelled Column stats group to its menu:
  count, distinct and empty values, and min, max, average and sum for numbers (min and max for dates), over the
  filtered rows. Each stat is a menu item that copies its value; `DataGridColumnStats` renders the same figures as a
  definition list outside menus. Pass an array
  (`['min', 'max', 'avg']`) to pick stats and `meta.statsFormat(value, id)` to format them. `getDataGridColumnStats`
  reads the column's own `getAggregationValue` first, so a server-backed aggregation supplies its values.
- **Add columns.** `createDataGridColumnRegistry(entries)` groups addable columns (`{ id, label, icon?, keywords?,
  children?, column }`) for `DataGridColumnPicker`, a searchable Cascader that disables columns already shown. The host
  keeps the added ids and builds `columns` with `registry.getColumns(ids)`.
- **Heat cells.** `DataGridHeatmapCell` colours a number with the HeatmapChart scale and chart tokens (`heatmap`, or
  `diverging` around `midpoint`), against its column's visible range or a given `domain`;
  `getDataGridHeatmapColor` returns the fill and ink for custom cells. For trend cells, lazy-load
  `Sparkline` from `@gaudi/design-system/charts` so the chart runtime stays out of the table's bundle.
- **Status tabs.** `DataGridStatusTabs` puts an All tab and one tab per status, each with a live count, above the grid,
  which renders as the tab panel. With `columnId` a tab filters that column (give it `filterFn: dataGridEqualsFilter`)
  and counts come from its facets, which ignore the column's own filter; otherwise pass `value`, `onValueChange` and
  `counts`.
- **Virtualized selection.** Under `DataGridTableVirtual` with `onFetchMore` and `manualPagination`, Select all takes
  every loaded row and reads as partial when the next page arrives. For "every matching record", keep a flag in the
  host and derive the selection from it, as the Shipment exceptions example does; bulk actions then target the query,
  not only loaded rows.

Every string is in `DATA_GRID_VIEW_LABELS` and translates through the grid's `i18n.labels`. The view popovers are
labelled dialogs that return focus to their trigger; column moves keep focus on the moved row and are announced, and
layout, column and export changes are announced through status regions.

## Implementation ownership

`dataGridFeatures.js` owns engine registration for both APIs. Clipboard serialization and selection models stay separate from DOM fill sessions and editor overlays. Table headers, rows, controls, resizing and framing live in `components/`; public exports remain in `index.js`. Constants and helpers live in server-safe modules (`dataGridModel.js`, `dataGridStructureModel.js`, `dataGridViewModel.js`, `dataGridColumnStats.js`, `dataGridCellContent.js` and the selection, clipboard and table models) and `index.js` re-exports them from there, never through a `'use client'` file, so server components receive values rather than client references. The convenience API retains `sortingFn` column callbacks and adapts them to the shared engine.

components.readme:
# Dialog

Modal, confirmation and bare full-screen surfaces share the `Dialog` component. Use a modal to edit or inspect something without leaving the page, a confirmation for decisions that need an explicit answer, and `bare` for lightboxes, players and launchers that bring their own layout. Use `Sheet` for side panels.

[Open the Docs page](http://localhost:6007/?path=/docs/core-dialog--docs) for every example with copyable source.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Dialog } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Dialog
  trigger={<Button>Edit title</Button>}
  title='Edit article'
  description='Update the title readers see.'
>
  <Field>
    <FieldLabel>Title</FieldLabel>
    <Input defaultValue='A useful idea' />
  </Field>
</Dialog>
```

Use the confirmation variant for actions that require an explicit decision:

```jsx
<Dialog
  variant='confirmation'
  trigger={<Button>Archive draft</Button>}
  title='Archive this draft?'
  description='You can restore it from the archive.'
  confirmLabel='Archive draft'
  onConfirm={archiveDraft}
/>
```

## API

| Prop / export                       | Type                         | Contract                                                        |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`                           | React element                | Optional button that opens the dialog; it must forward its ref. |
| `title / description`               | ReactNode                    | Accessible title and optional supporting description.           |
| `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange` | boolean / boolean / function | Controlled or uncontrolled visibility.                          |
| `variant`                           | modal, confirmation or bare | Modal is the default; confirmation uses explicit action/cancel behavior; bare drops the chrome. |
| `label / container / initialFocusRef / restoreFocusRef` | string / Element / Ref / Ref | Bare only: accessible name without a visible title, portal container, first focus, and fallback focus target. |
| `children / footer`                 | ReactNode                    | Modal: scrollable body and persistent action region. Bare: the whole surface. |
| `contentProps`                      | object                       | Modal and bare: Radix content callbacks, including initial-focus customization. |
| `onConfirm`                         | () => void or Promise<void>  | Confirmation only: success closes; rejection displays recovery feedback. |
| `confirmLabel / cancelLabel / pendingLabel` | string               | Confirmation only: localized action copy.                       |
| `errorMessage / tone`               | string / semantic tone       | Confirmation only: recovery message and confirm-button intent.  |

## Composition and migration

`Dialog` reuses its exported title and description parts, so prop-driven and compound dialogs share typography and accessible naming. It is built on the same Radix parts it exports. Use `DialogRoot`, `DialogContent` and the other `Dialog*` parts for custom modals. Use `DialogConfirmationRoot`, `DialogConfirmationContent`, `DialogConfirmationAction`, `DialogConfirmationCancel` and their related parts for custom confirmations. These exports are available from the package root and `@gaudi/design-system/core/Dialog`.

Replace `<AlertDialog ... />` with `<Dialog variant='confirmation' ... />`. The previous `AlertDialog` and `AlertDialog*` aliases have been removed. Use `DialogConfirmationRoot` and its parts for compound confirmations. Confirmation dialogs initially focus Cancel, prevent repeated submissions, block dismissal while pending, and restore focus when closed.

## Ownership and verification

The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

# DropdownMenu

Action menus with item, checkbox, label and separator primitives. Supply a single button trigger; onSelect belongs to each action. Disabled items stay discoverable and inactive.

components.readme:
# Embed

The shared preview vocabulary for messages and content. `Embed` is a thin switch that hands each piece of content to the owner that already renders it, so a chat reply, an article and a dashboard show links, code and pages the same way.

| Type | Rendered by |
| --- | --- |
| `link` | `LinkPreview` (`variant` card, compact or inline) |
| `code` | `CodeBlock` |
| `web` | `WebPreview` (generated HTML through `html`, or a live `url` with `type='web'`) |
| `image` | A LinkPreview image card, or `components.image` (for example a lightbox image) |
| `video` | A LinkPreview thumbnail card, or `components.video` (for example the MDX Video) |

`type='auto'` (default) picks from the content: `code` means code, `html` means a page, an image or video address means media, anything else is a link. `resolveEmbedType(content)` is the same rule as a pure function.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Embed } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Embed url='https://github.com/g-udi/design-system' />
<Embed code={source} language='html' filename='index.html' />
<Embed url='https://preview.example.dev/' html={generatedHtml} title='Generated page' />
<Embed src='/images/diagram.png' alt='Architecture diagram' components={{ image: ImageWithLightbox }} />
```

Core does not import the MDX `Image` or `Video` (they stay in the `./mdx` entry), which is why media renderers are passed in rather than built in.

## Accessibility

Embed adds only a wrapper (`span` for inline links); accessibility comes from the owner it renders. Give images `alt` text and generated pages a `title`.

# EmptyState

An empty state explains why a list, search or panel has nothing to show and offers the next step: create the first item, clear filters, or go elsewhere.

```jsx
import { Button, EmptyState, Icon } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<EmptyState
  title='Make room for your first idea'
  description='Start a draft and build it into something worth sharing.'
  icon={<Icon name='FileText' decorative size='sm' />}
  actions={<Button onClick={createDraft}>Write an article</Button>}
/>
```

- `icon` sits in a small muted tile and is hidden from assistive tech.
- `actions` takes one or two buttons; lead with the action that fixes the situation.
- `compact` tightens the padding for cards and side panels.
- It is plain content, not a live region. Pass `role='status'` when it appears in response to a user action.
- For custom layouts (illustrations, search fields, inline links), compose `Empty`, `EmptyHeader`, `EmptyMedia`, `EmptyTitle`, `EmptyDescription` and `EmptyContent`.

components.readme:
# EventCalendar

A scheduling calendar with month, week, day, agenda and resource views, drag to move and resize, slot selection, recurring events and time zones. Use it for bookings and team schedules; use a Calendar to pick dates and a Gantt to plan work over weeks or months.

```jsx
import { EventCalendar, EventCalendarNav, EventCalendarContent } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<EventCalendar defaultEvents={events} defaultView='week' onEventsChange={save} className='h-[600px]'>
  <EventCalendarNav />
  <EventCalendarContent />
</EventCalendar>
```

- Events are `{ id, title, start, end, allDay?, color?, recurrence?, resourceId? }`. `EVENT_CALENDAR_COLORS` lists the offered colours.
- `defaultView` / `view` pick the view; `interactions` turns drag, resize and slot selection on or off; `apiRef` adds, updates and removes events from outside.
- `renderEvent` and `renderEventTooltip` customise chips. `timeZone`, `weekStartsOn`, `locale` and `i18n` localise every view.
- Week and resource columns keep a readable minimum width and scroll horizontally inside the calendar. `scrollMode='page'` lets the schedule grow vertically with the page; the default `contained` mode scrolls within the supplied height. `scrollbars='native'` selects browser scrollbars for a contained schedule.
- With the default automatic event limit, narrow month cells show an event count that opens the existing detail popover. Wider cells show event chips directly; an explicit `maxEventsPerCell` remains authoritative.
- `recurrence` repeats an event daily, weekly, monthly or yearly (`FREQ`, `INTERVAL`, `COUNT`, `UNTIL`, `BYDAY`, `BYMONTHDAY`, `BYMONTH`, `WKST`), with excluded and extra dates. `parseRRuleString` and `formatRRuleString` convert RRULE text. Gantt uses the same engine.

## Accessibility

Navigation buttons are labelled, and the month view is a grid with column and row headers. Every visible string, including button labels and date formats, comes from `i18n`.

components.readme:
# Field

Wraps a form control with its label, help text and error, and connects them for assistive technology. Use it around every Input, Textarea or `FieldInput`.

## Usage

```jsx
import { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldLabel } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <EmailInput name='email' />
  <FieldDescription>Used for article updates only.</FieldDescription>
  {error ? <FieldError>{error}</FieldError> : null}
</Field>;
```

A `FieldError` marks the control invalid and adds itself to its description. For fieldsets, horizontal rows and choice cards, use the layout parts: `FieldSet`, `FieldLegend`, `FieldGroup`, `FieldContent`, `FieldTitle`, `FieldSeparator` and `Label`.

## Accessibility

The label targets the control, and the description and error are read with it through `aria-describedby`. Errors are announced as alerts.

`FieldInput` inherits `caretMode` from `InputConfigProvider` and supports a local `native` or `smooth` override. See [Input caret mode](../Input/README.md#smooth-caret-mode) for behavior and native fallbacks.

components.readme:
# FileUpload

Controlled file selection with type, size and count limits. files and onFilesChange own the selection. getFileState supplies progress/error/success, and onRetry/onCancel delegate transport actions.

## Usage

```jsx
const [files, setFiles] = useState([]);
<FileUpload
  files={files}
  onFilesChange={setFiles}
  multiple
  accept='.pdf,.md'
  maxFiles={3}
  maxSize={5000000}
/>;
```

## API

| Prop / export           | Type                       | Contract                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `files / onFilesChange` | File[] / function          | Controlled selected files. List existing server attachments with Attachment.     |
| `accept / multiple`     | string / boolean           | Native accept syntax and single/multiple selection.                              |
| `maxSize / maxFiles`    | number                     | Bytes and count. Negative/NaN limits allow zero; omission removes a limit.       |
| `onReject`              | function([{file, reason}]) | Reports type, size or count rejection; never clears a valid existing selection.  |
| `getFileState`          | function(file)             | Supplies status, measured progress and error text.                               |
| `onRetry / onCancel`    | function(file)             | Host-owned transport actions; the component starts no requests.                  |
| `labels`                | object                     | Overrides chooser, rejection, progress, success and action copy.                 |
| `useFileUpload`         | hook                       | Headless state (previews, drag, errors) for custom upload surfaces; same `accept` rules. |
| `formatBytes`           | function(bytes, decimals)  | Formats a size such as `1.8MB`; FileUpload uses it for each row.                 |

## Ownership and verification

The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

components.readme:
# FilterBar

The toolbar above a collection: a search with a live result count, a Filters popover with one tab per facet and option
counts, and a removable "Field: Value" chip for every applied filter. It composes the DS Input, Button, Popover, Tabs
and Badge, and only presents state: the host owns matching and persistence.

```jsx
import FilterBar from '@gaudi/design-system/core/FilterBar';

<FilterBar
  query={query}
  onQueryChange={setQuery}
  count={{ shown: visible.length, total: rows.length }}
  facets={[{ id: 'status', label: 'Status', multiple: true, options: statuses, value: status, onChange: setStatus }]}
  onClearFilters={() => setQuery('')}
  actions={<Button size='sm'>New article</Button>}
/>
```

- A facet is `{ id, label, options: [{ value, label, count?, keywords?, disabled? }], value, onChange, multiple?, disabled? }`.
  Facets with more than six options get a search field.
- Long option labels truncate to the popover width and keep the full text as a tooltip.
- Below the small breakpoint the facet rail becomes a one-line facet select (`labels.facet` names it, falling back to
  `filterLabel`) above a scrollable option list, so phones keep the height for options.
- `filters` with `onRemoveFilter` shows host-applied filters as chips when you do not use facets; `onClearFilters` clears everything.
- `children` adds controls beside the search; `labels` translates every visible and accessible string.
- Phrases with a name are label functions, so translations control word order: `labels.removeFilter(value, field)` (default "Remove {value} filter"), `labels.findIn(facet)` (default "Find {facet}") and `labels.findPlaceholder(facet)`. The older string labels (`remove`, `find`) still work.
- `dir` sets the bar's reading direction (and its search field's); `inputProps` passes other attributes (name, autoComplete, id…) to the search input.
- Use the `Filters` and `FiltersAdvanced` parts for rule builders with operators, groups and drag and drop.

components.readme:
# FloatingMenu A compact, inverted pill of destinations that floats over the top of the page once the reader has scrolled away from the site header, with an optional Back to top button. `LayoutContainer` renders it with the SiteConfig `navigation.links`; use it directly for a custom shell or a scrollable panel. ```jsx import { FloatingMenu } from '@gaudi/design-system'; ``` By default the pill appears when the reader scrolls back up past `threshold` (50px) and hides on the way down; `revealOn='scroll'` keeps it visible whenever the threshold is passed. `links` falls back to SiteConfig `navigation.links`; the link matching the current path (or one with `active`) gets `aria-current="page"`. `actions` adds controls such as a call to action after the links, and `backToTop={false}` drops the Back to top button. Inside a scroll container, pass `targetRef` to observe it and `position='sticky'`, and render the menu as the container's first child: ```jsx const pageRef = useRef(null);
…
``` ## Accessibility The pill is a navigation landmark named by `label` (Quick navigation). It stays in the tab order while hidden, and focusing any of its controls reveals it, so keyboard users are never stranded. Transitions stop and Back to top jumps instantly when the reader prefers reduced motion. On narrow screens the Back to top label collapses to its icon and the links scroll inside the pill rather than widening the page.

components.readme:
# Flow

A node-and-edge canvas for automation workflows, pipeline runs, agent trees and driver maps. It is built on React Flow and themed with Gaudi tokens, so cards, handles, edges, the minimap and the controls follow the theme, the radius and the space scale. Use Gantt for work over time and Timeline for a linear history.

Flow is opt-in so apps that don't use it skip the canvas library: install the optional peer `pnpm add @xyflow/react`, import the stylesheet once, and import Flow from its subpath (it is not part of the root entry).

```jsx
import '@gaudi/design-system/flow.css';
import { Flow, layoutFlow } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Flow';

const edges = [{ id: 'draft-review', source: 'draft', target: 'review' }];
const nodes = layoutFlow([
  { id: 'draft', type: 'pill', data: { title: 'Draft ready', icon: 'FileText', target: false } },
  { id: 'review', type: 'step', data: { title: 'Editor review', status: 'running', meta: ['Due today'] } }
], edges);

<Flow label='Publishing pipeline' nodes={nodes} edges={edges} className='h-[32rem]' />
```

- `tile` nodes render `FlowTileNode`: a service or brand `icon` on a tile with a run badge under it, the `title` and a `meta` line (`metaTone: 'danger'` for an error). `shape: 'circle'` makes a satellite such as a connection, test or model. `task` nodes render `FlowTaskNode`: a one-line card with an inline `action` (for example Approve) and a warning ring while `waiting`.
- `step` nodes render `FlowNode`: `data` takes `title`, `description`, `icon` (registry name or element), `tone`, `status` / `statusLabel`, `badge`, `meta` (facts such as duration or cost), `owner`, `progress`, `content`, `footer`, `actions` (a menu), `toolbar` (shown while selected), `outputs` (named branch handles) and `ports` (dashed attachment handles). `pill` nodes are compact triggers, ends and attachments.
- `FLOW_STATUSES` maps `idle`, `queued`, `running`, `success`, `failed`, `waiting`, `blocked` and `skipped` to a Badge, an icon, a tinted ring and the minimap colour. `FlowStatus` renders the same badge outside the canvas.
- Edges default to `FlowEdge`: `data.label`, `tone`, `status` (`running` flows in the accent, `failed` turns danger, `waiting` warning, `success` success), `variant` (`solid`, `dashed` or `dotted`), `animated` (the dots or dashes travel toward the target; a solid line carries moving dots over it), `path` (`smoothstep`, `bezier`, `step`, `straight`), `emphasis` and `onInsert`, which adds a plus button on the connector when hovered or focused. Motion stops under reduced motion and the pattern stays. Satellite links read best as `variant: 'dotted'` without `animated` or an arrow.
- `layoutFlow(nodes, edges, { direction: 'TB' | 'LR' })` is a small layered layout for tidy trees and driver maps. Nodes marked `attachment: true` sit beside the step they link to instead of taking a rank. `topologicalOrder`, `createsCycle`, `hasEdge`, `descendants` and `unreachableNodes` cover replay order, relink validation and reachability. `useFlowHistory` gives undo and redo that treat one drag as one step.
- `FlowPanel`, `FlowControls` and `FlowMiniMap` place toolbars, zoom controls and the overview map on the canvas. `FlowControls variant='toolbar'` lays the controls in one row with a select / pan switch (`tool`, `onToolChange`, paired with `Flow tool`), the zoom level and an issues button (`issues`, `onIssues`); `onAutoLayout` adds an Auto layout button (nodes glide into place) and `showFitSelection` a Fit selection button. Every control has a label and a tooltip.
- `FlowInspector`, rendered inside `Flow`, is the side panel for a selected node. Open it from `Flow onNodeActivate`, which fires on a click and on Enter from a focused node, so keyboard users reach it too: a header with the node's icon, title and status, `tabs` (such as Settings and Wiring), a `callout` for its state, and Cancel / Save (disabled until `dirty`). It floats over the canvas and becomes a Sheet when the canvas is narrower than 768px; focus moves in when it opens and back to the node (`nodeId`) when it closes, and Escape closes it. Wrap the canvas and outside controls in `FlowProvider` to use `useReactFlow` beside it.
- Every other prop goes to React Flow, such as `onConnect`, `onBeforeDelete` (confirm deletes), `snapToGrid`, `nodeOrigin` and `onNodeContextMenu`.

Install the `@xyflow/react` peer dependency. Its structural CSS is imported by the Gaudi stylesheet, so no extra import is needed.

## Accessibility

The canvas is a labelled region described by a step count, followed by a visually hidden list of each step, its status and where it leads. Nodes and edges are focusable: Enter or Space selects, the arrow keys move a selected node with a live announcement, and Delete removes it. Zoom controls, node menus and connector buttons are labelled; connection handles are pointer targets, so the node name and the step list carry their meaning. Every string, including React Flow's keyboard instructions, comes from `labels`.

React Flow has no keyboard way to draw a connection between two handles, so offer a menu action or inspector field for linking, as the impact map example does. Dragging should never be the only way to change the graph.

components.readme:
# Gantt

A timeline of tasks against a resource tree, with day to year scales, progress, dependencies, baselines, milestones, drag to move and resize, and row reordering. Use it to plan work over weeks or months; use an EventCalendar for hour-level schedules.

```jsx
import { Gantt, GanttNav, GanttView } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Gantt defaultEvents={tasks} resources={teams} defaultScale='month' treePanel={{ width: 200 }} className='h-[580px]'>
  <GanttNav />
  <GanttView />
</Gantt>
```

- Tasks are `{ id, title, resourceId, start, end, progress?, dependencies?, baselineStart?, baselineEnd?, color? }`; a zero-length task renders as a milestone. `GANTT_COLORS` matches the EventCalendar colours.
- `resources` is a tree of `{ id, title, children? }`; `treePanel` configures the left panel, such as its `width`.
- `defaultScale` / `scale` zoom between `GANTT_SCALES`; `interactions` turns drag, resize and slot selection on or off; `apiRef` and `onEventsChange` connect edits to your data.
- Time-zone, lane and recurrence helpers are shared with EventCalendar, so both components read dates and RRULEs the same way.
- `columns` adds tree columns (owner, status, load) beside the row names, and `treePanel` sizes the resizable split; `renderEvent`, `renderEventMenu` and `renderResourceLabel` customise bars, their right-click menu and row labels.
- `canDropEvent` validates a drag or resize while it happens; add `enforceCanDrop` so a refused drop snaps back. `checkDependencies(update, events)` returns `{ ok, blockedBy, blocking }` for finish-to-start rules, and `getCriticalPath(events)` returns the task ids that drive the finish date.

```jsx
import { Gantt, GanttNav, GanttView, checkDependencies } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Gantt
  defaultEvents={tasks}
  resources={phases}
  apiRef={apiRef}
  canDropEvent={(update) => checkDependencies(update, apiRef.current.getEvents()).ok}
  enforceCanDrop
>
  <GanttNav />
  <GanttView />
</Gantt>
```

Examples cover a project planner with live dependency validation and an edit dialog, a day dispatch on an hour grid with a skills guardrail, an agent playbook with retry lanes and a critical path, and a capacity-aware resource planner with booking cards and full create, edit, copy and delete.

## Accessibility

Navigation and row controls are labelled buttons, and bars scrolled out of view get labelled jump buttons at the edge of the timeline. Every visible string comes from `i18n`. When a drop is refused, say why in a `role='status'` line, as the examples do, and keep a non-drag path: bars are buttons, so a click opens a dialog or sheet with the same edits.

## Implementation ownership

`GanttView` composes private row and overlay components. Owner-local hooks manage the time scale, packed row layout, synchronized viewports and row reordering; models and recurrence remain separate from rendering.

components.readme:
# Icon

Icons from the Gaudi registry at token sizes and semantic colours. Pass `label` when the icon carries meaning on its
own, or `decorative` when text beside it already does. `kind` with `href` renders a labelled social or email link.

```jsx
import { AnimatedIcon, Icon, IconStack, IconTile } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Icon name='Info' size='lg' color='primary' label='More information' />
<IconTile variant='soft' size='lg'><Icon name='Star' decorative /></IconTile>
<AnimatedIcon name='Bell' active={hovered} size='md' color='primary' />
```

- `IconTile` frames an icon as media in lists, cards and empty states (`outline`, `elevated`, `soft`, `solid`, `frame`;
  sizes `xs` to `xl`; `radius='full'` for circles). Retint it with text and background tokens.
- `IconStack` draws a layered stack of cards behind an icon for empty and onboarding states.
- `AnimatedIcon` moves only while the host sets `active`, and rests for reduced motion, offscreen placement and hidden documents.

components.accessibility: Thumbnails are named buttons. Enter or Space opens the viewer. Arrow keys move between images (respecting direction), Home and End select the first and last images, and Escape closes. Touch supports swiping and browser pinch zoom. notes: Provide useful alt text; captions add visible context. Offscreen slides are hidden from assistive technology. Navigation stops at either end and disappears for a single image.
