components.readme:
# ImageGallery

A masonry or grid collection whose images open in a shared viewer. Pass one item for a full-width, click-to-expand image; the same component handles both uses.

```jsx
import { ImageGallery } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ImageGallery';

<ImageGallery
  label='Coastal photographs'
  images={[
    {
      id: 'north-coast',
      src: '/images/north-coast.jpg',
      thumbnailSrc: '/images/north-coast-small.jpg',
      alt: 'Waves breaking against a rocky coastline',
      caption: 'The north coast',
      width: 1200,
      height: 800
    }
  ]}
/>
```

Use local, host-supplied assets. Gaudi's examples use local files and do not fetch third-party demo resources.

## API

| Prop | Default | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `images` | `[]` | Array of `{ id, src, alt, caption?, thumbnailSrc?, width?, height? }`. Supply unique, stable string IDs and meaningful alternative text. |
| `label` | `'Image gallery'` | Accessible name of the gallery region; distinguish multiple galleries on a page. |
| `layout` | `'masonry'` | `'masonry'` preserves thumbnail ratios; `'grid'` crops thumbnails to 4:3. |
| `columns` | `{ mobile: 1, tablet: 2, desktop: 3 }` | Positive integer column counts. Each omitted field keeps its default. One image always uses one full-width column. |
| `showCaptions` | `true` | Shows captions below thumbnails. The viewer always shows the active caption, alternative text, or `'Image preview'`. |
| `selectedId` | `undefined` | Controlled selection. A matching ID opens the viewer; `null` closes it. |
| `defaultSelectedId` | `null` | Initial selection when uncontrolled. |
| `onSelectedIdChange` | — | Receives the requested ID, or `null` when closing. |
| `disabled` | `false` | Disables thumbnail activation and hides the viewer while preserving selection. |
| `className`, `style` | — | Applied to the gallery region. Other DOM props also pass to this outer element. |

`src` supplies the full image. `thumbnailSrc`, when present, supplies only the preview. Provide both `width` and `height` to reserve the thumbnail's aspect ratio; a source with a different ratio is cropped to fit. Without dimensions, masonry uses the loaded image's natural ratio. The viewer contains the full image without cropping.

Columns respond to the **gallery container width**: `mobile` below 640px, `tablet` from 640px, and `desktop` from 1024px. Masonry reads down each column before moving to the next; grid reads across rows. Keyboard and viewer navigation follow the supplied `images` order.

## Controlled selection

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ImageGallery } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ImageGallery';

function Gallery({ images, disabled = false }) {
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(null);

  return (
    <ImageGallery
      images={images}
      selectedId={selectedId}
      onSelectedIdChange={setSelectedId}
      disabled={disabled}
    />
  );
}
```

Thumbnail activation, navigation buttons, keyboard navigation, swiping, and closing request selection changes. The controlled host must accept a request by updating `selectedId`; it can also refuse or replace it. An ID absent from `images` hides the viewer without clearing the stored selection. Disabling behaves the same way: re-enabling reopens the retained image if it still exists. Set `selectedId` to `null` when the host wants to clear it permanently.

## Interaction and recovery

- Thumbnails are named buttons. Enter or Space opens the viewer and focuses Close. Left/Right arrows navigate with the current text direction; Home/End select the first/last image. Navigation stops at either end, and previous/next controls are omitted for a single image.
- Escape, Close, or the backdrop requests dismissal. Dialog contains focus and restores the opener when it remains connected and enabled; otherwise, it falls back to the gallery region. Offscreen slides are hidden from assistive technology, and the active caption is announced politely.
- Carousel owns touch swiping. Browser pinch zoom remains available; there are no separate zoom controls. Reduced motion removes animated slide movement and the expansion hint's transition.
- Thumbnails and inactive full images use lazy loading; the selected full image loads eagerly. Failed sources show an accessible `Image unavailable` placeholder. Replace the effective preview source (`thumbnailSrc || src`) to recover a thumbnail, or `src` to recover a full image. An empty collection displays `No images to display.`

## Shared ownership

ImageGallery composes Gaudi's Dialog, Carousel, Button, and Icon, using the existing neutral themes, radius tokens (4px by default), and density scale. The masonry and expansion behavior was informed by Shadix UI.

The existing MDX `Image` and `ImageModal` APIs share this viewer through the MDX adapter. The Core entry exports only `ImageGallery`; use a one-item collection for a standalone expandable image. The shared lightbox is private.

components.readme:
# Input

A single-line text field for names, emails, URLs, numbers and dates. `prefix` and `suffix` add text or icons inside the border (they render as InputGroup addons); every native attribute and the ref reach the input itself. Wrap it in a Field for its label, help and error.

For buttons, menus or several addons inside the border, compose `InputGroup`, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupButton`, `InputGroupText` and `InputGroupInput` directly.

## Usage

```jsx
import { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Field';

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email address</FieldLabel>
  <EmailInput
    name='email'
    autoComplete='email'
    placeholder='you@example.com'
  />
  <FieldDescription>Used for your reading digest.</FieldDescription>
</Field>;
```

## Accessibility

Visible labels are connected through Field. Inputs retain native validation, autocomplete and form submission.

## Examples

The Playground uses EmailInput for its email field and NumberField for its monthly budget; both inherit the global Caret toolbar. Other type choices use Input. Its preview controls include a per-field caret override, adornments, invalid and disabled states. The catalogue adds native types, password strength, and every addon placement. The chat composer built on InputGroup is `ChatInput` in the Chat area.

The same `InputGroup` and native control remain mounted when `prefix` or `suffix` appears or disappears. Conditional clear buttons and validation adornments preserve typed values, focus, selection, and the input ref.

## EmailInput

`EmailInput` is the single-address email editor exported from this owner. It uses a text input with `inputMode='email'`, `autoComplete='email'`, no capitalization and no spellcheck. Its caret supports the same provider and field override as Input.

```jsx
import { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Field';

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email address</FieldLabel>
  <EmailInput name='email' required placeholder='you@example.com' />
  <FieldDescription>Enter one email address, without spaces.</FieldDescription>
</Field>
```

The browser validates the [HTML email-address grammar](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#email-state-(type=email)) through `pattern`. Invalid addresses block normal form submission and report `validity.patternMismatch`; empty required fields report `validity.valueMissing`. Optional empty fields are valid. This works from server-rendered HTML, without a validation effect or hidden input. `onInvalid`, `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`, `setCustomValidity()`, form reset, native validation styles and FormData continue to work.

`value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, refs, `name`, `form`, `required`, length constraints, disabled/read-only states, adornments and ARIA attributes follow Input. `autoComplete` can be overridden. An additional `pattern` further restricts valid email addresses; invalid author patterns are ignored without disabling email validation. Use `FieldError` and `onInvalid` for specific, localized feedback, as shown in the Email Address story.

This is a text editor with email validation, not a native `type='email'` input: it preserves typed whitespace (which is invalid), reports `patternMismatch` rather than `typeMismatch`, and accepts one address only. `type`, `inputMode` and `multiple` are fixed by the component. Internationalized domain names must be provided in ASCII/Punycode form; it does not convert them. Keep `Input type='email'` when native email sanitization or multiple-address entry is required.

For numeric values with smooth movement, compose [NumberField](../NumberField/README.md). Put `caretMode` on `NumberFieldInput` for a per-field override; the root manages numeric values, bounds, stepping and formatting.


## Smooth caret mode

Smooth movement is the default, including without a provider. Use `InputConfigProvider` around the application or a form to change that default. `caretMode='smooth'` adds a short glide while typing or moving within a line; `caretMode='native'` keeps the browser caret. The Storybook **Caret** toolbar switches the default across examples. Individual controls override the inherited value without remounting or changing their value.

```jsx
import { InputConfigProvider } from '@gaudi/design-system/context';
import Input from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';

<InputConfigProvider caretMode='smooth'>
  <Input aria-label='Project name' />
  <Input caretMode='native' aria-label='Reference code' />
</InputConfigProvider>
```

The setting reaches FieldInput, Input, EmailInput, Textarea, InputGroup controls, phone inputs, chat composers, autocomplete/combobox search fields, command search, Cascader, Questionnaire and NumberField text controls. Native text editor overlays in DataGrid inherit the setting. Set `caretMode` on the actual input part for a local override.

Editing, validation, form data, undo, autofill, selection and refs remain native. The decoration is hidden from assistive technology, stays inside the field, and uses the field's caret color and typography. Only a focused field is measured, with updates batched to animation frames; no motion dependency is required. Wrapped-line changes snap vertically.

Reduced motion, forced colors, touch selection, IME composition, selected text, read-only fields, password masking, bidirectional text and input types without browser selection APIs retain the native caret. Supported types are text, search, URL, telephone and textarea. These fallbacks preserve the browser's specialized editing UI.

Inspired by [Skiper UI's smooth caret input](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper106); Gaudi's implementation uses DOM text layout and its existing motion tokens.

components.readme:
# InputOtp

Separate boxes for a one-time code, such as a sign-in or verification code sent by email or text.

## Usage

```jsx
import { InputOTP, InputOTPGroup, InputOTPSeparator, InputOTPSlot } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<InputOTP maxLength={6} aria-label='Verification code' value={code} onChange={setCode}>
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
  </InputOTPGroup>
  <InputOTPSeparator />
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={4} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={5} />
  </InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>;
```

`pattern` limits which characters are accepted, and `onComplete` fires once every slot is filled.

## Accessibility

One real input sits behind the slots, so pasting, autofill and screen readers treat the code as a single field. Give it an `aria-label` or a visible label.

components.readme:
# Item

A flexible row for lists of people, settings, integrations, navigation links, activity and run logs. Compose media, a title and description, trailing actions, and an optional header or footer; group rows with `ItemGroup` and divide them with `ItemSeparator`.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Button, Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemTitle, RegistryIcon } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ItemGroup>
  <Item variant='outline'>
    <ItemMedia variant='icon'><RegistryIcon lucide='GithubIcon' aria-hidden='true' /></ItemMedia>
    <ItemContent>
      <ItemTitle>GitHub</ItemTitle>
      <ItemDescription>Sync pull requests and issues.</ItemDescription>
    </ItemContent>
    <ItemActions><Button href='/settings/integrations/github' size='sm' variant='outline'>Connect</Button></ItemActions>
  </Item>
</ItemGroup>
```

The parts are also available from `@gaudi/design-system/core/Item`.

## Parts

| Part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `Item` | `variant` (default, outline, muted), `size` (default, sm, xs), `as` for the element and `asChild` to render a link or button. |
| `ItemMedia` | `variant` default, icon or image. |
| `ItemContent`, `ItemTitle`, `ItemDescription` | Main text column; the description clamps to two lines. |
| `ItemActions` | Trailing badges, buttons or menus. |
| `ItemHeader`, `ItemFooter` | Full-width rows above and below the content. |
| `ItemGroup`, `ItemSeparator` | A `role='group'` list wrapper and a horizontal divider. |

## Accessibility

Use `asChild` with a link when the whole row navigates, and keep independent actions outside that link. Name icon-only actions after their row ("Remove Odile Marchetti"). Give a group of rows an accessible name with `aria-label` when the surrounding heading does not describe it.

## Log examples

The Item docs include a live run status, phases separated by labelled rules, changed files with badges, and log links with a reversible action. These compose Item, Separator, Badge, Loader, Link and Button without a separate marker wrapper.

# KanbanBoard A controlled board for editorial workflows. Supply columns, items, renderItem and onMove. Moves are explicit menu actions accessible by keyboard and touch; this version does not implement drag-and-drop. ## Usage ```jsx setItems( items.map((item) => (item.id === id ? { ...item, columnId } : item)) ) } /> ``` ## API | Prop / export | Type | Contract | | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | `columns` | {id, label, limit?}[] | Ordered workflow columns; `limit` shows a WIP count. | | `items` | {id, title, columnId, ...data}[] | Host-owned records and placement. | | `renderItem` | function(item) | Optional card body. | | `onMove` | function(id, columnId) | Receives a move request. Update items in the host. | | `disabled` | boolean | Disable move actions while host work is pending. | | `label / moveLabel / emptyLabel` | string | Accessible and empty-state copy. | ## Drag-and-drop composition `Kanban`, `KanbanBoardPrimitive`, `KanbanColumn`, `KanbanColumnContent`, `KanbanItem`, the two handles and `KanbanOverlay` compose a drag-and-drop board with keyboard sorting. For richer boards: | Part / prop | Contract | | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `KanbanBoardPrimitive layout='scroll'` | Fixed-width columns in their own focusable, horizontally scrolling region. Name it with `aria-label`. | | `KanbanColumn collapsed` + `KanbanColumnRail` | A collapsed column drawn as a vertical rail button that expands it; cards dropped on it still land in the column. | | `KanbanColumnCount count limit` | The column count, or `count/limit`; over the limit it turns to the warning tone and says so. | | `KanbanItem withHandle` | Moves the sortable role and focus to `KanbanItemHandle`, so a card can hold its own buttons. | ```jsx item.id}> {Object.entries(columns).map(([id, items]) => ( {hidden.includes(id) ? ( show(id)} /> ) : ( <>

{titles[id]}

{items.map(renderCard)} )} ))} ``` ## Ownership and verification The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

# Kbd

A keyboard key or shortcut hint, such as "Press ⌘ K to search".

```jsx
import { Kbd } from '@gaudi/design-system';

Press <Kbd keys='command,k' size='sm' /> to search
```

- `keys` takes comma-separated key names (`command`, `shift`, `enter`, `escape`, `up`…) or an array of them (`['command', 'k']`). Named keys show as symbols, and a combination is announced as one label ("Command plus K").
- `children` render one literal key with no extra label.
- `variant`: `raised` (default) for standalone hints, `outline` or `flat` inside dense UI. `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
- For custom content such as icons, compose `KbdRoot` and `KbdGroup`; inside a tooltip they pick up its colours.

components.readme:
# Link

A link moves the reader to another page, a section of this page, or another site. Use `Button` with `href` when the link should look like an action.

```jsx
import { Link } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Link href='/blog/publications' tone='accent'>publications</Link>
```

- `variant`: `inline` for links in prose (default), `muted` for secondary links such as "Edit this page", `nav` for navigation, and `bare` to inherit the parent colour.
- `tone` colours `inline` links by meaning: `accent`, `neutral` (default), `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `attention`, `discovery`. Older hue names (`blue`, `gray`, `red`…) still work.
- Internal paths use client navigation, external URLs open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and a missing `href` renders plain text.

components.readme:
# LinkPreview A link enriched with what the destination is. One pure normaliser, `normalizeLinkPreview`, turns the app's preview payload into a display model, and three variants present it: - `inline` (default): the link text, with a rich card on hover or focus. This is what the blog's MDX `Preview` renders. - `card`: a Card with the Open Graph image, `orientation` vertical or horizontal; the title links to the destination. - `compact`: a one-line row with the favicon, title, host and leading metadata. ## Usage ```jsx import { LinkPreview, SiteConfigProvider } from '@gaudi/design-system';

The source is in .

// The app owns the endpoint and any derived images; Gaudi loads nothing by default. {children} ``` ## What each link shows `normalizeLinkPreview(data, { url, title, resolveImage, locale })` returns `{ kind, status, unavailable, title, linkTitle, description, excerpt, image, favicon, icon, site, label, author, date, formattedDate, readingTime, duration, tags, stats, meta, videoId, embeddable }`. The payload `type` wins; otherwise the URL decides the kind: | Kind | Detected from | Rich information | | --- | --- | --- | | `internal` | `type: 'internal'` or an app path (`/blog/…`) | Category badge, post title, summary, date, reading time, tags. No image. | | `repository` | `github.com` | `owner/repo` title, image (payload or `resolveImage`), language, stars and forks when the endpoint supplies them. | | `video` | YouTube, youtu.be, Vimeo | Thumbnail with a play badge and duration chip, channel, views. | | `social` | x.com, twitter.com, bsky.app | Author handle (from the URL when missing), the post text, replies and likes. | | `wikipedia` | `wikipedia.org` | Article name and excerpt instead of an image. | | `package` | `npmjs.com` (synthesized, no fetch) | Package name, package icon, version. | | `docs` | MDN, `docs.*`, readthedocs, `/docs` paths | Cleaned title (site suffixes removed), description. | | `image` / `file` | Image or document extensions | The image itself / the file type badge (PDF, CSV…). | | `article` | Medium, Substack, dev.to, or any payload with an author or published time | Author, date, reading time. | | `website` | Everything else | Title, description, image, site name. | Titles drop noisy suffixes (` - MDN Web Docs`, ` - YouTube`, ` · GitHub`…) and cap at 60 characters. Failures with status 400, 404 or 410 are `unavailable` and render a red link named "(link may be unavailable)"; other failures and missing endpoints render an ordinary link. Gaudi derives no images of its own; see [Images](#images). ## Data `usePreviewData(url, title, { previewData, endpoint, timeout })` calls the endpoint (`endpoint` option, then `SiteConfigProvider preview.endpoint`) with an LRU + TTL cache, request deduplication and a stale-response guard. A string endpoint receives `?url=`; a function returns the full request URL. **There is no default endpoint**: with none configured nothing is fetched, and links render from `previewData` or as plain links. Stories and tests pass static `previewData`. ## Images A card shows the payload's `image`, or the link itself when it points at an image. Gaudi ships no thumbnail, Open Graph or screenshot service URLs. For anything else, pass `resolveImage` (prop, or `SiteConfigProvider preview.resolveImage`); it is called for links whose payload has no image with `{ kind, url, host, data, videoId, repository }` (`videoId` for YouTube links, `repository: { owner, repo }` for GitHub links) and returns an image URL or `null`. Instead of a function, `resolveImage` can be a template map: link kinds (`video`, `repository`, `website`, `article`…, plus `default`) to URL templates with `{url}` (encoded), `{rawUrl}`, `{host}`, `{videoId}`, `{owner}` and `{repo}`. A kind mapped to `null` shows no image, and a template whose placeholder has no value yields none. Templates are plain data, so a server component can pass them. Without a resolver those links show no image. ## Migrating from the built-in defaults (2026-10-02) Earlier versions called `/api/preview` without being asked, derived YouTube thumbnails and GitHub Open Graph cards from the URL, used a Microlink screenshot when the MDX `Preview` had no image, and gave npm links a favicon from npmjs.com. Those defaults are gone, along with the `MICROLINK_SCREENSHOT_API`, `YOUTUBE_THUMBNAIL_API`, `GITHUB_OPENGRAPH_API`, `NPM_FAVICON_URL` and `DEFAULT_PREVIEW_ENDPOINT` exports and the `screenshotFallback` option. An app that wants the old behaviour configures it once: ```jsx // Plain data, so it can be passed from the server LayoutContainer. const preview = { endpoint: '/api/preview', resolveImage: { video: 'https://img.youtube.com/vi/{videoId}/maxresdefault.jpg', repository: 'https://opengraph.githubassets.com/1/{owner}/{repo}', wikipedia: null, // Wikipedia shows its excerpt instead default: 'https://api.microlink.io/?url={url}&screenshot=true&meta=false&embed=screenshot.url' } }; // or ``` The old screenshot applied only to the MDX `Preview`; with this setting it applies to every LinkPreview without an image. To keep it MDX-only, pass `resolveImage` to the MDX `Preview` map entry instead of the provider. ## Parts `LinkPreviewBody`, `LinkPreviewCard`, `LinkPreviewCompact`, `LinkPreviewMedia`, `LinkPreviewMeta`, `LinkPreviewTags`, `LinkPreviewFavicon`, `LinkPreviewSkeleton` and `LinkPreviewFallback` take the normalised `preview` and can be composed into other surfaces (chat sources, link lists). ## Accessibility Every variant is a real link with a readable name, so the destination never depends on the card. The hover card opens on focus as well as hover and only adds detail. Stats are read with their unit ("1.3K stars"), and images inside cards are decorative except for image links.

With reduced motion, rotation, travel, scaling and bouncing stop; the whole indicator breathes slowly in place. For an already-labelled button or busy region, use aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate announcements.
notes: Use className="text-current" to inherit surrounding text, or a semantic tone such as text-text-muted. Explicit size utility classes can override the dimensions. Keep the bar at its natural 3:1 ratio.

Import Loader from the root, core, or core/Loader entry. Spinner, SpinnerRoot and core/Spinner have been renamed to Loader, LoaderRoot and core/Loader; update existing imports.
The Shadix UI loader reference informed the variant family. Geometry and motion are implemented locally using Gaudi colors, density and motion conventions.

components.readme:
# Loader

A named loading status with eleven CSS animation variants. `Loader` replaces `Spinner`, and the Storybook owner is `Core/Loader`.

```jsx
import { Loader } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Loader';

<Loader variant='three-dots' size='md' label='Loading articles' />
```

- `variant`: `arc` (default), `dual-arc`, `bar`, `beat`, `bounce`, `circle-dots`, `clip`, `puff`, `three-dots`, `triangle`, or `two-dots`. These indicate an unknown wait; use `Progress` for measured completion.
- `size`: `xs` 12px, `sm` 16px, `md` 20px (default), or `lg` 32px. The bar is three times as wide as it is tall. Other variants are square. Intrinsic dimensions stay fixed across density presets.
- `label`: accessible status label, default `Loading`. Describe the active operation and provide visible status text where useful.
- `className`: use `text-current` to inherit surrounding color or a semantic tone such as `text-text-muted`. Explicit size utilities can override dimensions; preserve the bar's 3:1 ratio.
- SVG attributes and refs pass through. Set `aria-hidden='true'` when a button or containing region already announces the same state.

`LoaderRoot` is the composition primitive: the same variants, `sm` default, current text color, and `aria-label` instead of `label`. `loaderVariants` exports the supported names. All three are available from the root, `core`, and `core/Loader` entries; the leaf also has a default `Loader` export.

Reduced motion stops rotation, travel, scaling, and hopping. The indicator uses Gaudi's slow opacity breath while keeping its status label. The SVG/CSS implementation has no timers, and server rendering is deterministic. Unmount it when work finishes; the host owns loading state, cancellation, errors, and recovery.

Existing button, input, inline-status, overlay, and empty-state examples remain under Loader. Update `Spinner`, `SpinnerRoot`, and `core/Spinner` imports to `Loader`, `LoaderRoot`, and `core/Loader`. The Shadix UI reference informed the variant family; no remote animation code or assets are loaded.

components.name: Map
components.title: Core/Map
components.description: An interactive geographic map with selectable markers, route lines, and camera controls. Powered by MapLibre; applications supply their own style, geography, and prepared data.

props.name: mapStyle
props.description: A stable style object or an application-configured style URL. Gaudi has no built-in map service, access token, geocoding, or routing endpoint. Memoize object styles. Changing the style preserves the camera.

props.name: initialViewState
props.description: Initial camera. Later changes use ref.flyTo, ref.fitBounds, or ref.reset. Coordinates always use longitude before latitude.

props.name: markers
props.type: Array<{ id, coordinates, label, tone?, icon?, badge? }>
props.description: Stable unique IDs, [longitude, latitude] coordinates, and an accessible label. tone uses Button tones, icon is a React slot, and badge is optional visible metadata; include its meaning in label.

props.name: selectedMarkerId
props.description: Controlled selection. Pointer and keyboard activation request a selection; the host chooses whether to accept it. Selection does not move the camera.

props.name: onMarkerClick
props.description: Controlled selection. Pointer and keyboard activation request a selection; the host chooses whether to accept it. Selection does not move the camera.

components.accessibility: The named region contains a focusable map canvas: arrows pan, plus/minus zoom. Marker buttons and controls work with Enter/Space and show focus. Selected markers expose aria-pressed. Browser touch gestures and reduced motion are supported. Geographic canvas content itself is not a screen-reader equivalent: provide a linked list or textual route summary, as the tracking example does.
notes: Use an app-owned basemap and preserve the provider’s attribution. Style URLs, tiles, sprites, and glyphs are only requested when configured by the host. For local demos, the bundled NYC geometry and system fonts need no external services.
The tracking story is a composition of Map, Button, Input, Select, Icon, and Pill. Vehicles and journeys are fictional, stored locally, and do not imply live tracking, traffic, or route calculation.

Keep markers and route IDs stable. Updating coordinates moves the existing marker and preserves its button identity. Resource failures show a recoverable state with a list fallback; WebGL support is required to draw the map.
components.readme:
# Map `Map` renders a host-supplied MapLibre style with selectable markers, route lines, camera controls, and a recoverable unavailable state. Import it from the public owner entry: ```jsx 'use client'; import { useState } from 'react'; import { Map } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Map'; const meeting = { id: 'meeting', coordinates: [-73.983, 40.7535], label: 'Bryant Park meeting point' }; export function MeetingMap({ mapStyle }) { const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(null); return (

Bryant Park, 42nd Street and Sixth Avenue, New York.

{selectedId === meeting.id && (

Meet at the Sixth Avenue entrance.

)}
); } ``` Pass your application's MapLibre style object or style URL as `mapStyle`. Keep object styles stable, for example with a module constant or `useMemo`. Load `@gaudi/design-system/styles.css` once in your application's stylesheet entry; it already includes MapLibre's CSS. ## Data and application ownership Coordinates always use `[longitude, latitude]`. Supply valid coordinates and stable, unique string or number IDs. Keep each ID's type consistent across data, selection, and callbacks. Updating a marker's coordinates moves its existing button, preserving focus. | Prop | Contract | | --- | --- | | `mapStyle` | Required MapLibre style object or URL. Changing it preserves the current camera and reloads the style and overlays. | | `markers` | Array of `{ id, coordinates, label, tone?, icon?, badge? }`; defaults to `[]`. `label` is the button's accessible name. `tone` uses Button tones and defaults to `accent`; `icon` accepts a React node and defaults to a map pin. | | `selectedMarkerId` | Controlled selection. Match a marker ID exactly, or use `null` for no selection. | | `onMarkerClick` | Receives the activated marker's ID, including activation from the fallback list. Update `selectedMarkerId` to accept the selection. | | `routes` | Array of `{ id, coordinates, color?, width?, dashed? }`; defaults to `[]`. Each route needs at least two coordinate pairs. Defaults are `#2563eb`, `3` pixels, and a solid line. | Selecting a marker does not change the camera. Focusing an offscreen marker brings it into view. Routes are prepared line strings, without route calculation or route selection. The host determines status labels, colors, filtering, selected route emphasis, and any location details shown beside the map. Gaudi supplies no basemap, provider endpoint, access token, geocoding, routing, traffic, or tracking service. The application owns those integrations, data updates, tiles, sprites, glyphs, and required attribution. Include attribution in the supplied style's sources; the map shows MapLibre's compact attribution control. Avoid the reserved source ID `gaudi-routes` and layer IDs `gaudi-routes-solid` and `gaudi-routes-dashed` in your style. Storybook's tracking, single-location, and recovery examples use local NYC geography in `.storybook/public/static/maps` and fictional journey data. Those assets are documentation fixtures and are not shipped in the npm package. ## Camera and events | Prop | Default and behavior | | --- | --- | | `initialViewState` | `{ center: [0, 0], zoom: 2 }`. Accepts `center`, `zoom`, `bearing`, and `pitch`. Applied on mount and retry; later prop changes do not move the camera. Reset uses the latest value. | | `interactive` | `true`. Enables pan, zoom, and keyboard navigation. When false, camera gestures and controls are disabled; marker buttons remain selectable. | | `controls` | `true`. Shows reset, zoom in, and zoom out while interactive. | | `scrollZoom` | `false`. Opt in to wheel zoom when appropriate for the surrounding page. | | `minZoom` / `maxZoom` | `0` / `20`. Updates clamp the current camera without replacing the map. | | `onLoad` | Receives the view when the map is ready, and again after a replacement style becomes ready. | | `onViewStateChange` | Receives the view after camera movement ends. This is a notification, not a controlled camera prop. | | `onError` | Receives renderer, style, or source errors. The unavailable state handles recovery locally. | Views have `{ center: [longitude, latitude], zoom, bearing, pitch }`. Attach a React ref for explicit camera actions after `onLoad`: | Ref method | Behavior | | --- | --- | | `flyTo(view)` | Moves to the supplied camera values. | | `fitBounds(bounds, options?)` | Fits `[[west, south], [east, north]]`; accepts MapLibre fit options and defaults to `48` pixels of padding. | | `reset()` | Returns to the latest `initialViewState`. | | `getViewState()` | Returns the current view, or `null` before renderer initialization. | Camera methods use a 600 ms transition, or no transition when reduced motion is requested. Built-in zoom controls use 200 ms. Passing a duration does not override these timings. ## Layout, accessibility, and recovery The map fills its container width, defaults to `32rem` tall, and resizes with its container. Use `style` or `className` to set the required height. `children` appear in a bottom-left overlay while ready; keep legends and location cards concise so they fit narrow containers and leave the attribution accessible. Set `label` for the named map region and keyboard canvas; its default is `Map`. Arrow keys pan, plus/minus zoom, and marker and control buttons support Enter/Space. Selected markers expose `aria-pressed`. A marker's `badge` is visual metadata hidden from assistive technology, so include its meaning in `label` (for example, “TRK-208, 25 minutes delayed”). Provide a visible list or textual summary for important locations and routes; the geographic canvas is not a screen-reader equivalent. Use labels, icons, or line patterns alongside status colors. Keep essential information outside `children`, which is hidden during loading and failure. While loading, the map announces its loading status. On error, it presents an unavailable message, a selectable marker list, and a retry button. Supply `fallback` to replace the list with application-specific content; retry remains available. Retry rebuilds the renderer with the current style and initial view. Replacing a failed style with a valid one also supports recovery. After recovery from a focused fallback or retry button, focus moves to the map canvas. Override state and control text with `labels={{ loading, unavailable, retry, zoomIn, zoomOut, reset }}`. These keys localize those messages and buttons; they do not replace the canvas keyboard instructions or the controls group's accessible name. The component imports MapLibre in a client effect, so server rendering does not initialize WebGL. Drawing the map requires browser WebGL support. MapLibre is a package dependency and uses its bundled worker; no custom worker setup or Vite dependency exclusion is required. If the host enforces a Content Security Policy, its worker policy must allow `blob:` workers and its resource policy must allow the host's configured map resources.

components.readme:
# NavigationMenu A site navigation bar with plain links and dropdown panels of related destinations. Use it for a header's primary navigation; use `DropdownMenu` for actions and `Tabs` for views within one page. ```jsx import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuDropdown, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuPanel } from '@gaudi/design-system'; Blog Data ``` Dropdowns open on click, close on Escape (focus returns to the trigger) or an outside click, and only one is open at a time. `align` and `width` place and size a panel, which is nudged back inside the viewport near an edge; `defaultOpen` starts one open. `active` marks the current page with `aria-current="page"`. Links close the open panel when followed. The convenience components are built on the composition parts (`NavigationMenuRoot`, `NavigationMenuTrigger`, `NavigationMenuContent`, `NavigationMenuLinkPrimitive`, `NavigationMenuViewport`, `NavigationMenuIndicator`), which add hover-to-open and a shared animated viewport for custom menus. For a two-block panel, pass `aside` to `NavigationMenuDropdown`: the children fill the first column and the aside the second (stacked below `sm`, `width='2xl'` gives both room). `NavigationMenuAside` is the usual second block, a muted column with a small title, an optional `action` (`{ href, label }` renders a "See all →" link) and its own links, labelled by its title for assistive technology. ```jsx
    {posts.map((post) =>
  • {post.title}
    • )}
} >
    {categories.map((category) =>
  • {category.title}
    • )}
 ```

components.readme:
# NumberField

A numeric input with step buttons, for quantities, durations and prices within a known range. Use a Slider when an approximate value is enough.

## Usage

```jsx
import { NumberField, NumberFieldDecrement, NumberFieldGroup, NumberFieldIncrement, NumberFieldInput, NumberFieldScrubArea } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<NumberField defaultValue={5} min={0} max={10} step={1}>
  <NumberFieldScrubArea label='Articles per week' />
  <NumberFieldGroup>
    <NumberFieldDecrement aria-label='Decrease' />
    <NumberFieldInput />
    <NumberFieldIncrement aria-label='Increase' />
  </NumberFieldGroup>
</NumberField>;
```

`size` (`sm`, `default`, `lg`) sets the control height, and `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options for units and currency.

Inside `Field`, the input automatically receives its label ID, description and error state. Use an explicit root `id` when composing primitive labels.

The editor is text-based, so it inherits `InputConfigProvider` smooth caret mode. Use `NumberFieldInput caretMode='native'` or `caretMode='smooth'` for an individual override. Prefer this component to `Input type='number'` when you need smooth caret movement with numeric bounds, stepping and formatting. The native number input does not expose its caret position.

## Accessibility

Arrow keys step the value, Home and End jump to `min` and `max`, and typed values clamp on blur. Give the step buttons an `aria-label`.

components.readme:
# Pagination

Moves between pages of a long list. Use `PaginationBar` under a post archive or search results; compose the parts for numbered, compact or table-footer pagers.

```jsx
import { PaginationBar } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<PaginationBar currentPage={3} totalPages={8} getHref={(page) => `/blog/page/${page}`} />
```

`PaginationBar` shows Previous, an "n of total" status and Next. Previous and Next disable at either end; clicking the status or pressing Enter or Space opens page shortcuts, with ellipses past five pages. From a server component, where functions can't cross into this client module, pass strings instead of `getHref`: `hrefTemplate='/blog/page/{page}'` and `firstPageHref='/blog'`. `POSTS_PER_PAGE` (7) is safe to import on the server. Pass `onPageChange` for client-side paging: page links become buttons and the host owns `currentPage`. `label` names the landmark; `previousLabel`, `nextLabel`, `ofLabel` and `shortcutsLabel` (also on `PaginationStatus`) translate the remaining copy, defaulting to Previous, Next, of and Page shortcuts.

The parts (`Pagination`, `PaginationContent`, `PaginationItem`, `PaginationLink`, `PaginationPrevious`, `PaginationNext`, `PaginationEllipsis`) are built on `Button`: `PaginationLink` is a router-aware link with `href`, a button with `onClick`, or a disabled button with `disabled`, and `isActive` marks the current page with `aria-current="page"`.

components.readme:
# PhoneInput

A phone number field with a searchable country picker that stores the number in international (E.164) format.

## Usage

```jsx
import { PhoneInput } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<PhoneInput id='phone' defaultCountry='US' value={phone} onChange={setPhone} />;
```

`variant` (`sm`, `default`, `lg`) sets the height, and `international` shows the calling code in the input.

## Accessibility

Label the input with a `Label` or `aria-label`. Setting `aria-invalid` marks the country picker and the number together.

components.readme:
# Pill

A small label for a status, category, tag or count. Use `Pill` when you want a named tone (`blue`, `green`, `amber`…) with a
`variant` for emphasis; use `Badge` when you compose with the semantic variants (`success-light`, `destructive-outline`…).
Both render the same Badge element, and Pill tones read from the shared Button tone scale, so they switch with the theme.

```jsx
import { Badge, Pill } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Pill tone='green' variant='soft' size='sm' pulse>Live</Pill>
<Pill href='/blog/tags/tokens' tone='gray' variant='soft'>#tokens</Pill>
<Badge variant='success-light'>Shipped</Badge>
<Badge variant='discovery-light'>Suggested</Badge>
<Badge variant='attention-light'>Needs review</Badge>
```

- `tone`: `blue` (default), `green`, `amber`, `red`, `indigo`, `teal`, `rose`, `neutral`, `gray`; `yellow` is an alias of `amber`.
- `variant`: `solid` (default), `soft`, `outline`, `ghost`, `subtle`. `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`. `radius`: `sm` (default), `md`, `full`.
- `href` renders a link with a comfortable hit target; `icon` adds a decorative leading icon; `pulse` adds a decorative live dot, so keep the meaning in the text.
- `Badge` variants: `default`, `secondary`, `outline`, and the semantic `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`,
  `discovery`, `attention`, `focus`, `invert`, each with `-light` and `-outline` treatments (`primary-light`/`primary-outline` too).
  Use `discovery` for suggested or generated labels (for example tags proposed by an assistant) and `attention` for records
  that need a person to look (staged, unreviewed). They read from the `--ds-color-discovery*` and `--ds-color-attention*` tokens.
- `BadgeRoot` and `badgeVariantsPrimitive` are kept as aliases of `Badge` and `badgeVariants`.

components.readme:
# Pointer

A decorative pointer scoped to a container. It supplies direct, spring, and lazy tracking with dot, ring, corner-frame, and contextual-label variants.

```jsx
import { Pointer, Button } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Pointer variant='frame' tracking='lazy' className='min-h-80 p-8'>
  <Button>Explore work</Button>
</Pointer>
```

Also available from `@gaudi/design-system/core/Pointer`. Load Gaudi's stylesheet once. `tone` is `neutral` or `accent`; `hideCursor={false}` keeps the native cursor beside the effect. `disabled` turns off the decoration without disabling the content. The forwarded ref and DOM props belong to the container. A cancelled pointer enter/move handler prevents that event from moving the follower.

For `variant='label'`, supply a default `label` and optional `data-pointer-label='View project'` on individual targets. Keep a visible accessible label on each action; the pointer label is only a decoration. Set `data-pointer-native` on selectable text or any region that should retain its native cursor. Inputs, textareas, selects, and editable content do this automatically.

The follower appears only after a real mouse enters. Touch, pen, reduced motion, window blur, scrolling, and keyboard use hide it and restore the native cursor. The overlay is clipped to its container, is hidden from assistive technology, and never intercepts clicks. Springs settle when movement stops and are stopped on exit; listeners are cleaned up on unmount. Nested followers have independent scopes.

The lazy frame revisits the dot-and-corner-frame behavior of an earlier website cursor by the same author. The motion references are [Asterisk](https://www.withasterisk.com/) and [Skiper UI's mouse-follow examples](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper61). Gaudi uses its existing Motion dependency, shared hooks, icons, and tokens; no Skiper or Asterisk source or remote assets are included.

components.readme:
# Popover

A button that opens a small, non-modal panel for supporting content: share settings, quick filters, a short form. Use a hover card for read-only previews that open on hover, and a Dialog when the task needs the user's full attention.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Popover } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Popover trigger='Share' side='bottom' align='start'>
  <PopoverHeader>
    <PopoverTitle>Share this draft</PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverDescription>Anyone with the link can view.</PopoverDescription>
  </PopoverHeader>
</Popover>
```

## API

| Prop                                         | Type                            | Contract                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`                                    | ReactNode                       | Content of the outline button that opens the panel.       |
| `children`                                   | ReactNode                       | Panel content.                                            |
| `side / align`                               | top, right, bottom, left / start, center, end | Preferred placement; collisions may flip it. |
| `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange / modal`  | boolean / boolean / function / boolean | Controlled or initial visibility.                  |
| `className / contentClassName`               | string                          | Classes for the trigger button and the panel.             |

## Composition

`@gaudi/design-system/core/Popover` exports the compound parts: `Popover`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `PopoverAnchor`, `PopoverHeader`, `PopoverTitle`, `PopoverDescription`, and `HoverCard`, `HoverCardTrigger`, `HoverCardContent`. From the package root the parts are `PopoverPrimitive`, `PopoverTriggerPrimitive` and `PopoverContentPrimitive`, because `Popover` there is the convenience component.

## Accessibility

The trigger is a native button with `aria-expanded`. Escape and a click outside close the panel and return focus to the trigger. Keep the content short; move long forms into a Dialog.

components.readme:
# Progress

A progress bar for one task. `Progress` adds a label and an optional value text to the `ProgressRoot` bar; use
`ProgressRoot` on its own when the label lives elsewhere (a stepper, a series box, a file row).

```jsx
import Progress, { ProgressRoot } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Progress';

<Progress label='Uploading references' value={31} max={50} valueText='31 of 50 files' tone='accent' />
<ProgressRoot value={62} aria-label='Series progress' />
```

- `value` is clamped between 0 and a finite positive `max` (default 100). Omit it when the amount of work is unknown: the bar
  stays indeterminate instead of inventing a percentage, and stays still for reduced motion.
- `valueText` is shown beside the label and announced as the value; `tone` is `accent`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`.
- The bar is a `progressbar` named by the label, with `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuemax`.

## Progress ring

`ProgressRing` is the circular form for compact places such as board cards and table cells. It carries the same
`progressbar` semantics as the bar: pass `label` (or `aria-labelledby`), `value`, `max`, an optional `valueText`, a
`tone` (accent, info, success, warning, danger, discovery, attention, neutral) and a `size` (xs, sm, md, lg). `showValue`
prints the percentage in the centre at md and lg.

```jsx
import { ProgressRing } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ProgressRing value={58} tone='success' label='BUG-452 completion' />
```

components.readme:
# Questionnaire

A form that shows one question at a time, with progress, keyboard shortcuts for choices, validation and Previous, Skip, Next and Submit actions. Use it for onboarding, surveys and guided setup; use a plain form when people need to see every field at once.

```jsx
import { Questionnaire, QuestionnaireProgress, QuestionnaireItem, QuestionnaireTitle, QuestionnaireChoices, QuestionnaireChoice, QuestionnaireError, QuestionnaireActions, QuestionnairePrevious, QuestionnaireNext, QuestionnaireSubmit } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Questionnaire items={items} onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <QuestionnaireProgress />
  <QuestionnaireItem name='goal' required>
    <QuestionnaireTitle>What brings you here?</QuestionnaireTitle>
    <QuestionnaireChoices>
      <QuestionnaireChoice value='system'>Build a design system</QuestionnaireChoice>
    </QuestionnaireChoices>
    <QuestionnaireError />
  </QuestionnaireItem>
  <QuestionnaireActions>
    <QuestionnairePrevious />
    <QuestionnaireNext />
    <QuestionnaireSubmit />
  </QuestionnaireActions>
</Questionnaire>
```

- `QuestionnaireItem multiple` turns choices into checkboxes; `QuestionnaireInput` takes a written answer; `QuestionnaireSkip` appears on optional questions.
- `shortcuts` labels choices with `letters` or `numbers`; `defaultItem` / `onItemChange` control the active question.
- The actions are Button-styled: Previous and Skip are neutral outlines, Next and Submit are filled. Pass `variant` or `size` to change them.

## Accessibility

Each question is a fieldset, choices are native radios or checkboxes, and the progress is a labelled progress bar. Hidden questions are inert, so focus and screen readers only reach the active one.

# RadioGroup

A set of options where people pick exactly one, such as a plan or a delivery speed. Use a Select when there are more than about seven options.

## Usage

```jsx
import { RadioGroup } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<RadioGroup
  label='Reading digest'
  name='digest'
  defaultValue='weekly'
  variant='cards'
  options={[
    { value: 'weekly', label: 'Weekly', description: 'A concise update every Friday.' },
    { value: 'monthly', label: 'Monthly', description: 'The highlights, once a month.' },
    { value: 'off', label: 'Off', disabled: true }
  ]}
/>;
```

`variant='list'` shows compact rows; `cards` makes each option a bordered card. For custom layouts, compose `RadioGroupRoot` and `RadioGroupItem` with the Field parts.

## Accessibility

A fieldset and legend name the group. Arrow keys move the selection and skip disabled options, and `name` and `required` take part in native form submission.

# Rating

Shows a score as stars, or lets people choose one. Use it for reviews and feedback.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Rating } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Rating rating={4.5} showValue />
<Rating rating={score} editable onRatingChange={setScore} />;

`size` is `sm`, `default` or `lg`, `maxRating` sets the number of stars, and `starClassName` restyles the stars.

A read-only rating is one image named "Rated 4.5 out of 5". An editable rating is a radio group: arrow keys move and select, Home and End jump to the ends.

The indicator does not capture scrolling or text selection; only the optional ring handle receives input. Reduced motion removes the number transition. Progress measures scroll position, not comprehension.
notes: Resizes and content growth are measured automatically. A non-scrollable document is complete (100%); an unresolved target starts at 0%.

Reserve a side gutter for the ruler and room for the ring so they do not cover reading text. Set style.top to place a fixed bar below a site header. For a top bar with no extra configuration, render <ReadingIndicator /> once in the page.

components.readme:
# ReadingIndicator

Track reading position with a top bar, vertical ruler, or circular meter.

```jsx
import { ReadingIndicator } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/ReadingIndicator';

<ReadingIndicator />
```

The default bar is fixed to the top of the page. Set `style={{ top: 64 }}` to clear a fixed header. `variant='ruler'` sits at the end edge; `variant='ring'` sits at the bottom end. Both show a percentage by default. `tone` accepts `accent` or `neutral`.

Pass `targetRef` for a scrolling element or a Gaudi `ScrollArea` root. Inside a panel, use `position='absolute'` and a positioned parent; `position='inline'` leaves placement to the host. Reserve a gutter for the ruler and space for the ring so they do not obscure text.

`contentRef` restricts progress to an article inside the scroll target: 0% when its top reaches the top of the viewport, 100% when its bottom comes into view. Related content is excluded. A fully visible, non-scrollable range is complete. Missing refs remain at 0%. Resizes and dynamic content update the range.

For externally measured progress, set `value` (0–100). Values are clamped; non-finite values become 0. Automatic scroll tracking is suspended while `value` is supplied.

`draggable` gives the ring a handle. `dragBoundsRef` constrains it to a panel; otherwise it stays within the viewport. Arrow keys move by 10px, Shift by 40px; Home or Escape resets it. Inline meters are not draggable. The handle is the only pointer-interactive part.

Use `label` or `aria-labelledby` to name the progressbar. No live region announces every scroll. Reduced motion disables the number transition. Progress describes position, not reading comprehension. The ref and DOM props belong to the outer container.

Visual references: [Skiper UI scroll progress 003](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper95) and [scroll progress 001](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper89). This implementation composes Gaudi progress primitives and Motion; it does not copy registry source or load remote resources.

# Resizable

Panels separated by draggable handles, for layouts where readers choose how much space each area gets: an editor beside a preview, or a mail list beside a reading pane.

```jsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ResizablePanelGroup orientation='horizontal'>
  <ResizablePanel defaultSize='30%' minSize='20%'>Folders</ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle withHandle />
  <ResizablePanel defaultSize='70%'>Messages</ResizablePanel>
</ResizablePanelGroup>
```

- `orientation` sets the split direction; nest a group to split the other way.
- String sizes are percentages. `collapsible` lets a panel close below its `minSize`.
- `withHandle` shows a grip on the handle. Handles are focusable separators: arrow keys resize, Home and End jump to the limits, Enter collapses a collapsible panel.

components.readme:
# SchemaDisplay

An API endpoint or a JSON Schema as a reference card: the method badge, the path with its parameters highlighted, and the parameters, request body and response as an expandable property tree with types, formats, enums, required markers and descriptions.

It lives in Core rather than Chat because API reference is as common in blog posts and app settings as it is in a tool result. In a chat, render it inside a reply or as `ChatMessageTool` output.

## Usage

```jsx
import { SchemaDisplay } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<SchemaDisplay
  method='GET'
  path='/posts/{slug}/comments'
  parameters={[
    { name: 'slug', in: 'path', type: 'string' },
    { name: 'limit', in: 'query', type: 'integer', description: 'At most 50.' }
  ]}
  responseBody={commentsSchema}
  showJson
/>

<SchemaDisplay title='Comment' schema={commentSchema} defaultExpandDepth={2} />
```

## API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `method` / `path` | Endpoint verb (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE colour-coded) and path; `{id}` and `:id` are highlighted. |
| `parameters` | `{ name, in, type?, schema?, required?, description? }`; path parameters are always required. |
| `requestBody` / `responseBody` / `schema` | Plain JSON Schema: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `items`, `enum`, `format`, `description`, `oneOf`/`anyOf`. |
| `defaultExpandDepth` | Levels of nested objects that start open (default 1). |
| `showJson` | Adds a Schema / JSON toggle with the raw definition in `CodeBlock`. |
| `headingLevel` | Heading level of the section titles (default 3). |
| `SchemaDisplayMethod`, `SchemaDisplayPath`, `SchemaDisplayProperties` | The badge, the path and the property tree on their own. |

It reads schemas only. Fetching, `$ref` resolution and validation stay in the app.

## Accessibility

Section titles are real headings. Nested objects open from disclosure buttons with `aria-expanded`. "required" is written out rather than shown by colour, and highlighted path parameters keep their braces.

components.accessibility: Give the viewport a useful accessible name using aria-label or aria-labelledby. Constrain the area dimensions and retain keyboard access. Reduced motion skips the smooth engine entirely; native scrolling remains available before hydration or if the enhancement cannot load. Nested scrollable content keeps its own wheel behavior.
notes: A page that scrolls as a whole, such as a blog post between a site header and footer, keeps native page scrolling and uses ScrollEdges without targetRef for the same blurred edges. Use a bounded ScrollArea when the reading area is the only scroller, as in the Article examples.

Smooth scrolling is an enhancement to the existing ScrollArea owner, not a second global page scroller. Bound the height, including min-h-0 when using a flex layout. Avoid stacking a second document-wide smoothing engine around it.

Native fragment links, keyboard scrolling, focus, text selection and touch retain browser behavior. Pointer and keyboard intent interrupt any pending wheel inertia. Code, tables and other nested scroll regions scroll natively.
Theme the track and thumb through scrollbarClassName. Keep enough contrast and an adequate hit area. Use ScrollBar with orientation="horizontal" for content that deliberately overflows horizontally.
Inspired by Shadix UI Smooth Scroll Area. Gaudi composes its existing Radix viewport with the packaged Lenis engine; it does not load remote scripts or copy registry source.

# Scrollspy Highlights the link for the section currently in view and scrolls to a section when its link is clicked. Use it for a table of contents beside a long document or a scrollable panel. ```jsx import { useRef } from 'react'; import { ScrollArea, Scrollspy } from '@gaudi/design-system'; const targetRef = useRef(null);
…
…

components.readme:
# Select

Pick one or several values from a list. Use it for form fields with a known set of options; use a combobox when people type to filter a long list, an autocomplete when free text is also allowed, and a native select for the plainest, platform-styled field.

```jsx
import { Select } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Select
  aria-label='Topics'
  options={[{ value: 'design-systems', label: 'Design systems', description: 'Tokens and components.' }]}
  multiple
  searchable
  onValueChange={setTopics}
/>
```

- `options` takes `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`; native `<option>` children work when `options` is empty.
- `multiple` keeps the popup open and counts the selection in the trigger. `searchable` adds a filter field that matches labels and descriptions.
- `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` control the selection; `name` submits it with a form. `invalid`, `disabled` and `loading` cover the field states.
- The options API composes the shared `Combobox` trigger, popup, search input and rows; keyboard navigation, focus and viewport collision handling belong to that primitive.

## Composition

`@gaudi/design-system/core/Select` also exports the compound families: `SelectRoot` with `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`, `SelectContent`, `SelectItem`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectLabel`, `SelectSeparator`; `Combobox*` (with chips for multiple values); `Autocomplete*`; and `NativeSelect`, `NativeSelectOption`, `NativeSelectOptGroup`.

## Accessibility

The trigger is a button with `aria-haspopup='listbox'`. Arrow keys, Home and End highlight options; disabled options remain discoverable but cannot be selected. Enter selects an enabled option, and Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Give every select a visible label or `aria-label`.

components.readme:
# Separator

A thin rule that divides content horizontally or vertically.

```jsx
import { Separator } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Separator />
<Separator orientation='vertical' />
```

- Separators are decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology. Set `decorative={false}` when the rule marks a real change of section, so it is announced as a separator.
- Vertical separators stretch to the height of their flex row; give them a height to keep them shorter.

components.readme:
# SignaturePad Composable signature entry with SVG ink, mouse/touch/pen input, undo/redo, a native form value, saved previews, and PNG, JPEG, SVG, or JSON export. Adapted from [ReUI Signature Pad](https://reui.io/docs/components/base/signature-pad), under the MIT notice in the [root README](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices). ```jsx import { SignaturePad, SignaturePadArea, SignaturePadGuide, SignaturePadPlaceholder, SignaturePadClear, SignaturePadSave } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/SignaturePad';
save(dataUrl, strokes)} />
``` ## Value and editing Each stroke is `{ points: [[x, y, diameter], ...], color? }`. Coordinates use the drawing area's CSS pixel space; the display scales existing ink uniformly when a container becomes smaller without mutating the stored data. `onValueChange` fires once when a stroke completes or history changes, never for each pointer move. Treat values as immutable. `value` is controlled; `defaultValue` initializes local state. Equal deep copies preserve history. A different external value starts a new history. Refused controlled changes leave the accepted strokes and history authoritative. History retains up to 100 changes. `color` is optional: unset ink follows the theme. `minWidth` / `maxWidth` set the ink diameter (0.8 / 3.2 by default); `smoothing` is 0–1. `sizing='auto'` uses pen pressure and mouse/touch velocity. Use `pointerTypes={['pen']}` to reject touch. Pointer cancellation, lost capture, Escape, a resize during drawing, or disabling/locking the pad discard unfinished ink. Overlay controls do not draw beneath themselves. ## Parts and API - `SignaturePadArea`: labelled drawing area; `variant='default' | 'muted' | 'ghost'`. Fills its container width with a default height of `12rem`; override its height with a class. - `SignaturePadGuide`, `SignaturePadPlaceholder`: optional non-interactive overlays. - `SignaturePadControls`: pinned controls; `position='top-start' | 'top-end' | 'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end'`. - `SignaturePadUndo`, `SignaturePadRedo`, `SignaturePadClear`, `SignaturePadSave`: Gaudi buttons, supporting button props and text children. Their click handlers compose with host handlers and honor `preventDefault()`. - `SignaturePadPreview`: a server-renderable, standalone SVG from `strokes`, cropped with `padding` (default 4). Supply an `aria-label` for its purpose. - `useSignaturePad()` or `apiRef`: `strokes`, `isEmpty`, `isDrawing`, `canUndo`, `canRedo`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `clear()`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `focus()`, `toSVG(options)`, `toDataURL(options)`, `toBlob(options)`, `serialize(format, options)`. Editing operations also respect disabled/read-only state. ## Styling The pad follows Gaudi's compact neutral styling: shared rounded corners, input border, semantic background/foreground colors, and the accent token for visible focus. These tokens support light and dark themes. Component gaps and internal padding follow the `--ds-space-scale` multiplier. Pinned controls wrap within the drawing area; completed ink preserves its proportions as the container shrinks, as described above. ## Forms and exports `name` creates a native field; `form` associates it with an external form. `required` rejects an empty value and focuses the drawing area. `format` defaults to SVG. PNG/JPEG form formats rasterize after each completed change; SVG/JSON avoid that work. A disabled pad is omitted from `FormData`. Native reset restores `defaultValue` and clears history; cancelling reset preserves the value. `invalid` and `aria-describedby` connect application validation feedback. Save returns a data URL for PNG, JPEG, or SVG; JSON returns the stroke array as a string. It does not upload or download. Export helpers are `getSignaturePadBounds`, `getSignaturePadStrokePath`, `signaturePadToSVG`, `signaturePadToDataURL`, `signaturePadToBlob`, and `serializeSignaturePad`. Raster helpers require a browser and belong in handlers/effects; SVG/JSON helpers and previews work on the server. Empty serialization is an empty string. Exports crop to the ink including stroke thickness and 8px padding. Both `width` and `height` fix a frame; `crop: false` keeps the origin. With the pad API, `crop: false` uses its displayed coordinate frame. `color` defaults to black; `background` is transparent except JPEG, which defaults to white. Raster `scale` defaults to 2; `type` and `quality` configure the image. Use `toBlob()` for uploads without base64 expansion. ## Accessibility and application boundaries Give the area a visible label with `aria-labelledby` and instructions through `aria-describedby`. `labels` overrides default labels and instructions. Undo/redo supports Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z, and Ctrl/Cmd+Y; editable overlays and IME keep their own keyboard handling. The surface shows focus, preserves ink across themes, and returns focus from actions that disable themselves. Drawing has no keyboard equivalent. The Draw or Type example composes existing Tabs, Input, and Button and stores the typed name as a separate application value. Applications own consent, document identity, persistence, upload, and signing policy; this component collects input.

Shimmer keeps its words as real text; put it in a status region when the change should be announced. Both hold still for reduced motion. SkeletonMorph marks its region aria-busy and announces its label in a status message while loading; placeholders stay hidden, content renders only once loaded, and reduced motion swaps without animating.

components.readme:
# Skeleton A skeleton is a grey placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the layout does not jump when it arrives. ```jsx import { Skeleton } from '@gaudi/design-system';
Loading the latest article
``` - Shape each block with `className` (height, width, `rounded-full` for avatars) to match the content it stands in for. - Inside text, such as a paragraph or a link, render it as a span: ``. - Skeletons are hidden from assistive tech. Mark the region `aria-busy` and add a status message that names what is loading. - Use a skeleton when the layout is known; use `Loader` for short waits or when the shape is unknown. ## Shimmer `Shimmer` is the text counterpart: a highlight sweeps across a label while work is in progress, such as "Thinking…" in a chat reply or "Searching the web…" in an agent step. ```jsx import { Shimmer } from '@gaudi/design-system';

Searching the web…

Drafting the summary ``` - `duration` is one sweep in seconds (default 2); `spread` is the band width in pixels per character (default 2); `active={false}` rests it as plain text. - The words stay real text, so they are read, selectable and translated. Put the label in a status region when the change should be announced. - The sweep is the `shimmer` utility on the text tokens; it holds still for reduced motion and in forced-colour modes. ## Skeleton morph `SkeletonMorph` grows its placeholders into the loaded content instead of swapping them: when `loading` turns false, each `SkeletonMorphBlock` resizes from its placeholder to its content as the content fades in, one block after another in document order. ```jsx import { SkeletonMorph, SkeletonMorphBlock } from '@gaudi/design-system'; …

{user?.name}

{user?.bio}

 ``` - Size each placeholder like its content: `width`/`height` for a block (numbers are pixels), or `lines` with the content's `lineHeight` (default 20) for text. `shape='circle'` is for avatars. - Block children render only once loaded, but the JSX is still evaluated while loading, so read optional data (`user?.name`). - The region is `aria-busy` while loading and announces `label` in a status message; `as` renders it as another element or component, such as `CardContent`. Placeholders stay hidden from assistive tech, and focus is not moved. - Reduced motion swaps without animating. Use it for cards, short lists and dashboards whose layout is known in advance; keep plain `Skeleton` rows for long tables, where animating layout is costly, and `Loader` for waits longer than a few seconds.

components.readme:
# Slider

Picks a value, or a range with two thumbs, by dragging along a track. Use it for approximate settings such as volume or a price range; use a NumberField when the exact number matters.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Slider } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Slider aria-label='Volume' defaultValue={[50]} min={0} max={100} step={5} onValueChange={setVolume} />;
```

Pass two values for a range. `orientation` is `horizontal` or `vertical`.

## Accessibility

Each thumb is a `slider` named from `aria-label` (numbered for ranges). Arrow keys step the value, Home and End jump to the ends. Show the current value as text next to the slider.

components.readme:
# Sortable

Drag-and-drop reordering for lists, lanes, and grids, with keyboard support. Use it when the order of items matters to the reader, such as a checklist or a gallery cover.

```jsx
import { Sortable, SortableItem, SortableItemHandle } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Sortable value={tasks} onValueChange={setTasks} getItemValue={(task) => task.id}>
  {tasks.map((task) => (
    <SortableItem key={task.id} value={task.id}>
      <SortableItemHandle aria-label={`Reorder ${task.title}`}>⋮⋮</SortableItemHandle>
      {task.title}
    </SortableItem>
  ))}
</Sortable>
```

- `strategy`: `vertical` (default), `horizontal`, or `grid`.
- `onValueCommit` fires once per completed move, which is where you persist the new order.
- `disabled` on an item pins it in place. `SortableOverlay` customises the lifted copy shown while dragging.
- Handles are buttons: Space picks up an item, arrow keys move it, Space drops it, and Escape cancels.

components.readme:
# Switch

A toggle for a setting that takes effect immediately, such as notifications or dark mode. Use a Checkbox when the choice is only saved with a form.

## Usage

```jsx
import { Switch } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Switch label='Email notifications' size='md' checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} />;
```

`size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg`. For rows with icons and descriptions, compose `SwitchRoot` (sizes `sm`, `default`, `lg`) with the Field parts.

## Accessibility

The control is a `switch` with `aria-checked`, toggled by Space or a click on its label.

components.readme:
# Tabs

Switches between related panels on the same page. Use it for views of one thing (overview, history, settings); use `NavigationMenu` or links when each view has its own URL.

```jsx
<Tabs defaultValue='overview'>
  <TabsList aria-label='Article'>
    <TabsTrigger value='overview'>Overview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='history'>History</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value='overview'>Article details</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value='history'>Revision history</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

| Prop / export | Type | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value / defaultValue / onValueChange` | string / string / function | Controlled or uncontrolled active panel. |
| `orientation` | horizontal or vertical | List direction and arrow keys. |
| `activationMode` | automatic or manual | Select on focus, or wait for Enter/Space. |
| `TabsList variant` | default or line | `line` drops the rule under the list. |
| `TabsTrigger / TabsContent` | components | Match their `value`; triggers accept `disabled`. |

Label each `TabsList`. Use manual activation when a panel is expensive to load.

Keyboard focus is drawn inside each trigger, so the scrolling list never clips it. In forced-colours mode (Windows High Contrast) idle tabs drop their border and the selected tab draws it, and its underline, in `Highlight`.

components.readme:
# Textarea

Multiline fields reuse FieldInput validation and description wiring. Supports native rows, maxLength, required, readOnly and form attributes.

## Usage

```jsx
import Textarea from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Textarea';

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Summary</FieldLabel>
  <Textarea name='summary' placeholder='What should the reader take away?' />
  <FieldDescription>
    A short introduction for the article index.
  </FieldDescription>
</Field>;
```

## Accessibility

Labels and errors are associated with the textarea. Vertical resizing preserves the available width.

## Examples

The Playground shows a review note with a counter and the invalid and disabled states; the catalogue adds field states and auto-resize.

`caretMode='smooth'` enables animated caret movement within a line; wrapped-line changes snap vertically. It inherits `InputConfigProvider` when omitted. See [Input caret mode](../Input/README.md#smooth-caret-mode) for native fallbacks.

# Timeline

A dated activity feed or a set of milestones. `Timeline` takes an `items` array and renders an ordered list built from
the Timeline parts; compose `TimelineRoot`, `TimelineItem`, `TimelineIndicator`, `TimelineSeparator`, `TimelineHeader`,
`TimelineTitle`, `TimelineDate` and `TimelineContent` directly for steps, horizontal rails or avatars.

```jsx
import Timeline from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Timeline';

<Timeline
  label='Editorial activity'
  items={[{ id: 'published', title: 'Article published', time: '2 days ago', dateTime: '2026-09-27T09:00:00Z', icon: <Icon name='CircleCheck' decorative /> }]}
/>
```

- Each item needs a stable `id` and a `title`; `description`, `time` with a machine-readable `dateTime`, a decorative `icon`
  and `children` (actions, quotes, files) are optional.
- `label` names the list. Icons are decorative, so keep the meaning in the text.
- `TimelineRoot` tracks the active step (`value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `orientation`); `TimelineRoot`,
  `TimelineItem` and `TimelineTitle` accept `asChild` to render your own element, such as `<ol>`, `<li>` or a heading level.

components.readme:
# Toast

Short, non-blocking notifications for finished actions, errors and background work. Mount one `ToastProvider` per app and call `toast()` from anywhere. The toast surface uses Gaudi tokens and its action, cancel and close buttons use the Button variants.

## Usage

```jsx
<ToastProvider />
<Button onClick={() => toast.success('Draft saved')}>Save draft</Button>
```

## API

| Prop / export   | Type             | Contract                                                                          |
| --------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ToastProvider` | component        | Mount once; forwards Sonner configuration including position, duration and theme. `toastOptions.classNames` are merged with the Gaudi classes. |
| `toast`         | function         | Use toast(), toast.success(), toast.error(), toast.promise() and toast.dismiss(). |
| `action`        | {label, onClick} | Optional recovery or undo action on a notification.                               |

## Ownership and verification

The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

# ToggleGroup

A toggle group lets people pick one option (a view mode) or several (filters, formatting) from a short set of buttons.

```jsx
import { ToggleGroup } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<ToggleGroup
  label='Collection view'
  defaultValue='list'
  options={[
    { value: 'list', label: 'List' },
    { value: 'grid', label: 'Grid' },
    { value: 'board', label: 'Board', disabled: true }
  ]}
/>
```

- `type='single'` (default) keeps one value and allows clearing it; `type='multiple'` keeps an array.
- `variant` (`outline` or `default`), `size` (`sm`, `default`, `lg`) and `spacing` (0 attaches the items) change the look.
- Icon-only options need an `ariaLabel`.
- For custom item content, compose `ToggleGroupRoot` and `ToggleGroupItem`; use `Toggle` for a single on/off button.
- Arrow keys move between options and skip disabled ones.

# Tooltip

Short, supplementary hints for named controls. Pass content and a single ref-forwarding trigger. Keep it to short text; use a Popover when the content needs a link or a button.

## Usage

```jsx
import Tooltip from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Tooltip';

<Tooltip content='Copy a link to this article'>
  <Button variant='outline' tone='neutral'>
    Copy link
  </Button>
</Tooltip>;
```

## Accessibility

Opens on focus and hover and closes with Escape. The trigger still needs its own accessible name; use Dialog or Popover for interactive details.

## Composition

`TooltipProvider`, `TooltipRoot`, `TooltipTrigger` and `TooltipContent` build custom tooltips; the `Tooltip` component is those parts with one trigger and one hint. Mount one `TooltipProvider` around a toolbar so moving between buttons skips the delay.
