components.accessibility: All controls have accessible names. Space or Enter activates focused buttons; the seek and volume sliders support arrow keys, Home and End. Captions use native text tracks; provide captions for speech and meaningful audio. Dialog traps focus, closes with Escape, and restores focus to its poster. Touch controls stay visible, and reduced motion removes elastic movement.
notes: autoPlay, defaultMuted, and defaultVolume are initial preferences applied when a source mounts or its dialog opens. Updating them does not restart playback or directly update the active video’s muted state or volume. Use the native ref for subsequent programmatic changes.

Only documented video props are supported; arbitrary native attributes such as crossOrigin are not forwarded. Cross-origin media setup belongs to the host integration. className and style apply to the outer player wrapper.
The custom toolbar supports finite-duration files. Unknown or infinite durations disable seeking. Use nativeControls for live streams or device-specific playback features.

Picture-in-picture and fullscreen appear only when supported. Their state follows browser events, and rejected requests show a recoverable message. Support depends on the browser, operating system, and embedding permissions.

Custom controls remain visible. Below a 640px player width they flow below the video; larger standard players place them over the frame. Enabling captions keeps the controls below so they cannot cover the text. Minimal controls stay below the frame at every width.
The Skiper 67, 91, and 97 references informed the interactions. This implementation uses Gaudi primitives and native media APIs; it does not load remote examples or copy registry source.
components.readme:
# VideoPlayer

Native video playback with three presentations: `standard` adds a complete toolbar, `minimal` pares it back around an elastic seek rail, and `dialog` opens the player from a poster with a Gaudi Pointer label.

```jsx
import { VideoPlayer } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/VideoPlayer';

<VideoPlayer
  src='/media/film.webm'
  poster='/media/film.webp'
  title='A short film'
  tracks={[{ src: '/media/film.en.vtt', srcLang: 'en', label: 'English', default: true }]}
/>
```

`aspectRatio` defaults to `16 / 9`; `fit='cover'` crops the frame. Pass `variant='minimal'` or `variant='dialog'` for the other workflows. Dialog supports `open`, `defaultOpen`, and `onOpenChange`. It stops playback on close and restores focus to its poster.

`autoPlay`, `defaultMuted`, and `defaultVolume` are initial preferences applied when a source mounts or its dialog opens. They are not controlled playback props: changing them does not restart playback or directly update the active video's muted state or volume. Browser policy may reject autoplay; the player keeps Play available and explains the failure. `loop` and `preload` map to the native video. Media events drive the controls; `onPlay`, `onPause`, `onEnded`, `onTimeUpdate`, and `onError` receive native events. A forwarded `ref` points to the active HTMLVideoElement, or null while the dialog is closed; use it for subsequent programmatic playback changes. Changing `src` resets playback and ignores pending work from the old source.

The standard toolbar includes play/pause/replay, buffered seeking, mute, volume, caption selection, speed, and supported fullscreen/picture-in-picture actions. Minimal retains play, seeking, time, mute, captions, and supported fullscreen. The custom timeline supports finite-duration media; unknown or live durations disable seeking. Set `nativeControls` for browser-owned controls or device-specific/live playback. This still requires a browser-playable `src`; it does not add streaming adapters or codec support. Fullscreen and picture-in-picture depend on browser support and embedding permissions; failures leave inline playback available.

Buttons support Enter/Space. Sliders support arrow keys, Home and End, with spoken time/volume values. The dialog uses Gaudi’s focus trap and Escape handling. Reduced motion disables elastic movement. Touch targets enlarge, and controls wrap below videos in containers narrower than 640px. Captioned playback keeps controls below the frame at every width, preserving authored cue placement. Minimal controls always stay below the frame.

Provide accurate WebVTT captions for meaningful audio. Tracks default to `kind='captions'`; only captions and subtitles appear in the caption selector. Selecting a language or turning captions off changes only those track modes, leaving metadata and chapter track modes untouched. The component accepts the documented video props rather than forwarding arbitrary native attributes, including `crossOrigin`. Serve tracks from the same origin; cross-origin media setup belongs to the host integration. `className` and `style` apply to the outer player wrapper.

## Story assets and inspiration

The 12-second WebM, WebP poster, and English VTT in `.storybook/public/static/media/video-demo*` are local demo assets. The clip slowly zooms Gaudi’s existing `static/images/art/0.svg` with a title overlay and a quiet synthesized 220Hz tone fading in/out. It was generated from a browser render of the SVG with ImageMagick (960×540, Arial title) and FFmpeg (`zoompan`, VP9, 24fps, Opus); no external media is loaded. `video-invalid.webm` intentionally contains text to demonstrate media-error recovery.

Interaction references: [Skiper 67](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper67), [Skiper 91](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper91), and [Skiper 97](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper97). Independently implemented with native media APIs and Gaudi components; no registry source is copied.

components.readme:
# WebPreview

A framed browser for showing a live or generated page inside an interface: back, forward and reload, an editable address bar, open in a new tab, device widths, a sandboxed iframe with a loading state, an optional console, and a LinkPreview card when a site refuses to be framed. Use it for assistant replies that built a page, deploy previews and documentation demos.

## Usage

```jsx
import { WebPreview } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<WebPreview
  defaultUrl='https://preview.example.dev/'
  srcDoc={(url) => generatedPages[url]}
  logs={logs}
  title='Generated landing page'
/>

// The app knows a site refuses framing (its preview endpoint can read X-Frame-Options).
<WebPreview defaultUrl='https://github.com/vercel/next.js' embeddable={false} previewData={payload} />
```

- `url` / `defaultUrl` with `onUrlChange`; `device` / `defaultDevice` (`desktop`, `tablet` 768px, `phone` 390px) with `onDeviceChange`. Narrow screens scroll inside the frame, never the page.
- `srcDoc` renders generated HTML; a function `(url) => html | null` serves several pages so the address bar works offline.
- `logs` (`{ level: 'log' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error', message, timestamp? }`) shows the console; the host collects them (for example over `postMessage`), the preview never reads the framed page.
- `sandbox` defaults to `allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-presentation allow-modals`. `allow-same-origin` is left out on purpose: with scripts it would let the page reach the host.
- The address bar adds `https://` to bare hosts and refuses `javascript:`, `data:` and `file:` addresses (`normalizeWebPreviewUrl`).

## Parts

Compose `WebPreviewRoot`, `WebPreviewNavigation`, `WebPreviewHistoryButtons`, `WebPreviewNavigationButton`, `WebPreviewUrl`, `WebPreviewOpenButton`, `WebPreviewDevices`, `WebPreviewBody` and `WebPreviewConsole` for a different toolbar; `useWebPreview()` reads the state. The history, address and log rules are pure functions in the same entry.

## Accessibility

The controls sit in a labelled toolbar with named buttons and tooltips, the address bar is a labelled field that reports unusable input in an alert, the width toggle is a radio group, the iframe has a `title`, the body is `aria-busy` while loading, and the console is a disclosure over a `role="log"` list whose toggle names errors and warnings.

components.readme: # App Shell ## Patterns The app-shell examples (`Blocks/App Shell`) are Gaudi compositions for knowledge, reading, research and finance workspaces: a library rail, a reading desk, research projects, a digest inbox, a publishing console, notebook tabs, a research assistant, a newsletter reader, study chat, two top-bar layouts (collections and journal), crawler control, a source network and a finance dashboard. Every example follows these conventions so parallel work stays consistent. **Files and names** - Fixture `src/components/blocks/AppShell/stories/fixtures/app-shell/app-shell-.jsx` exports `Pattern`; the slug is a short descriptive kebab-case name (for example `app-shell-library-rail`), never a number. Import Gaudi parts directly from public namespaces such as `@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AppShell`, `@gaudi/design-system/core/Button`, `@gaudi/design-system/icons/RegistryIcon`, and `@gaudi/design-system/hooks/interaction/use-hotkey`. Package self-reference lets the fixture and its copyable source share the same imports. - Story `export const = { name, ...pattern('', description), play }` lives in an owner-local story file: most patterns use `AppShellPatterns.stories.jsx`, the library rail is the primary story in `AppShell.stories.jsx`, and finance uses `FinanceDashboard.stories.jsx`. Keep the shared `Blocks/App Shell` title and owner ID. `name` is `Topology · key features` (for example `Icon rail · workspace switcher, nested nav and user menu`); the description says what the reader can do and how it behaves in a narrow frame. - Each story has a play test built from `AppShell.story-steps.js` helpers: `expectFramed`, `openNavigation` (the docked sidebar, or the phone sheet opened from the header) and `desktopSidebar`. Cover the current page (`aria-current`), the example's actions, any menus or nested navigation, and collapse/expand when the sidebar is docked. The vitest browser is phone sized, so tests must pass in both layouts. - Add the example to `src/docs/catalogue/coverage.json` (`name`, `title`, `description`, `file`, `sha256` of the fixture bytes, `storyId` `blocks-application-appshell--`), then run `pnpm catalogue:sync`. **Visual vocabulary** (reuse these parts; do not restyle them per fixture) - `AppShellFrame` is the root of every example: the bordered app window on the shared card radius, 48rem tall by default (40rem on phones), with internal scrolling. Use `surface='muted'` (default) when the content sits in an inset panel and `surface='default'` for a plain surface with a flush or floating sidebar. - `SidebarProvider` → `Sidebar` (`collapsible='icon'` for rails, `variant='floating'` for cards) → `AppShellPanel` (the `main` landmark; `inset` by default, `inset={false}` for flush content). `AppShellHeader` holds breadcrumbs, search or actions. Place `SidebarTrigger` first in the header, or at the top inside `SidebarHeader` with a header trigger on phones; `AppShellBody` holds the page. - `AppShellNav` follows explicit item `href` links; items without `href` invoke `onValueChange` without navigation. Modifier-clicks keep native link behavior. It renders sidebar groups from data: icons or status dots, count `badge`, inline `tag`, live `indicator`, nested `items` (collapsible, a flyout menu on the icon rail, remembered section view), `collapsible` group labels, `hideOnRail`, and `actions` row menus. Use `itemClassName` for topology-specific active rows (for example raised rows on a floating card). - Collapsed `SidebarMenuButton` rows center their first visual and keep later children screen-reader-only. Portraits are capped at 24px to fit the rail; do not compensate with negative margins. Labels and account menus remain accessible. - `AppShellNav` also takes `item.leading` (a custom mark such as a `ProgressRing` or a presence avatar; speak its value through `status`) and `action` (a `SidebarGroupAction` at the end of the group label). Rows with a count badge keep their label clear of it. - Use `SidebarTrigger` at the top of the shell, inside the sidebar header or before the breadcrumbs. Keep the trigger visible and in the same place when collapsed; do not add a floating edge toggle or reserve a gutter for one. Several shells share the docs page, so give at most one of them the ⌘B shortcut (`shortcut={false}` on the others). - Compose Core `Skeleton` for loading content. Rich placeholder layouts live only in `stories/fixtures/AppShellPlaceholder.jsx` and the Loading layouts story; they are example compositions, not package exports. - The research-assistant, newsletter-reader and study-chat shells add: `SidebarProvider defaultWidth` with `SidebarResizeHandle` (a focusable separator on the edge: drag, arrow keys, Home/End, double-click resets), Core Skeleton compositions for an unloaded conversation, and `AppShellNav` people rows (`avatar`, `presence`, `suffix`), bare counts (`badge: { label, variant: 'plain' }`), a hover `quickAction` beside the row menu and a `action`. Chat shells compose the Chat parts (`ChatModelSelect` with model `icon`/`details`, `ChatPromptComposer actions`) and Core `EmptyState` with a labelled list of Core `Button` starter prompts in a responsive grid. - More placeholder presets: `tiles` (3 × 3 block cards), `board` (tiles under a row of blank cards), `quad` (four short cards above a 2 × 2 grid) and `stack` (three metric tiles above a tall list), from the `block`, `blank`, `tile` and `rows` kinds. - Top bars spanning the window: give `SidebarProvider` `className='flex-col'`, render the header first and put `Sidebar` and `AppShellPanel` in a `relative flex` row below it. `AppShellNotifications` is the bell and notifications sheet (`inset` floats it); `Sidebar` takes `mobileWidth`, `mobileClassName`, `mobileTitle` and `mobileDescription` for a wider or renamed phone sheet; `AppShellNav` takes `labelIcon` and `labelClassName` for route-group headings. - Overlays: menus and tooltips portal to the page; the phone sidebar sheet opens inside the frame. Command palettes (`CommandDialog`) open over the page. - Gaudi tokens only: semantic colours (`bg-success`, `text-text-muted`…), `rounded-(--ds-radius-control)` / `--ds-radius-card` for tiles and cards (circles only for dots and avatars), registry icons through `RegistryIcon`, brand marks from `src/icons/brands`, Gaudi's generated illustrations from Storybook's local `/avatars/...` assets for avatars, and the shared hooks (`useHotkey` for ⌘K). - Check each example at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1600 px in light and dark: the frame border is visible inside the preview, nothing overflows the page, and the rail, nested navigation, menus and phone sheet work. ### Finance dashboard example [FinanceDashboard.stories.jsx](stories/FinanceDashboard.stories.jsx) presents the [finance dashboard fixture](stories/fixtures/app-shell/app-shell-finance-dashboard.jsx) as a copyable composition. It combines flat, labelled navigation groups and a compact search header with stacked revenue bars, report totals, visitor distribution, product sales and a customer table. The layout uses App Shell and Dashboard parts, `BarChart`, `DataTable` and Core controls; actions and selection use Gaudi's default accent, while charts inherit the standard chart palette. Success colours are reserved for positive changes and account or payment status. Navigation switches local views, search finds pages and record details, role and plan filters update the customer table, and report, transaction and invoice tables offer CSV export. All figures and records are illustrative fixture data. Copy the story's public-import source into the consuming application, replace the sample data and `/avatars/` assets, and connect routing, services, permissions and persistence there. The fixture and its private helpers are examples, not package exports. The frame is 62rem tall with a 40rem compact height and internal panel scrolling. Narrow frames use the sidebar sheet, stack the dashboard panels and filters, and keep horizontal table scrolling inside each table. Preserve the frame-scoped ⌘/Ctrl+K search shortcut so other examples on the page do not respond. Closing record details returns focus to the opening control, with the search button as the fallback when a search result has unmounted. ## Overview Application frames at three levels: - **`AppShell`**: a simple responsive workspace with a navigation rail (or a top bar), a mobile navigation sheet, a header, the content landmark, a skip link, an optional detail rail and an optional status bar. It stays in document flow. - **Sidebar parts** (`SidebarProvider`, `Sidebar`, `SidebarInset`, `SidebarTrigger`, `SidebarRail`, menus, groups and sub-menus): for richer shells, such as a rail that collapses to icons, floating and inset sidebars, nested groups with badges and row menus, secondary panels, and right-hand inspectors. On phones the sidebar becomes a Sheet drawer. - **Frame parts** (`AppShellFrame`, `AppShellPanel`, `AppShellHeader`, `AppShellBody`, `AppShellNav`): present either kind of shell as an app window inside a page, a marketing section or a documentation preview. ## Usage ```jsx import AppShell, { AppShellFrame } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AppShell'; import { SkeletonRoot as Skeleton } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Skeleton'; Articles} aside={} statusBar={All changes saved} > // Sidebar-free apps put the brand and navigation in the header. }>… // Inside a page, present the shell as an app window. … ``` ```jsx import { AppShellBody, AppShellFrame, AppShellHeader, AppShellNav, AppShellPanel, Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AppShell'; import { SkeletonRoot as Skeleton } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Skeleton'; {breadcrumb} ``` ## Frame `AppShellFrame` draws a bordered window on `--ds-radius-card` with clipped overflow and a fixed height (`height`, 56rem by default and 40rem in compact layouts; the CSS variables `--ds-app-shell-frame-height` and `--ds-app-shell-frame-height-compact` also set it). Content scrolls inside: `AppShellPanel` (and the simple `AppShell` workspace) scroll on their own, and the sidebar is positioned against the frame instead of the viewport. The frame measures itself, and sidebar parts switch to the phone layout when the frame, not the viewport, is narrower than `compactBelow` (768px). The phone sheet portals into the frame, so it opens inside the window. Menus, tooltips and dialogs still portal to the page. ## API | Prop / export | Type | Contract | | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `brand / navigation / header / footer` | ReactNode | Supplied slot content; the host owns route state and active links. | | `layout` | `sidebar` / `topbar` | A navigation rail, or brand and navigation in the header. | | `aside / asideLabel` | ReactNode / string | A named complementary rail beside the content; stacks below it under xl. | | `statusBar` | ReactNode | A status strip under the content. | | `children` | ReactNode | Page content inside the shell main landmark. | | `navigationLabel / menuLabel / skipLabel` | string | Localized accessible labels. | | `className` | string | Root composition; the desktop rail begins at 1024px. | | `AppShellFrame.height / compactBelow` | string or number / number | Window height (56rem; 40rem when compact) and the frame width for the phone layout (768). | | `AppShellFrame.surface / label` | `muted` / `default`; string | The window surface, and an optional region name. | | `AppShellPanel.inset` | boolean | A bordered panel set into the frame (default), or flush beside a floating sidebar. | | `AppShellHeader.bordered` | boolean | A rule under the sticky panel header. | | `AppShellNav` | items, value, … | Data-driven sidebar group; see the Patterns section and the component docs. | | `SidebarProvider.storageKey` | string | Restores and saves the expanded state in localStorage after mount. | | `SidebarProvider.shortcut` | string / false | The ⌘/Ctrl key that toggles the sidebar (`b`); `false` turns it off. | | `SidebarProvider.labels` | object | `expanded`, `collapsed` announcements and the `toggle` trigger name. | | `Sidebar.variant / collapsible / side` | string | `sidebar`, `floating` or `inset`; `offcanvas`, `icon` or `none`; edge. | | `SidebarTrigger.label / tooltip` | string / boolean | Trigger name, and a tooltip with the shortcut keys. | | `SidebarMenuButton.tooltip` | string / object | Names the item on the collapsed icon rail. | ## Accessibility Keep the skip link and the main landmark, and name each navigation and complementary region. Mark the current page with `aria-current` (`AppShellNav` does; a remembered section view is only highlighted). The trigger reports `aria-expanded` and `aria-keyshortcuts`, and expanding or collapsing is announced politely. Keep the trigger at the top of the sidebar or before the breadcrumbs, including when collapsed. On phones the sidebar is a Sheet that traps focus and returns it to the trigger, and choosing a page closes it. Collapsed icon rails name every item with a tooltip, and nested sections open as menus. Status dots carry a spoken `status`; placeholder grids are decorative and hidden from assistive technology, and their skeletons do not animate. When several shells share a page (as in these docs), turn the shortcut off on all but one, because each provider listens on the window. ## Ownership and verification The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

components.readme:
# AuthForm

Password and email-link form recipes with native validation, pending state and recoverable errors. onSubmit receives form values. Applications own providers, credentials, sessions and navigation.

## Usage

```jsx
<AuthForm
  title='Sign in'
  description='Continue to your writing workspace.'
  onSubmit={signIn}
/>
```

Reuse the recipe for other account steps by renaming the copy: a reset request is `mode='email'` with its own `submitLabel`
and `pendingLabel`.

```jsx
<AuthForm
  title='Reset your password'
  mode='email'
  submitLabel='Send reset link'
  pendingLabel='Sending…'
  emailPlaceholder='you@example.com'
  successMessage='If that address has an account, a reset link is on its way.'
  onSubmit={requestReset}
/>
```

Add single sign-on above the email fields and a reset link beside the password:

```jsx
<AuthForm
  title='Welcome back'
  passwordAction={<Link href='/reset'>Forgot password?</Link>}
  providers={[{ id: 'google', label: 'Google', icon: <Icon name='Google' decorative /> }]}
  onProvider={startOAuth}
  onSubmit={signIn}
/>
```

## API

| Prop / export                                 | Type                         | Contract                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onSubmit`                                    | function({email, password?}) | Required host-owned authentication callback. Reject to show an error. |
| `mode`                                        | password, email or signup    | Password, email-link or sign-up form (name, email, new password).     |
| `title / description / footer`                | ReactNode                    | Product context and links.                                            |
| `submitLabel / successMessage / errorMessage` | string                       | Action and outcome copy.                                              |
| `nameLabel / emailLabel / passwordLabel`      | string                       | Visible accessible field labels.                                      |
| `emailPlaceholder / passwordPlaceholder`      | string                       | Optional example text inside the fields. No placeholder by default.   |
| `passwordHint`                                | ReactNode or false           | Help text under the password; defaults per mode, `false` hides it.    |
| `passwordMinLength` | number | Optional native minimum supplied by the host; signup imposes no minimum by default. Pair it with a matching `passwordHint`. |
| `passwordAction`                              | ReactNode                    | A link beside the password label, such as Forgot password.            |
| `identifier`                                  | email or username            | `username` asks for a username field that also accepts an email.      |
| `providers / onProvider`                      | {id, label, icon}[] / fn(id) | Sign-on buttons above the form; they share its pending and error state. |
| `providerLayout / dividerLabel`               | grid or stack / string       | Provider buttons side by side or stacked, and the divider copy.       |
| `showPasswordLabel / hidePasswordLabel` | string | Reveal-button names; default `Show password` / `Hide password`. |
| `children`                                    | ReactNode                    | Extra fields before submit, such as keep me signed in or terms.       |
| `pendingLabel`                                | string                       | Submit text while `onSubmit` is pending. Defaults per mode.           |

Email identifiers use `EmailInput`, so they inherit the default smooth caret and single-address pattern validation. Username identifiers remain text inputs; masked passwords retain the native caret. A surrounding `InputConfigProvider caretMode='native'` opts the form out of smooth mode.

## Ownership and verification

The host supplies password policy (`passwordMinLength` and matching help text), data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. Gaudi owns layout, semantics and local interaction. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

components.readme:
# Dashboard

Full dashboards for blogs and applications, composed from Stat Cards, Charts, DataTable, FilterBar, Tabs, Progress and the other Core parts. Dashboard adds only the two pieces those owners don't cover: a grid that reflows by its own width, and a period toolbar.

## Usage

```jsx
import { DashboardGrid, DashboardPanel, DashboardToolbar, dashboardSpan } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Dashboard';
import { StatCard } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/StatCard';
import { AreaChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';
import DataTable from '@gaudi/design-system/core/DataTable';

<DashboardToolbar defaultPeriod='30d' defaultCompare onChange={(period) => load(period)} />
<DashboardGrid label='Shop revenue'>
  <StatCard label='Revenue' value='$184,950' delta='+11.6%' deltaDirection='up' deltaTone='success' className={dashboardSpan(3)} />
  <DashboardPanel title='Revenue by product line' span={8}>
    <AreaChart framed={false} data={revenue} stacked series={series} />
  </DashboardPanel>
  <DashboardPanel title='Order queue' span={12}>
    <DataTable caption='Order queue' rows={orders} columns={columns} sortable searchable exportable />
  </DashboardPanel>
</DashboardGrid>
```

## API

| Prop / export | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `DashboardGrid` | A container-query grid: one column when narrow, six from 42rem and twelve from 64rem of its own width, so it fits a page, a split view or a sidebar. `label` names the region. |
| `DashboardPanel` | A titled panel on the Core Card. `span` (of twelve), `spanMd` (of six) and `rowSpan` place it; `title`, `description`, `action`, `toolbar` and `footer` fill it. `scroll` (`x`, `y`, `both`) with `scrollLabel` and `maxHeight` makes the body a focusable scroll region. |
| `dashboardSpan(span, spanMd, rowSpan)` | Placement classes for any grid child, such as a StatCard. |
| `DashboardToolbar` | Period presets, a custom range from the Calendar, a compare switch and a slot for actions. `period`, `range` and `compare` are each controlled or uncontrolled; `onChange` receives `{ period, from, to, days, previous, compare }`. |
| `resolveDashboardPeriod(period, { today, range, periods })` | The dates a period covers and the equally long period before it. |
| `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_PERIODS` / `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_LABELS` | The 7d, 30d, 90d and 12m presets and the English copy. |

Charts inside a panel usually pass `framed={false}` so the panel supplies the border and title. Tables keep their own scroll region; give a panel `scroll` only for custom content such as a timesheet.

## Accessibility

The grid and panels are named regions, and panel titles are headings. A scrolling panel body is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it. The presets are a single-choice group, the custom range opens in a popover, and the toolbar announces the active range, with its comparison, politely when it changes.

components.readme:
# Forms

Form behaviour for blogs and applications on top of the Core Field parts: validation with accessible errors, a summary
that takes focus after a failed submit, values you edit in place and live character counts. Layout stays with
`FieldGroup` and `Field` (use `orientation='responsive'` for label-control rows); Forms adds behaviour, not wrappers.

```jsx
import { FormErrorSummary, useFormValidation, validators } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Forms';
import { FieldError, FieldGroup, FieldLabel, FieldRoot as Field } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Field';
import { EmailInput } from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Input';

const form = useFormValidation({
  initialValues: { email: '' },
  rules: { email: [validators.required('Enter your email address.'), validators.email()] }
});

<form noValidate onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(subscribe)}>
  <FormErrorSummary form={form} labels={{ email: 'Email' }} />
  <Field data-invalid={form.errors.email ? true : undefined}>
    <FieldLabel htmlFor={form.id('email')}>Email</FieldLabel>
    <EmailInput {...form.field('email')} />
    <FieldError id={form.errorId('email')}>{form.errors.email}</FieldError>
  </Field>
</form>
```

## API

| Prop / export                                        | Type                                      | Contract                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useFormValidation({ initialValues, rules, validateOn })` | hook                                  | Form state. `rules` maps a name to a validator or a list; `validateOn` is `blur` or `submit`. |
| `form.field(name, { describedBy })`                  | props                                     | `id`, `name`, `value`, `onChange`, `onBlur`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`.       |
| `form.id(name)` / `form.errorId(name)`               | string                                    | Control and error ids, also used by the summary links.                                    |
| `form.setValue` / `setValues` / `handleSubmit` / `reset` | functions                             | Update values, block invalid submits (`onValid(values)`), restore a state.                |
| `validators`                                         | required, email, minLength, maxLength, pattern, min, max | Message-returning checks; custom rules receive `(value, values)`.                |
| `FormErrorSummary`                                   | `form`, `labels`, `title`                 | After a failed submit, lists each error, takes focus and links to the control.            |
| `EditableField`                                      | `label`, `value`, `onSave`, `validate`, `format`, `renderControl` | Value with Edit; Enter saves, Escape cancels, a thrown save error keeps it open. |
| `CharacterCount`                                     | `value`, `max`, `id`                      | Remaining characters, announced politely near the limit.                                  |

## Accessibility

- Errors sit beside their control, are referenced by `aria-describedby` and set `aria-invalid`.
- Format validators pass on empty values, so optional fields stay optional; add `validators.required` when needed.
- `FormErrorSummary` is an alert that receives focus; each link moves focus to its field, or to the first control in a
  group such as a rating or a checkbox list.
- `EditableField` returns focus to its Edit button after Save, Cancel or Escape.

components.readme: # Hero A responsive marketing introduction, showcased in **Blocks → Marketing → Heroes**. ```jsx import { Hero } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Hero'; import Button from '@gaudi/design-system/core/Button'; Get started} media={} /> ``` `layout` supports `centered`, `split`, `editorial`, and `background`. Split and editorial layouts stack below a 48rem container width. With no media, split keeps a single content column. Slots accept existing Gaudi components; the block does not own navigation, forms, destinations, or product data. `eyebrow` places a short label, Badge, or mark above the heading without changing the section name. `children` adds supporting content below the actions. The section labels itself with its heading. Use `headingAs` to fit the document hierarchy. Supply decorative, non-interactive media for `background`; its opaque content panel keeps text readable in both themes. Images require descriptive alt text unless decorative. Button and Link provide the action semantics, focus, and keyboard behavior. For an animated hero, place the Hero inside a Gaudi background such as `Borealis` or `Grainient`, give the Hero `className='bg-transparent'`, and offer a pause control. Use the dark theme scope for dark effects so text keeps its contrast.

components.readme:
# Navigation

The site header block: brand, the primary `NavigationMenu` (site links plus a two-block Blog panel of categories and recent posts, or a Categories panel on the supplied blog route), search, the theme switch and, below `lg`, a phone sheet. `LayoutContainer` renders it from `menuProps`; render `Menu` directly in a custom shell inside a `SiteConfigProvider`.

```jsx
import { Menu } from '@gaudi/design-system';

<Menu blogLink={blogLink} categories={categories} posts={posts} projects={projects} publications={publications} tags={tags} />
```

| Prop | Type | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blogLink` | `{ href, title }` | Prepared destination that enables the blog panel and identifies its current route. |
| `categories` | `Array<{ id, href, title, description }>` | Prepared Blog panel, Categories panel and phone sheet destinations. |
| `posts` | `Array<{ id?, slug?, href, title, date }>` | The newest three become Recent posts; all are searchable. |
| `projects / publications / tags / thoughts` | `Array` | Command launcher search records. |
| `logo` | `ReactNode` | Replaces the default brand mark inside the home link. |

Site links come from SiteConfig `navigation.links` (`showInPath` / `hideInPath` filter them per route); the home link is named by the SiteConfig author or title.

The phone sheet and the brand mark are private parts. `MenuSearch`, the header's search entry, is exported for custom headers that open `Commander`. For the Blog panel on its own, compose `NavigationMenuDropdown` with `aside={<NavigationMenuAside … />}` (see Core/Navigation/NavigationMenu).

## Accessibility

One `Main navigation` landmark with real links; the current destination gets `aria-current="page"`. Panels open on click and close on Escape (focus returns to the trigger) or an outside click. The phone sheet is a named modal dialog that takes focus, isolates the page, closes on Escape or Close and returns focus to the menu button; searching from it closes the sheet before the launcher opens.

Supply `href` on searchable records as well as category and recent-post links. The header passes host navigation to Commander and does not construct content routes. Without `blogLink`, it renders the prepared primary links without a blog panel.

## Apple-style mega menu example

`Blocks/Navigation → Apple-style mega menu` composes the public `NavigationMenuRoot` parts with `Dialog`, `AccordionRoot`, `Button`, and `Icon`. Inspired by [Skiper 38](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper38), it uses a full-width desktop panel, large primary links, quieter secondary groups, a short stagger, and a blurred backdrop. Hover, click, arrow keys, Escape, and outside dismissal work; reduced motion removes transitions.

Below 1024px, a modal menu contains expandable sections and its own scroll region, returning focus to its opener when closed. The example contains the overlay within its preview; an application can portal to the document instead. Demo navigation updates local content and calls `onNavigate({ title, href })`; wire the supplied hrefs to application routes. Copyable source includes the example styles. This is a header recipe, not another public component or a change to `Menu`.

## Scroll-merging header example

`Blocks/Navigation → Scroll-merging header` follows [Skiper 57](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper57): a project breadcrumb row scrolls away while the section tabs move alongside the brand in one compact sticky header. It composes `ScrollArea`, `Tabs`, and `Breadcrumb` with `useScrollPosition`, `useElementSize`, and `usePrefersReducedMotion`. A single tab list retains selection and keyboard focus through the merge; narrow layouts scroll the tabs within the header. The measured row height keeps alignment correct at each spacing density.

The scroll demonstration is contained within its own workspace in Docs. Arrow keys, Home, and End navigate the local sample sections; `onSectionChange(value)` reports selection. The brand button returns the workspace to the top. Reduced motion uses the compact header throughout. Copyable source includes the styles and local sample data.

## Theme switch animation

The theme switch animates the change with a view transition. Set `data-theme-transition` on `<html>` to choose the style: `fade` (default crossfade), `circle` (the new theme grows from the toggle), `wipe` (sweeps down from the top), `blur` (a soft blurred crossfade) or `none`. Reduced motion and browsers without view transitions switch instantly.

components.readme:
# Screens

Full-screen frames for sign-in, sign-up and onboarding. `Screen` puts the main column (an AuthForm, Wizard or settings panel) beside an optional `aside` for imagery, customer quotes or logos, with `header` and `footer` bands. `ScreenTestimonial` rotates customer quotes in an aside. The catalogue also collects composed profile, settings, wizard, onboarding and auth screens built from AuthForm, Wizard and Core parts.

## Usage

```jsx
import { AuthForm } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/AuthForm';
import { Screen, ScreenTestimonial } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/Screens';

<Screen
  aside={<ScreenTestimonial quotes={quotes} rating={4.8} className='p-10' />}
  asideSide='start'
  header={<Logo />}
  footer={<LegalLinks />}
>
  <AuthForm onSubmit={signIn} />
</Screen>;
```

## API

| Prop / export                         | Type                              | Contract                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `aside`                               | ReactNode                         | Panel beside the main column; hidden below md so the form comes first.    |
| `asideSide`                           | start or end                      | Side of the aside from md up. The main column stays first in source.      |
| `asideClassName / className`          | string                            | Classes for the aside panel and the frame.                                |
| `header / footer`                     | ReactNode                         | Bands for a logo, account links, legal links or customer logos.           |
| `ScreenTestimonial.quotes`            | {quote, name, role, avatar?}[]    | Customer quotes; more than one rotates and shows named dots.              |
| `ScreenTestimonial.rating / interval` | number                            | Optional star rating and rotation delay (6000 ms by default).             |

## Ownership and verification

The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence; authentication and validation stay in AuthForm, Wizard and the consuming app. Rotation pauses on hover, focus and reduced motion. Examples document working behavior and states, with Storybook interaction/axe checks and a server-rendering contract test alongside the component.

components.readme:
# StatCard

Metric cards compose Core Card, Badge and IconTile. Applications supply the formatted values and their meaning.

```jsx
import { StatCard, StatDelta } from '@gaudi/design-system/blocks/StatCard';

<StatCard label='Failed runs' value='12' delta='−0.5%' deltaDirection='down' deltaTone='success' />
<StatDelta value='+0.00%' direction='flat' tone='neutral' />
```

`StatDelta` preserves `value` exactly, including its sign and zero. `direction` (`up`, `down`, `flat`) is optional and controls the icon and spoken direction. `tone` defaults to `neutral`; choose `accent`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `discovery` or `attention` explicitly. A lower value can be favorable or unfavorable depending on the metric.

`StatCard` passes `delta`, `deltaDirection` and `deltaTone` to its badge. The previous `invert` prop and automatic sign/color inference are removed; provide direction and tone explicitly when migrating. Card `tone` independently controls its optional icon and tinted background. Other slots are `label`, `value`, `icon`, `action`, `description`, `footer` and `children`; `variant` is `default`, `tinted` or `inverse`.

`valueMotion='reel'` animates a text or number `value` with [ReelText](../../animations/ReelText/README.md): its digits spin into each new figure, for example when a range switch in `action` changes the period. Other values render unchanged, and reduced motion swaps the figure instantly.

`StatMeter` accepts `segments` with `label`, numeric `value` and optional `tone`, plus `label` and `formatValue`. Its decorative bar has a text legend for assistive technology even when `showLegend={false}` visually hides it.

A changed sequence of step IDs resets the flow and discards stale results. ## Usage ```jsx const [name, setName] = useState(''); Boolean(name.trim())} onComplete={saveCollection} > {(step) => step === 0 ? ( setName(e.target.value)} /> ) : (

{name}

) } ; ``` ## API | Prop / export | Type | Contract | | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `steps` | {id, label, description?}[] | Ordered stable stage IDs; changing the sequence resets the flow. | | `children` | function(index) | Stage content. Keep form values above Wizard. | | `validateStep` | function(index) => boolean or Promise | False prevents progress. All preceding stages are rechecked before advance/completion. | | `onComplete` | function() => void or Promise | Required host action; rejection retains the form for retry. | | `title / description` | ReactNode | Flow context. | | `completionTitle / completionDescription` | ReactNode | Success content after the callback resolves. | | `labels / completeLabel / errorMessage / validationMessage` | object / string | Localized action and state copy. | | `indicator` | steps, progress, dots or vertical | Numbered steps, a progress bar, compact dots or a vertical list beside the form. | | `aside` | ReactNode or function(index, complete) | A live summary or preview beside the form. | | `navigable` | boolean | Completed steps become buttons that go back; steps ahead stay behind validation. | | `completion` | ReactNode | Replaces the default finished state, for example a celebration with next actions. | ## Ownership and verification The host supplies data, translations, network calls, permissions and persistence. components.readme:
# ChatAgentMark

The assistant’s mark. By default each agent gets a Gaudí-inspired motif (trencadís mosaic, basilica spires, a wrought-iron spiral, a rose window, the palmetto gate, the flower paving tile, a twisted chimney, a sun medallion or the nativity star) glazed in one of eight tile hues. The seed, or the name, picks both, so an agent keeps the same mark everywhere. An icon, image or monogram can sit on a token tile instead, and an optional activity badge shows what the agent is doing.

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatAgentMark } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatAgentMark name='Gaudi' state='thinking' />
<ChatAgentMark name='Research agent' seed='agent_42' size='sm' decorative />
<ChatAgentMark name='Gaudi' motif='trencadis' hue='teal' size='xl' />
<ChatAgentMark name='Research agent' icon='Search' tone='discovery' size='sm' decorative />
```

## API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The accessible name, the monogram source and the default seed. |
| `seed` | A stable id (for example the agent id) that picks the motif and hue. |
| `motif` / `hue` | Pin a motif (`agentMotifs`) or a glaze (`agentHues`); `auto` derives them from the seed. |
| `icon` / `image` / `monogram` | Show these on a `tone` tile instead of a motif. |
| `size` / `tone` | xs to xl; tone (accent, discovery, neutral, solid) applies to icon, image and monogram tiles. |
| `state` | Adds an ChatActivityIndicator badge. |
| `resolveAgentMark(seed)` | Returns the `{ motif, hue }` a seed resolves to, for legends. |
| `decorative` | Hides the mark when a visible name sits beside it. |

## Accessibility

The mark is `role="img"` with the agent’s name unless `decorative`. Its badge names the state for screen readers; the tile is fixed geometry at every density.

components.readme:
# ChatFileExplorer

A conversation’s shared files, uploads, and agent outputs, composed from Core Tree, Input, Button, Badge, Alert, EmptyState, Skeleton, and ChatAgentMark. Hosts supply the file map and own loading, permissions, preview content, and downloads.

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatFileExplorer } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

const files = {
  root: { name: 'Files', children: ['shared', 'researcher'] },
  shared: { name: 'Shared', children: ['brief'] },
  brief: {
    name: 'launch-brief.md', typeLabel: 'MD', sizeLabel: '4.2 KB',
    modifiedLabel: 'Edited 10:40', modifiedAt: '2026-10-03T10:40:00Z',
    downloadUrl: '/files/launch-brief.md'
  },
  researcher: {
    name: 'Researcher', agent: { name: 'Researcher', seed: 'research-agent' },
    children: ['notes']
  },
  notes: { name: 'interview-notes.md', meta: '6 sources' }
};

<ChatFileExplorer
  items={files}
  defaultExpanded={['shared', 'researcher']}
  selectedId={selectedId}
  onSelect={(id, file) => setSelectedId(id)}
  onPreview={(id, file) => openPreview(file)}
  onRefresh={reloadFiles}
/>
```

## Data

`items` remains a flat map by stable string ID. `rootId` identifies its hidden root; `children` defines folder hierarchy and order. Group roots for shared files, uploads, and agents are ordinary folders, so the component needs no second grouping API.

| Item field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | File or folder name. Long names truncate with a full-name title. |
| `children?` | Child IDs; even an empty array identifies a folder. |
| `meta?` | Existing short supplementary text, retained for compatibility. |
| `typeLabel?` | Prepared file type. Defaults to the filename extension; an empty string hides it. |
| `sizeLabel?` | Prepared size such as `18 KB`; Gaudi does not reformat it. |
| `modifiedLabel?` / `modifiedAt?` | Prepared time text and optional machine-readable `dateTime`. No polling or relative-time engine. |
| `downloadUrl?` / `downloadName?` | Host-supplied site-relative, HTTP(S), or blob destination and optional saved filename. Unsafe protocols produce no action. |
| `canPreview?` | Set false to omit a file’s explicit Preview action; file selection still works. |
| `agent?` | ChatAgentMark identity props such as `{ name, seed, motif, hue, state }`, used on folders. |

Missing child IDs and repeated/cyclic references are omitted. Input objects are not mutated. Counts cover reachable files; empty folders remain visible and expandable without increasing the file count.

## Props

| Prop | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `items` / `rootId='root'` | Prepared map and hidden root ID; omitted data shows an empty state. |
| `defaultExpanded=[]` | Normal folder expansion at mount. Core Tree owns subsequent expansion. |
| `selectedId` / `defaultSelectedId=null` | Controlled or initial selected file. Folder focus does not replace file selection. |
| `onSelect(id, item)` | Called on file activation, including repeat activation. Receives the original host item. |
| `onPreview(id, item)` | Adds explicit Preview actions. Preview also selects the file. |
| `searchable=true` | Local search across names, type/size/modified labels, supplementary metadata, and agent names. Matches keep ancestor folders; matching a folder shows its descendants. Clearing search restores normal expansion. |
| `loading` / `refreshing` | Announces busy state and disables refresh/retry. With existing files, keeps the list visible; without them, shows Skeleton rows. |
| `error` / `onRetry` | Error text and retry callback. Existing files remain visible. Retry falls back to `onRefresh` when supplied. |
| `onRefresh` / `actions` | Optional header refresh button and host action slot. |
| `label='Files'` / `className` | Region/tree name and outer layout classes. Place in a bounded flex panel to make its tree scroll internally. |
| `labels` | Overrides `search`, `clearSearch`, `preview`, `download`, `refresh`, `loading`, `errorTitle`, `retry`, `emptyTitle`, `emptyDescription`, `noResultsTitle`, and `noResultsDescription`. |

Downloads use real native anchors with `download`; the host supplies a valid URL and cross-origin download headers where needed. No fetch, file content, permission, polling, or preview implementation is built in.

## Accessibility

Core Tree provides arrows, folder expansion, focus, and Enter activation. Selection is single-file and exposed with `aria-selected`. Preview/download actions are separate controls, available in the focused row’s tab sequence; their keys do not activate the tree row. Search is labelled, updates announce match counts, errors use Alert, and loading announces its state. File actions stay visible for touch users. Rows use non-button treeitems to avoid nested interactive buttons.

When a host update removes the focused row, focus moves to a remaining visible row. An empty replacement focuses the first available panel control, or the labelled panel itself. Updates leave focus in Search and outside controls alone.

## Examples

- **Playground:** grouped shared/upload/agent files, nested search, metadata, preview, genuine local downloads, and refresh.
- **Controlled selection:** host-selected files and a header action.
- **Live file updates:** focus recovery when the host replaces or clears the file map.
- **Empty folders:** folder navigation and search before any files exist.
- **Loading**, **Error and retry**, **Empty:** initial and recovery states.

components.readme:
# ChatInput

The composer for a chat: `ChatPromptComposer` (a multi-line prompt on the core InputGroup with mentions, commands, attachments and send or stop), `ChatPromptQueue` for messages waiting while a reply streams, and `ChatModelSelect` for the model and effort. The assistant toolbar adds `ChatPromptAttachMenu` (the `+` menu), `ChatPromptSettings` (effort and option switches), `ChatContextMeter` (prepared context usage, breakdown and cost). Applications supply model/provider catalogues and usage policy; richer sample data lives only in story fixtures.

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatEffortSlider, ChatModelSelect, ChatPromptComposer, ChatPromptQueue } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatPromptQueue items={queue} onEdit={edit} onRemove={remove} onSendNow={sendNow} onMove={move} />
<ChatPromptComposer
  status={streaming ? 'streaming' : 'ready'}
  mentions={people}
  commands={commands}
  onSubmit={(text, { queued }) => (queued ? enqueue(text) : send(text))}
  onStop={stop}
  leftControls={<ChatModelSelect searchable providers={providers} models={models} value={model} onValueChange={setModel}><ChatEffortSlider value={effort} onValueChange={setEffort} compact /></ChatModelSelect>}
/>
```

### Assistant composer

```jsx
import { ChatContextMeter, ChatModelSelect, ChatPromptAttachMenu, ChatPromptComposer, ChatPromptSettings } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatPromptComposer
  variant='card'
  labels={{ placeholder: 'Ask anything...' }}
  onSubmit={send}
  leftControls={
    <>
      <ChatPromptAttachMenu onAttach={addFiles} />
      <ChatModelSelect searchable models={models} providers={providers} value={model} onValueChange={setModel} />
    </>
  }
  rightControls={
    <>
      <ChatPromptSettings options={[{ value: 'web', label: 'Web search', icon: 'Globe' }]} values={options} onValuesChange={setOptions} effort={effort} onEffortChange={setEffort} />
      <ChatContextMeter usedTokens={usedTokens} maxTokens={contextLimit} breakdown={breakdown} cost={formattedCost} tone={contextTone} message={contextMessage} />
    </>
  }
  voice={({ insert }) => <MicButton onTranscript={insert} />}
/>
```

### Expanding tool icons

`ChatPromptToggle` composes the shared Toggle, Tooltip and AnimatedIcon for tools such as Search or Think. Hover animates the icon and shows a tooltip without moving adjacent controls. Keyboard focus or selection expands the label; selected tools retain their label and accent. Its accessible name stays constant and `aria-pressed` reports the selection. Prefer short labels; longer labels truncate within the available width and remain available through the tooltip and accessible name. The icon respects reduced motion, and touch targets are at least 44px. Tool selection belongs to the host and does not start a search or request.

```jsx
import { ChatPromptComposer, ChatPromptToggle } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat/ChatInput';

<ChatPromptComposer
  variant='card'
  onSubmit={send}
  leftControls={
    <ChatPromptToggle icon='Globe' label='Search' pressed={search} onPressedChange={setSearch} />
  }
/>
```

The `card` variant uses a muted writing area, an inset toolbar and matched control heights; it follows Gaudi's radius and spacing tokens in both themes. The attachment `+` rotates while its menu is open. The **Expanding tools** story demonstrates these interactions, inspired by [Skiper AI Input 001](https://skiper-ui.com/v1/skiper81), with an independent implementation using Gaudi primitives.

### Control placement

`leftControls` and `rightControls` accept any composition of the existing controls. Their child order sets the visual and keyboard order. Put `ChatPromptAttachMenu`, `ChatModelSelect`, `ChatPromptSettings`, `ChatContextMeter`, or custom buttons in either slot; both groups wrap to fit narrow containers. Left/right follow the reading direction, so they mirror in RTL.

The built-in `onAttach` button remains in the left group. For configurable attachment placement, use `ChatPromptAttachMenu` in either slot. Send, stop and the empty-prompt voice action stay together after the right controls.

Existing `toolbar` and `actions` remain aliases for the left and right slots. An explicit new slot takes precedence; `null` clears that slot without rendering its legacy alias. These slots work in both `default` and `card` variants.

Storybook’s **Assistant composer** example provides independent left/right controls for attachments, model, settings and context, with matching copyable source. **Split controls** and **All controls on the right** show common arrangements.

### Mixed attachments

`attachments` accepts `{ id, name, type?, mediaType?, fileType?, size?, kind?, previewUrl? }`. The composer reuses Core `AttachmentMedia`: audio and video get distinct icons, images use a supplied `previewUrl`, and `kind='link'` uses a globe. Without a thumbnail, or if it cannot load, the file-type icon remains. Supply image thumbnails or video posters explicitly; the component does not fetch the original media or create object URLs. The host owns those URLs and their cleanup.

The **Mixed attachments: compact media pills** story shows image, PDF, audio, video and link attachments, removal, reset and submission. `onSubmit` receives the same attachment objects in its second argument; `onRemoveAttachment(id)` keeps the tray controlled by the host.

## API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatPromptComposer` | `@` anywhere or `/` at the start opens `mentions` or `commands`; Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line; `status` streaming shows Stop and reports `{ queued: true }`; `leftControls`, `rightControls`, `footer`, `attachments` and `onAttach` fill the frame. |
| `ChatPromptComposer` `leftControls` / `rightControls` | ReactNode slots for independently arranged control groups; both wrap. New props override legacy `toolbar` / `actions`; `null` clears a slot. Built-in send/stop/voice remain after the right slot. |
| `ChatPromptQueue` | Waiting messages `{ id, text }`: edit in place, send now, remove, or move with Alt+Arrow. |
| `ChatPromptToggle` | `icon` is an icon registry name; `label` supplies the visible and accessible name. `pressed` / `defaultPressed` / `onPressedChange` follow the shared Toggle's controlled/uncontrolled contract; `disabled` prevents changes. Use it in either control slot. Hosts must pass their disabled/read-only policy to supplied slot controls. |
| `ChatModelSelect` | `models` `{ value, label, description?, details?, badge?, badgeTone?, icon? }` with `value` / `onValueChange`; `icon` is a brand mark, `details` short facts under the name; `variant` / `size` style the trigger (outline in a page header), `icon={false}` drops the default sparkle; `disabled` disables the trigger; `children` add a footer such as a ChatEffortSlider; a footer uses a popover containing a model list and separate controls. |
| `ChatModelSelect` (catalogue) | Models with a `provider` group under its name and mark (host-supplied `providers`, or the provider ID when absent); `contextWindow`, `speed` (`fast`, `balanced`, `slow`), `cost` (1 to 4) and `capabilities` (`vision`, `reasoning`, `tools`, `web`, `files`, `audio`, `code`, `image`) show under the name. `searchable` opens a command list with a search field instead of a menu. |
| `ChatPromptComposer` `variant` / `voice` | `card` is the roomier composer with a one-line prompt that grows; `voice` (element or `({ value, setValue, insert, disabled }) => element`) holds the send slot while the prompt is empty. |
| `ChatPromptAttachMenu` | `items` `{ value, label, icon?, description?, shortcut?, accept?, capture?, multiple?, separator? }`; items with `accept` open the file picker and call `onAttach(files, item)`, others call `onSelect(item)`. |
| `ChatPromptSettings` | `effort` / `onEffortChange` (a ChatEffortSlider, `effortLevels` for your own steps) and switches for `options` with `values` / `defaultValues` / `onValuesChange(values, changed)`; `children` add controls. |
| `ChatContextMeter` | `usedTokens`, `maxTokens`, optional `modelLabel`; prepared `breakdown` rows `{ id, label, value, detail? }`; prepared `cost` and `costLabel`; explicit `tone` (`accent`, `warning`, `danger`) and `message`. `formatTokens` defaults to exported `formatTokenCount`; `formatPercentage` formats the derived percentage. |
| `findPromptTrigger(text, caret)` | The mention or command being typed at the caret, or null. |

### Context data ownership

The meter only derives its percentage from `usedTokens` and `maxTokens`. It does not combine protocol token categories, calculate prices, choose warning thresholds or predict how a host handles a full context window. Supply formatted breakdown values and cost text unchanged, including zero. The host sets tone and any explanatory message.

The previous `usage`, `model`, `pricing`, `currency`, `warnAt` and `dangerAt` props and exported `estimateChatCost`, `chatModels` and `chatModelProviders` are removed. Move model/provider metadata and any billing calculation into the application. The Assistant composer story retains an illustrative catalogue and billing calculation in `stories/fixtures`.

## Accessibility

The prompt is a labelled combobox; suggestions are a listbox with the active option announced. Icon buttons (attach, send, stop, add to queue) have names, and every queue action names the message it acts on.

The model trigger names the current model. Searchable pickers and pickers with footer content use a dialog; searchable ones include a labelled search combobox. Without search, focus starts in the model list: arrow keys move and Enter selects, while Tab reaches the footer controls. Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Simple pickers without search or a footer retain menu keyboard behavior; options are grouped under provider headings, the current model is `aria-checked`, and capability icons and the cost scale have text alternatives. The options trigger lists the options that are on, and each switch is named. The context meter is a button named with the share used and the token counts; it opens the breakdown on press (not hover), so it works with touch and the keyboard, and the warning text appears in the breakdown as well as in colour. The `voice` slot only swaps while the prompt is empty, so focus stays in the prompt while typing.

# ChatMessage

One turn in a conversation: an avatar, a header with the sender and time, the content stack and a footer for status such as read or edited. A `ChatMessageGroup` runs several turns from one sender under one avatar.

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatBubble, ChatBubbleContent, ChatMessage, ChatMessageAvatar, ChatMessageContent, ChatMessageFooter } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessage align='end'>
  <ChatMessageAvatar><Avatar src={me.src} name={me.name} size='sm' alt='' /></ChatMessageAvatar>
  <ChatMessageContent>
    <ChatBubble align='end'><ChatBubbleContent>Moving the legend under the axis.</ChatBubbleContent></ChatBubble>
    <ChatMessageFooter>Read 10:42</ChatMessageFooter>
  </ChatMessageContent>
</ChatMessage>
```

## API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatMessage` | `align` start or end; the avatar flips with it. |
| `ChatMessageGroup` | Consecutive turns from one sender share an avatar. |
| `ChatMessageAvatar`, `ChatMessageHeader`, `ChatMessageContent`, `ChatMessageFooter` | Avatar column, sender and time, the content stack, and status. |

## Accessibility

Side alone is lost when a thread is read aloud: name the sender in a header or visually hidden text, and label reactions and icon-only actions.

components.readme:
# ChatMessageList

The conversation itself: `ChatMessageScroller` keeps a long thread anchored while new turns arrive, and `ChatMessageParts` renders each assistant turn from its parts (text, reasoning, tools, sources, files, data, errors and suggestions).

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatMessageParts, ChatMessageScroller, ChatMessageScrollerContent, ChatMessageScrollerItem, ChatMessageScrollerProvider, ChatMessageScrollerViewport } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessageScrollerProvider autoScroll>
  <ChatMessageScroller>
    <ChatMessageScrollerViewport aria-label='Conversation'>
      <ChatMessageScrollerContent>
        {turns.map((turn) => (
          <ChatMessageScrollerItem key={turn.id} scrollAnchor={turn.role === 'user'}>
            <ChatMessageParts parts={turn.parts} streaming={turn.streaming} />
          </ChatMessageScrollerItem>
        ))}
      </ChatMessageScrollerContent>
    </ChatMessageScrollerViewport>
  </ChatMessageScroller>
</ChatMessageScrollerProvider>
```

## API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatMessageScroller*` | Scroll container with anchoring, auto-scroll to the live edge, load-earlier without a jump, and `ChatMessageScrollerButton` to jump to the latest. |
| `ChatMessageScrollerItem.scrollAnchor` | Lifts a sent message near the top while a slice of the previous turn stays visible. |
| `ChatMessageParts.parts` | The parts of one assistant turn; unknown types are skipped so the host can render its own. |
| `ChatMessageParts.streaming` | Marks the turn as arriving: `aria-busy`, a live code fence and an open thinking trail. |
| `ChatMessageMarkdown` | Runtime markdown for reply text, with code through CodeBlock. |
| `ChatMessageCheckpoint` | A restore point between turns: `label`, `time` (string or Date), `onRestore` (confirmed in an alert dialog unless `confirm={false}`) and `restored`. |

## Parts model

An assistant turn is a list of parts, shaped like common AI SDK message parts but with no dependency on any SDK. `ChatMessageParts` renders them in order:

| Part | Renders as |
| --- | --- |
| `{ type: 'text', text }` | `ChatMessageMarkdown` |
| `{ type: 'reasoning', text?, steps?, duration? }` | `ChatMessageReasoning`: open while thinking, folds away a second after the answer starts unless the reader toggled it. Steps with a `label` (and `icon`, `description`, `text`, `results`, `images`) read as a chain of thought |
| `{ type: 'tool', name, status, input?, output?, error?, parts? }` | `ChatMessageTool`: statuses pending, running, done, failed or cancelled; input and output in `ChatMessageData` (a list or table, with a JSON view); nested calls as `parts`; a failed call opens with its error and a retry |
| `{ type: 'approval', name, description?, input?, state?, allowAlways?, output? }` | `ChatMessageToolApproval`: a tool waiting on the person; `onToolApproval(part, { approved, always })` answers it |
| `{ type: 'delegation', agent, status, instructions?, parts? }` | `ChatMessageDelegation`: work handed to another agent |
| `{ type: 'source', title, url?, kind?, site?, excerpt? }` | Gathered into one `ChatMessageSources` list; the text cites them as `[1]`, `[2]`… (or `[1, 3]` for several behind one pill) through `ChatMessageCitation` |
| `{ type: 'file', name, mediaType?, fileType?, previewUrl?, kind?, size?, description?, href? }`, `{ type: 'data', label?, value }` | Core `Attachment` with shared file media, and `ChatMessageData` |
| `{ type: 'error', title?, text? }`, `{ type: 'suggestions', items }` | Core `Alert` with retry, and labelled Core Button follow-ups (`onSuggestion(prompt, item)`) |

Add `ChatMessageFeedback` under a finished reply for copy, rating and regenerate.

### Delivered files

File parts reuse Core `AttachmentMedia`: supply `mediaType` (or `fileType`) for the MIME type, `previewUrl` for an explicit image or poster thumbnail, and `kind: 'link'` for a link icon. Without a preview, the shared media renderer chooses the file-type icon; failed thumbnails fall back to that icon. The file name remains visible beside the decorative media.

`onFileAction(action, part)` receives the original part for preview and host-managed download actions. An explicit `href` provides the download link instead. The host owns file retrieval and preview dialogs. When adapting upload metadata, preserve its MIME type before setting the part discriminator:

```jsx
<ChatMessageParts
  parts={files.map((file) => ({ ...file, type: 'file', mediaType: file.type }))}
  onFileAction={(action, file) => handleFileAction(action, file)}
/>
```

See **Chat / ChatMessage / Mixed attachments** for images, audio, video, documents, code, spreadsheets and links in a delivered reply.

### Checkpoints

A checkpoint sits between turns, outside `ChatMessageParts`, so the host decides where restore points fall and what restoring undoes.

```jsx
import { ChatMessageCheckpoint } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessageCheckpoint label='Before rewriting the intro' time={checkpoint.createdAt} onRestore={() => restore(checkpoint.id)} />
```

### Markdown

Replies arrive as plain markdown, a few tokens at a time, so `ChatMessageMarkdown` renders them at runtime instead of compiling them like MDX articles. It adds no markdown dependency:

- Code fences go through the CodeBlock `markdownFences` helper and `CodeBlock`; an unclosed fence keeps streaming.
- The text between fences uses a small grammar: headings (shifted below the conversation heading), paragraphs, ordered, unordered and task lists, quotes, rules, pipe tables, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links, bare URLs and numbered citations.
- Links render through the core `Link`.
- Unfinished markup while streaming stays as typed until its closing marker arrives.

Raw HTML is never interpreted.

```jsx
import { ChatMessage, ChatMessageContent, ChatMessageFeedback, ChatMessageParts } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessage>
  <ChatMessageContent>
    <ChatMessageParts parts={turn.parts} streaming={turn.streaming} onRetry={retry} onToolRetry={retryTool} />
    {turn.streaming ? null : <ChatMessageFeedback copyText={turn.text} onRegenerate={regenerate} />}
  </ChatMessageContent>
</ChatMessage>
```

## Accessibility

The thread scrolls inside a labelled region and never moves the page. While a reply streams, ChatMessageParts marks it `aria-busy`; announce the start and the end once in a polite status, never every token. A checkpoint is a group named by its label and time; its restore button is described by them, and the confirmation is an alert dialog that returns focus to the button.

Follow-up suggestions belong to `ChatMessageParts` as `{ type: 'suggestions', items }`, where items are strings or `{ id, label, prompt?, icon? }`. The renderer is private. Welcome prompts use Core Button directly alongside ChatPersona, EmptyState and ChatPromptComposer; see **Blocks / Chat / Welcome**. `ChatMessageSuggestions` is no longer a standalone package export.

components.readme:
# ChatPersona

The assistant’s presence in a voice conversation: an orb that rests, connects, listens, thinks, speaks, sleeps or shows an error. Eight renderers share one state model:

- `iridescent`: a thin-film sphere drawn by a small WebGL shader (no library), with a CSS gradient fallback.
- `mercury`: a polished metal sphere in CSS layers, with a rotating sheen and an energy-driven swell.
- `waveform`: a 2D canvas ring that ripples with the state or traces live time-domain samples.
- `activity`: a dotted sphere in SVG that turns, ripples, sweeps and swells.
- `circle`: a flat disc that breathes at rest, tightens with the level while listening, pulses while connecting or thinking, and swells with a glow while speaking.
- `bars`: five bars that rest as dots, follow the level while listening and speaking, and run a loading wave while connecting or thinking.
- `cloud`: a drifting WebGL sky with a milky horizon that draws in while listening and swells while speaking, with a CSS gradient fallback.
- `radial`: a WebGL pinwheel whose membrane ripples while listening and whose seams swing while speaking, with a CSS gradient fallback.

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatPersona, useAudioLevel } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatPersona name='Gaudi' state='listening' variant='iridescent' size='lg' />

// Live microphone level and waveform from a MediaStream
const { levelRef, waveformRef } = useAudioLevel(stream);
<ChatPersona name='Gaudi' state='listening' variant='waveform' levelRef={levelRef} waveformRef={waveformRef} />

// TTS playback level as a number
<ChatPersona name='Gaudi' state='speaking' variant='mercury' level={replyLevel} showLabel />
```

## API

| Prop | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | idle, connecting, listening, thinking, speaking, asleep or error (`personaStates`). |
| `variant` | iridescent, mercury, waveform, activity, circle, bars, cloud or radial (`personaVariants`). |
| `size` | xs 32, sm 48, md 96, lg 168, xl 240 (`personaSizes`), or a number of pixels. |
| `level` / `levelRef` | Live audio level, 0..1; without one each state keeps its own rhythm. |
| `waveformRef` | Time-domain samples (Uint8Array centred on 128) for the waveform ring. |
| `speed` / `active` | Animation multiplier (0 pauses); `active` defaults to true unless asleep. |
| `name` / `labels` / `showLabel` | Accessible name, copy per state and a visible state label. |
| `announce` / `decorative` | Polite status announcements (default on); hide everything when nearby text names the state. |
| `colorFrom` / `colorTo` | Hex overrides; by default the orb reads `--ds-voice-<variant>-from/to`, which point at colour tokens. |

## Accessibility

The orb is `role="img"` named “Gaudi: Listening”, and a polite status announces each change of state once. The state never depends on motion: the still frame differs per state and `showLabel` adds text. Animation runs only while the orb is on screen and the tab is visible, stops when asleep, and stops entirely (a still frame) for readers who prefer reduced motion.

## Attribution

The renderers adapt three MIT-licensed projects; their notices are kept in `orbs/LICENSE`.

- [VoiceOrbs](https://voiceorbs.vercel.app) ([amunozdev/voiceorbs](https://github.com/amunozdev/voiceorbs)) by Alexis Munoz, pinned at `339ab42d98f6c4ffa03709ffa71f9f6965a2171a`: the iridescent, mercury and waveform renderers and the shared orb model. Gaudi changes: JavaScript, Gaudi colour tokens, reduced-motion and off-screen pausing through Gaudi hooks, no microphone or audio fetching inside the orbs, and Mercury drawn with CSS instead of the [Paper Shaders](https://github.com/paper-design/shaders) library so no dependency is added.
- [Thinking Orbs](https://libraries.dev/orbs) ([Jakubantalik/Libraries.dev](https://github.com/Jakubantalik/Libraries.dev)) by Jakub Antalik, pinned at `0d448879917f92c2b9f2773c1f91054f4c83dae5`: the activity renderer's dotted sphere (a Fibonacci lattice on a turning, tilted sphere, shaded by depth), rewritten in SVG with Gaudi's voice states.
- [orb-ui](https://orb-ui.com) ([exprmntl/orb-ui](https://github.com/exprmntl/orb-ui)) by Alexander Chen, version 0.9.0 pinned at `0e78ad509e1b3a48013fb810eb25b130c355115d`: the circle, bars, cloud and radial styles. Only the visual themes are adapted; orb-ui's provider adapters, launch button and call controls are not included. Gaudi changes: palettes derived from `--ds-voice-<variant>-from/to` tokens, the asleep state, still frames for reduced motion, off-screen pausing, and the shared frame loop.

components.readme:
# ChatPlanPanel

The assistant’s plan for the current request: steps with status, owners and todos, a count of finished steps and a progress bar. It collapses to that summary.

## Usage

```jsx

<ChatPlan title='Plan' steps={[
```

components.readme:
# ChatReasoning

The thinking trail before an answer. While the model thinks, the label shimmers "Thinking…" and the trail stays open; a second after the answer starts it folds into "Thought for 6s", unless the reader opened or closed it. With detailed steps it becomes a chain of thought: search, read, analyse and decide, each with a status, details, search results and image thumbnails.

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatMessageReasoning, ChatMessageReasoningImage, ChatMessageReasoningResults, ChatMessageReasoningStep } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessageReasoning streaming={thinking}>
  <ChatMessageReasoningStep status='done'>Read the draft</ChatMessageReasoningStep>
  <ChatMessageReasoningStep status='running'>Suggest a tighter opening</ChatMessageReasoningStep>
</ChatMessageReasoning>

<ChatMessageReasoning streaming={thinking} variant='steps'>
  <ChatMessageReasoningStep status='done' icon='Search' label='Searched the web' meta='4 results'>
    <ChatMessageReasoningResults results={results} />
  </ChatMessageReasoningStep>
  <ChatMessageReasoningStep status='running' icon='Image' label='Comparing cover images'>
    <ChatMessageReasoningImage src={cover} alt='The current cover: a train window at dusk' caption='Current cover' />
  </ChatMessageReasoningStep>
  <ChatMessageReasoningStep status='pending' icon='Lightbulb' label='Recommend a headline' />
</ChatMessageReasoning>
```

## API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `streaming` | Opens the trail with a shimmering "Thinking…" label; it opens again whenever thinking restarts. |
| `duration` | Seconds spent; measured from the start to the end of `streaming` when omitted. |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | Disclosure state; the reader's choice wins over the automatic fold. |
| `variant` | `trail` (a quoted trail) or `steps` (detailed steps draw their own rail). |
| `thinkingLabel` / `label` / `autoCloseDelay` | The streaming label, a fixed label, and the fold delay in ms (default 1000). |
| `ChatMessageReasoningStep` | `status` from the shared vocabulary. Children alone make a plain step; `label` makes a detailed one with `icon`, `description`, `meta` and children as details that open from the label (the running step starts open). |
| `ChatMessageReasoningResults` | `results` as link chips with favicons; `max` shows the first few and "+n more". |
| `ChatMessageReasoningImage` | `src`, `alt` and `caption` for an image the step looked at. |
| `useReasoningDisclosure` | The same open-then-fold behaviour for a custom trigger. |

## Accessibility

The trail and every detailed step are disclosure buttons with `aria-expanded`. A step's status is spoken after its label ("Searched the web, Done"), never left to colour or the icon. The shimmer is real text and holds still for readers who reduce motion. Give thumbnails an `alt` that says what the model looked at.
