components.readme:
# ChatTool

One tool call the assistant made: its name and status, the input and output as readable data with a JSON view, nested calls, and an error with a retry. `ChatMessageToolApproval` is the call that waits for the person: what the tool wants to do, Approve or Deny (optionally "always allow"), then approved, denied or executed.

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatMessageTool, ChatMessageToolApproval } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMessageTool name='schedule_newsletter' status={status} input={input} output={output} error={error} onRetry={retry}>
  {nestedCalls}
</ChatMessageTool>

<ChatMessageToolApproval
  name='publish_post'
  description='Publish the draft to the blog and email subscribers'
  input={{ slug: 'local-first-drafts', notify: 4180 }}
  allowAlways
  state={state}
  onStateChange={setState}
  onApprove={({ always }) => run({ always })}
  onDeny={cancel}
>
  {state === 'executed' ? <ChatMessageData value={result} /> : null}
</ChatMessageToolApproval>
```

## API

| Prop / part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | pending, running, done, failed or cancelled; `awaiting` and `denied` for approvals. |
| `input` / `output` / `error` | Shown with ChatMessageData; a failed call opens on its own with the error. |
| `onRetry` | Adds a retry to a failed call. |
| `ChatMessageData` | `value` read as a list or table, with a JSON view; `label` names it. Keys retain their supplied casing and numbers are not localized implicitly. Pass prepared strings when formatting is needed. |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.state` | `requested`, `approved`, `denied` or `executed`; uncontrolled it follows the person's choice (`defaultState`, `onStateChange`). |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.onApprove` / `onDeny` | The decision; `onApprove` receives `{ always }`. |
| `ChatMessageToolApproval.allowAlways` / `reason` / `labels` | Offer "always allow", explain a denial, and replace any copy. Children are the result once `executed`. |

## Accessibility

The tool header is a disclosure button naming the tool and its status. Errors are alerts. The JSON view is a labelled toggle. An approval is a group named by its question; Approve and Deny are plain buttons, and after a decision focus moves to the outcome, which is also a status message.

components.readme:
# ChatVoice

Building blocks for talking to an assistant: dictate a prompt, pick the microphone, pick the voice that answers and play the spoken reply. They pair with ChatPersona for a full voice mode.

- `ChatSpeechInput`: a mic button for the composer’s mic slot, with idle, listening and processing states and a ring that follows the input level.
- `ChatMicSelector`: the input device picker, with permission, refresh and a test level meter.
- `ChatVoiceSelector`: a data-driven list of TTS voices with tags and sample playback.
- `ChatAudioPlayer`: a compact player for voice messages and TTS replies.
- Helpers: `useAudioLevel(stream)`, `useAudioInputs()`, `voiceSupport()`, `getSpeechRecognition()`, `computePeaks()`, `formatAudioTime()`.

## Usage

```jsx
import { ChatAudioPlayer, ChatMicSelector, ChatPromptComposer, ChatSpeechInput, ChatVoiceSelector } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatMicSelector value={deviceId} onValueChange={setDeviceId} />
<ChatSpeechInput
  deviceId={deviceId}
  onInterim={setDraftPreview}
  onTranscript={(text) => setDraft((draft) => `${draft} ${text}`.trim())}
  onAudio={(blob) => transcribe(blob)} // Firefox and Safari: return the transcript
/>
<ChatVoiceSelector voices={voices} groupBy='provider' value={voice} onValueChange={setVoice} onPreview={speakSample} />
<ChatAudioPlayer src={reply.audioUrl} title='Reply' peaks={reply.peaks} download='reply.mp3' />
```

The host supplies its available `voices`. The former `exampleVoices` package export now lives only in `stories/fixtures/exampleVoices.js` for the Voice mode demo.

## API

| Component | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatSpeechInput` | `onTranscript(text, { final })`, `onInterim(text)`, `onAudio(blob) => transcript?`, `onStateChange`, `onError(kind)`, `onLevel(level)`; `mode` auto, speech or recorder; `lang`, `deviceId`, `showLevel`, `labels`, plus Button `size` / `variant`. |
| `ChatMicSelector` | `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange(deviceId, device)`, `meter` (a Test button and level meter), `autoRequest`, `labels`. |
| `ChatVoiceSelector` | `voices` (`{ id, name, provider?, gender?, accent?, age?, style?, description?, previewUrl? }`), `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange(id, voice)`, `onPreview(voice, { signal })`, `groupBy`, `searchable`, `labels`. |
| `ChatAudioPlayer` | `src`, `title`, `peaks` (0..1), `duration`, `speeds`, `download` (true or a file name), `autoPlay`, `onPlay` / `onPause` / `onEnded`, `labels`. |
| `useAudioLevel(stream, { onLevel })` | `{ levelRef, waveformRef }` for ChatPersona, updated every frame without re-rendering. |
| `useAudioInputs({ autoRequest })` | `{ devices, permission, error, refresh, request }`. |

All browser APIs (SpeechRecognition, MediaRecorder, getUserMedia, enumerateDevices, AudioContext, Audio) are read lazily and guarded, so every part renders on the server; ChatSpeechInput stays disabled until the browser reports what it supports. Disabling it or changing `mode`, `deviceId` or `lang` cancels the current capture and ignores pending transcription results. Unmounting releases the microphone.

## Accessibility

ChatSpeechInput is a real button with `aria-pressed` while listening; Escape stops it; a polite status announces listening, transcribing and stopped, and a disabled button explains why through `aria-describedby`. ChatMicSelector names its select, explains a blocked permission with a retry, and only opens the microphone for an explicit test. ChatVoiceSelector is a fieldset of Core RadioGroup controls (arrow keys move the choice) with separate, named sample buttons. ChatAudioPlayer’s scrubber is a slider that reads time (“0:12 of 0:45”) and moves with the arrow keys, Page Up / Page Down, Home and End. Motion (the level ring, the meter, spinners) is not the only signal, and calms down for reduced motion.

components.readme:
# ChatWorkspace

A context panel for the agents and files around a conversation. An agent's **View files** action opens its folder in `ChatFileExplorer`; **All files** restores the complete hierarchy. `ChatShell` owns responsive placement and mobile sheets.

```jsx
import { ChatWorkspace } from '@gaudi/design-system/chat';

<ChatWorkspace
  agents={[{ id: 'research', name: 'Research', state: 'thinking', description: 'Checking sources', fileRootId: 'research-files' }]}
  fileExplorerProps={{ items, defaultExpanded: ['shared'], selectedId, onSelect, onPreview, onRefresh }}
/>
```

## API

| Prop | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `agents` | `{ id, name, description?, state?, labels?, fileRootId? }[]`. Stable opaque IDs determine each `ChatAgentMark`. `state` and `labels` use `ChatActivityIndicator`. |
| `fileExplorerProps` | The existing `ChatFileExplorer` props, including `items`, selection, search, actions and recovery states. No second file schema. |
| `view / defaultView / onViewChange` | Controlled or local `files` / `agents` tab. Defaults to `files`. |
| `agentId / defaultAgentId / onAgentChange` | Controlled or local agent scope; `null` means all files. The agent must point to an existing folder, including an empty one. |
| `title / description / actions` | Panel heading, optional supporting text and header actions. |
| `labels` | Override `files`, `agents`, `allFiles`, `viewFiles`, `noAgents`, `noAgentsDescription`, `noAgentFiles`. |
| `className` | Layout integration. The panel has no fixed height or overlay behavior. |

Scope changes reset the explorer's local search and expansion. A missing agent or removed folder falls back to the full tree. The host supplies preview content and file IO through the explorer callbacks. Keep agent permissions, task orchestration and fetching in the application.

When using `ChatShell.details`, control `view`, `agentId` and `fileExplorerProps.selectedId` from the host so the desktop panel and mobile sheet share the current selection. See **Blocks / Chat / Workspace context: agents, files and preview** for a complete example.

## Accessibility

Core Tabs provides tab keyboard navigation. Agent identity and activity have text equivalents. Choosing an agent's files or returning to all files focuses the Files tab; Core Tree owns the explorer's keyboard interaction. Empty agent/file states are explicit.

# AreaChart

Filled areas per series over categories, stacked into a total or overlapping from zero.

[Open the docs](http://localhost:6007/?path=/docs/charts-areachart--docs) for the Playground and detailed examples, each with its complete JSX.

## Usage

```jsx
import { AreaChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<AreaChart title='Readers by device' ariaLabel='Daily readers by device' data={days} series={devices} stacked showLegend />
```

Import from `@gaudi/design-system/charts` or `@gaudi/design-system/charts/AreaChart`. Charts are not exported from the root entry, so pages without a chart never load Recharts. In an article, render the same chart through MDX/Chart.

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `xKey / yKey` | string | label / value | Category field and the single value field when series is omitted. |
| `series` | Array<{ key, label?, dashed? }> | from yKey | Value fields drawn as series, in order; a dashed series reads as a projection or target. |
| `stacked` | boolean | false | Stack the areas into a total. |
| `curve` | monotone \| linear \| step | monotone | Area interpolation. |
| `references / annotations` | Array<{ x?, y?, label, tone? }> | — | Labelled guide lines and point notes. |
| `showGrid / showLegend / showTooltip` | boolean | true / false / true | Presentation. |
| `colors` | string[] | categorical palette | Override the series colours with chart tokens. |
| `title / description` | ReactNode | — | Figure caption above the plot. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | title or Chart | Accessible name of the plot, the single keyboard stop. |
| `height` | number | type-specific | Plot height in pixels. |
| `state` | loading \| error \| empty \| invalid | from data | Force a state; empty and invalid are otherwise detected from the data. |
| `labels` | Partial<DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS> | English copy | Copy for states, the keyboard hint, the data table and its toggle. |
| `locale / formatValue` | string / Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| (value) => string | runtime / number | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `showData` | hidden \| toggle \| visible | hidden | Data table visibility; hidden keeps it available to assistive technology. |
| `onActivate / onActiveChange` | (point, index) => void / (index \| null) => void | — | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `toolbar / framed` | ReactNode / boolean | — / true | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Accessibility

The plot is one tab stop named by ariaLabel. The arrow keys walk the points, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates and Escape clears; the active point is drawn and read out politely. Every value is mirrored in a data table, and the SVG is hidden from assistive technology.

Colours come from the chart palette tokens (`--ds-color-chart-1` … `-8`, the sequential, diverging and heatmap ramps and the chart neutrals), with light and dark values checked by the token tests.

See [source notices](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

# DonutChart

Parts of a whole as a donut with a centre summary, or a pie (PieChart); slices are selectable and small ones fold into Other.

[Open the docs](http://localhost:6007/?path=/docs/charts-donutchart--docs) for the Playground and detailed examples, each with its complete JSX.

## Usage

```jsx
import { DonutChart } from '@gaudi/design-system/charts';

<DonutChart title='Where readers came from' ariaLabel='Sessions by source' data={sources} otherThreshold={0.03} onSelect={(slice) => setSource(slice?.label)} />
```

Import from `@gaudi/design-system/charts` or `@gaudi/design-system/charts/DonutChart`. Charts are not exported from the root entry, so pages without a chart never load Recharts. In an article, render the same chart through MDX/Chart.

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data / nameKey / valueKey` | object[] / string / string | [] / label / value | Slices. |
| `selectable / selectedIndex / defaultSelectedIndex / onSelect` | boolean / number \| null / number \| null / (slice, index) => void | true for donuts | Selection pins a slice; the centre shows its share. |
| `otherThreshold / maxSlices / otherLabel` | number / number / string | — / — / Other | Fold small slices into Other. |
| `centerLabel` | string | Total | Caption under the centre value. |
| `innerRadius` | string \| number | '56%' (DonutChart), 0 (PieChart) | Hole size. |
| `colors` | string[] | categorical palette | Override the series colours with chart tokens. |
| `title / description` | ReactNode | — | Figure caption above the plot. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | title or Chart | Accessible name of the plot, the single keyboard stop. |
| `height` | number | type-specific | Plot height in pixels. |
| `state` | loading \| error \| empty \| invalid | from data | Force a state; empty and invalid are otherwise detected from the data. |
| `labels` | Partial<DEFAULT_CHART_LABELS> | English copy | Copy for states, the keyboard hint, the data table and its toggle. |
| `locale / formatValue` | string / Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| (value) => string | runtime / number | Number format for axes, tooltips, the readout and the table. |
| `showData` | hidden \| toggle \| visible | hidden | Data table visibility; hidden keeps it available to assistive technology. |
| `onActivate / onActiveChange` | (point, index) => void / (index \| null) => void | — | Click, Enter or Space on a point; the active point changed. |
| `toolbar / framed` | ReactNode / boolean | — / true | Controls beside the caption; the figure border and padding. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional classes on the outer element. |

## Accessibility

The plot is one tab stop named by ariaLabel. The arrow keys walk the points, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter or Space activates and Escape clears; the active point is drawn and read out politely. Every value is mirrored in a data table, and the SVG is hidden from assistive technology.

Colours come from the chart palette tokens (`--ds-color-chart-1` … `-8`, the sequential, diverging and heatmap ramps and the chart neutrals), with light and dark values checked by the token tests.

See [source notices](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

components.name: useArrowKeyNav
components.title: Hooks/A11y/useArrowKeyNav
components.description: Moves focus between items with the arrow keys, Home and End while the group stays one Tab stop. The active item has tabIndex 0 and the rest -1. Keys typed in text fields and keys with Command, Control or Alt are left alone.
components.summary: Arrow-key navigation with a roving tabindex for toolbars, lists and grids.

props.name: itemCount
props.description: Number of navigable items; the active index is clamped when items are removed.

props.name: options.orientation
props.description: Which arrow keys move: Up and Down, Left and Right, or all four.

props.name: options.wrap
props.description: Loop from the last item to the first and back.

props.name: options.dir
props.description: In right-to-left layouts ArrowLeft moves forward.

props.name: options.role
props.description: Container role; aria-orientation is added for roles that support it (toolbar, listbox, menu, tablist…).

props.name: options.defaultIndex
props.description: Initial active item, and a callback when it changes.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Initial active item, and a callback when it changes.

returns.name: containerProps
returns.description: Spread on the container, then give it an accessible name.

returns.name: setActiveIndex(index, { focus })
returns.description: Move the active item from code; focuses it unless focus is false.

components.accessibility: Implements the WAI-ARIA roving tabindex pattern: one Tab stop for the group, arrows inside it. Name the container (aria-label or aria-labelledby) and give it the role the widget really is, such as toolbar.
notes: Gaudi Tabs, ToggleGroup, RadioGroup and menus already handle their own arrow keys.
`getNextIndex(current, key, options)` is exported for custom key handling.

components.name: useFocusTrap
components.title: Hooks/A11y/useFocusTrap
components.description: While active, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the container. On activation it focuses the first tabbable element (or the container), and on release it returns focus to where it was. Traps nest, and portaled menus inside the trap keep their own focus.
components.summary: Keep Tab focus inside a custom overlay and restore it on close.

props.name: options.active
props.description: Whether the trap is on.

props.name: options.autoFocus
props.description: Move focus into the container when it activates.

props.name: options.initialFocus
props.description: Focus the first tabbable element or the container itself (give it tabIndex={-1}).

props.name: options.returnFocus
props.description: Return focus to the previously focused element on release.

props.name: options.containerRef
props.description: Use an existing ref instead of the returned one.

components.accessibility: A trap must always have a visible, keyboard-reachable way out (a Close button and Escape). Pair it with role="dialog", aria-modal and a label, and with useScrollLock so the page behind does not scroll.
notes: Gaudi Dialog, Dialog confirmation, Sheet and Drawer already trap focus; use this hook only for custom overlays.

components.name: useLiveAnnouncer
components.title: Hooks/A11y/useLiveAnnouncer
components.description: Announces short messages ("Saved", "3 results", "Copied") through shared visually hidden live regions. The regions exist before the first message so it is not lost, and repeating a message announces it again.
components.summary: Polite or assertive screen reader announcements for changes away from focus.

props.name: options.clearAfter
props.description: Milliseconds before an announced message is cleared from the region.

components.accessibility: Use 'polite' for almost everything. Reserve 'assertive' for errors and time-critical changes, keep messages short, and never announce every keystroke or streamed token.
notes: `announce(message, politeness)` is also exported for non-React code.

components.name: usePrefersReducedMotion
components.title: Hooks/A11y/usePrefersReducedMotion
components.description: True when the operating system reduce-motion setting is on, updated live. Built on useMediaQuery.
components.summary: Whether the reader asked to reduce motion.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Value during server rendering and hydration.

returns.name: reduced
returns.description: True when motion should be reduced.

components.accessibility: When set, skip autoplay, parallax, typing effects and smooth scrolling, or replace them with an instant change. global.css already shortens CSS transitions; use this hook for motion driven from JavaScript.
notes: `REDUCED_MOTION_QUERY` is exported for CSS-in-JS or imperative checks.

components.name: useLocalStorage
components.title: Hooks/Data/useLocalStorage
components.description: Stores a JSON value under a key. The server render and hydration use the initial value, and the stored value is read right after. Every caller with the same key stays in sync in this tab and in other tabs; blocked storage falls back to memory.
components.summary: useState persisted to localStorage, synced across components and tabs.

props.name: key
props.description: Storage key; namespace it, for example reader:font-size.

props.name: initialValue
props.description: Value on the server, during hydration and when nothing is stored.

props.name: options.serialize
props.description: Custom encoding.

props.name: deserialize
props.description: Custom encoding.

props.name: options.syncTabs
props.description: Follow writes from other tabs.

returns.name: [2] removeValue
returns.description: Delete the key and fall back to initialValue.

components.accessibility: Persisted preferences (text size, reduced motion, dismissed notices) must still have a visible control to change them back.
notes: Never store secrets, tokens or personal data in localStorage.
components.usage:
import { useLocalStorage } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const [fontSize, setFontSize, resetFontSize] = useLocalStorage('reader:font-size', 'md');

components.name: useMap
components.title: Hooks/Data/useMap
components.description: Accepts a Map or iterable of key-value pairs. Each mutation creates a new Map, preserving caller-owned input. The initial entries are snapshotted once, including single-use iterators; reset copies that snapshot.
components.summary: Map state with immutable set, replace, remove, clear and reset actions.

props.name: initialEntries
props.description: Initial contents, snapshotted at mount for reset. Later changes to this argument are ignored; use setAll to replace state.

returns.name: actions.set / remove / setAll / clear / reset
returns.description: Set one key, remove a key, replace all entries, empty the Map or restore the initial entries.

components.accessibility: Render stable keys and keep focus meaningful when entries are removed.
notes: Do not call map.set/delete/clear directly; those mutations cannot notify React.
components.usage:
import { useMap } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const [drafts, { set, remove, reset }] = useMap([['intro', 'Draft']]);

components.name: useReadLocalStorage
components.title: Hooks/Data/useReadLocalStorage
components.description: Reads through the same store as useLocalStorage, including same-tab notifications, native cross-tab storage events and blocked-storage fallback. It never exposes write actions.
components.summary: Read-only localStorage subscriptions shared with useLocalStorage.

props.name: key
props.description: Storage key to subscribe to.

props.name: initialValue
props.description: Server, hydration, absent-key and invalid-JSON fallback.

props.name: options.deserialize
props.description: Custom reader and whether to subscribe to cross-tab changes.

props.name: syncTabs
props.description: Custom reader and whether to subscribe to cross-tab changes.

components.accessibility: Announce meaningful changes in context. Do not put sensitive data in browser storage.
notes: Same-tab changes made with useLocalStorage notify readers. Direct localStorage.setItem calls in the same tab do not dispatch a storage event.
components.usage:
import { useReadLocalStorage } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const density = useReadLocalStorage('reading-density', 'comfortable');

components.name: useSelection
components.title: Hooks/Data/useSelection
components.description: Tracks selected ids for lists, tables and bulk actions. Uncontrolled from initialSelectedIds, or controlled with selectedIds and onSelectionChange; every change produces a new Set.
components.summary: Multi-select state in a Set, with select-all and indeterminate support.

props.name: options.selectedIds
props.description: Controlled selection.

props.name: options.initialSelectedIds
props.description: Initial selection when uncontrolled.

props.name: options.onSelectionChange
props.description: Called with the next selection.

components.accessibility: Give every checkbox a label naming its row, give the select-all checkbox an indeterminate state, and announce bulk results (for example with useLiveAnnouncer).
notes: DataTable has its own selection; use this hook for custom lists, galleries and cards.
components.usage:
import { useSelection } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { isSelected, toggleSelection, getSelectAllState, toggleAll, count } = useSelection();

components.name: useSessionStorage
components.title: Hooks/Data/useSessionStorage
components.description: The same API as useLocalStorage over sessionStorage: survives a reload, not a new tab. Good for wizard progress and half-filled forms.
components.summary: useState persisted to sessionStorage for one tab.

props.name: key
props.description: Storage key.

props.name: initialValue
props.description: Value on the server, during hydration and when nothing is stored.

props.name: options.serialize
props.description: Custom encoding.

props.name: deserialize
props.description: Custom encoding.

returns.name: [2] removeValue
returns.description: Delete the key and fall back to initialValue.

components.accessibility: Restoring a form after a reload helps people who navigate slowly or lose their place; tell them the draft was restored and let them clear it.
notes: Session storage is per tab, so there is no cross-tab sync.
components.usage:
import { useSessionStorage } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const [draft, setDraft, clearDraft] = useSessionStorage('contact:draft', { name: '', message: '' });

components.name: useDocumentTitle
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useDocumentTitle
components.description: The most recently mounted enabled hook owns the title. Updating that owner updates the title; removing it restores the remaining owner or the original title, even if owners unmount out of order.
components.summary: Set a document title and restore the previous owner on cleanup.

props.name: title
props.description: Title to display.

props.name: options.enabled
props.description: Disable without changing the document title.

returns.name: return
returns.description: Title changes happen in effects; server output is unchanged.

components.accessibility: Use concise page titles that identify the current content. Avoid rapidly changing titles or announcing pointer movement.
notes: Use framework metadata for server-rendered page titles. This hook handles client-owned surfaces.
components.usage:
import { useDocumentTitle } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

useDocumentTitle('Draft · Writing room');

components.name: useIsClient
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useIsClient
components.description: Defers browser-only output (theme toggles, local times, storage-backed values) without a hydration mismatch, and without the extra render of a mounted flag set in an effect.
components.summary: False on the server and during hydration, true on the client.

returns.name: isClient
returns.description: True once rendering on the client.

components.accessibility: Render a same-size placeholder on the server so the layout does not jump and focus order does not change when the client value appears.
notes: The ThemeSwitch uses it for its mounted state.

components.name: useIsMobile
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useIsMobile
components.description: The breakpoint the AppShell sidebar and DateSelector use to switch to their phone layouts. False during server rendering and hydration.
components.summary: True below the 768px phone breakpoint.

returns.name: isMobile
returns.description: True when the viewport is narrower than 768px.

components.accessibility: Switching layouts must not remove features: the phone layout should reach the same actions, often through a Sheet or Drawer.
notes: Built on useMediaQuery; use that directly for other breakpoints.

components.name: useIsMounted
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useIsMounted
components.description: Returns a getter that is false during server rendering and before its mount effect, true while mounted and false after cleanup. Checking it does not cause a render.
components.summary: A stable getter for whether this hook is currently mounted.

returns.name: isMounted()
returns.description: Read the mount state when an asynchronous callback completes.

components.accessibility: Keep pending, success and cancellation feedback visible to users.
notes: This does not cancel work or protect against stale responses after props change. Prefer AbortController or request identity for those cases.
Use useIsClient for a reactive hydration flag. React Strict Mode replays effects in development.
components.usage:
import { useIsMounted } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const isMounted = useIsMounted();

components.name: useMediaQuery
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useMediaQuery
components.description: Returns whether a media query matches and follows changes. Returns the fallback during server rendering and hydration so markup stays stable; client-only renders read the real value at once. Merges two earlier implementations.
components.summary: Track a CSS media query, SSR-safe.

props.name: query
props.description: A media query such as '(min-width: 1024px)'.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Value during server rendering and hydration.

components.accessibility: Prefer CSS for purely visual changes. Use the hook when the tree really differs (one pane instead of two), and keep the same content and controls reachable in both layouts.
notes: `matchesMediaQuery(query)` and `subscribeMediaQuery(query, notify)` are exported for non-React code.
components.usage:
import { useMediaQuery } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const wide = useMediaQuery('(min-width: 1024px)', true);

components.name: useOnlineStatus
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useOnlineStatus
components.description: Follows the online and offline events. False is reliable: queue work and say so. True only means 'maybe' (a captive portal reports online), so request errors stay the source of truth.
components.summary: Whether the browser reports a network connection.

returns.name: online
returns.description: False when the browser is offline; true during server rendering.

components.accessibility: Show offline state as text (an Alert or a status region), not only as a colour, and keep entered work.
notes: Do not block reading content offline; disable only the actions that need the network.

components.name: usePageVisibility
components.title: Hooks/Environment/usePageVisibility
components.description: True while the page is visible. Pause polling, carousels, video and animation loops when the reader switches tabs, and resume when they return.
components.summary: Whether the tab is visible, to pause work in the background.

returns.name: visible
returns.description: False while the tab is hidden; true during server rendering.

components.accessibility: Pausing hidden work also stops rotating content from moving on while the reader is away, so they return to what they left.
notes: Combine with useInterval: pass null as the delay while hidden.

components.name: usePrefersColorScheme
components.title: Hooks/Environment/usePrefersColorScheme
components.description: Follows the system preference live. This is not the site theme: read the active theme from the theme provider, and use this hook for system-default choices such as an embed or a chart palette.
components.summary: The operating system colour scheme: 'light' or 'dark'.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Value during server rendering and hydration.

components.accessibility: Both schemes must meet contrast requirements; use Gaudi tokens, which resolve per theme.
notes: Built on useMediaQuery.
components.usage:
import { usePrefersColorScheme } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const scheme = usePrefersColorScheme();

components.name: useScreen
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useScreen
components.description: Measures after mount and refreshes on window resize and screen-orientation changes. Returns a plain snapshot instead of the browser's mutable Screen object.
components.summary: Read a reactive snapshot of the browser screen properties.

returns.name: screen
returns.description: Undefined on the server. Includes width, height, availWidth, availHeight, colorDepth, pixelDepth, orientation and angle.

components.accessibility: Use viewport or container size for responsive layout; display size does not describe the space available to your component.
notes: Dimensions are screen CSS pixels and may be reduced or rounded by browser privacy settings. Orientation and angle are null when unavailable.
components.usage:
import { useScreen } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const screen = useScreen();

components.name: useScript
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useScript
components.description: Callers using the same resolved URL share one script. A null source or disabled hook stays idle. No URL is built in, and Storybook uses a local inert fixture. The copied example includes the public file location and contents to create in your app.
components.summary: Load an explicitly configured script with shared status and ownership.

props.name: src
props.description: Host-supplied script URL.

props.name: options.enabled
props.description: Whether this caller requests the script.

props.name: options.removeOnUnmount
props.description: Remove a hook-owned script after its final caller leaves, only if no caller requested retention.

returns.name: status
returns.description: Loading on server for enabled sources; idle for disabled/absent sources. Unknown means a pre-existing script has no observable load status.

components.accessibility: Provide text for loading/error states and an alternative when an integration is unavailable.
notes: Removing a script tag cannot undo code it already ran. Prefer retaining shared libraries.
Pre-existing scripts are never removed. Mark known external script state with data-gaudi-script-status="ready" or wait for its load/error event.
Failed retained scripts stay error; use a new URL or removeOnUnmount to release the failed entry before retrying.
components.usage:
import { useScript } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const status = useScript('/scripts/local-preview.js', { enabled: previewOpen });

components.name: useWindowSize
components.title: Hooks/Environment/useWindowSize
components.description: Reads the window after mount and updates on resize. Unchanged dimensions keep the same result object. The server and first client render use the supplied initial dimensions.
components.summary: Track layout viewport width and height in CSS pixels.

props.name: options.initialWidth
props.description: Deterministic dimensions before the first client measurement.

props.name: initialHeight
props.description: Deterministic dimensions before the first client measurement.

returns.name: size
returns.description: Layout viewport dimensions, not device screen or visual viewport dimensions.

components.accessibility: Prefer CSS responsive layout or useMediaQuery for breakpoints. Avoid hiding essential content based only on viewport size.
components.usage:
import { useWindowSize } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { width, height } = useWindowSize();

components.name: useCopyToClipboard
components.title: Hooks/Interaction/useCopyToClipboard
components.description: Writes text with the Clipboard API and falls back to a hidden textarea (restoring focus and selection) where the API is blocked. isCopied resets after the timeout. Merges two earlier implementations: copyToClipboard and copy are the same function.
components.summary: Copy text with a temporary copied state and a fallback.

props.name: options.timeout
props.description: Milliseconds before isCopied resets; 0 keeps it. A number may be passed instead of the options.

props.name: options.onCopy / onError
props.description: Called after a successful or failed copy.

returns.name: copy(text) / copyToClipboard(text)
returns.description: Copy; resolves to whether it worked.

components.accessibility: Keep the button name stable ("Copy link") and announce the result in a polite status region; swapping only the icon is not announced.
notes: CodeBlock already has a copy button; use this hook for custom copy actions.

components.name: useEventListener
components.title: Hooks/Interaction/useEventListener
components.description: Attaches a listener to window (default), document, an element or a ref, and removes it on unmount. The latest handler always runs without re-subscribing, and refs are re-read after every commit so the listener follows conditional elements.
components.summary: Declarative DOM event listener with cleanup.

props.name: eventName
props.description: DOM event such as 'keydown', 'scroll' or 'resize'.

props.name: handler
props.description: Called for each event; may change on every render.

props.name: target
props.description: Where to listen; null detaches.

props.name: options
props.description: capture, passive, once and signal.

returns.name: (nothing)
returns.description: The listener lives as long as the component.

components.accessibility: Keyboard listeners on window or document must not swallow keys that belong to focused controls; check event.target and event.defaultPrevented.
notes: Mark scroll and touch listeners passive so they never delay scrolling.

components.name: useHotkey
components.title: Hooks/Interaction/useHotkey
components.description: Runs a callback for a combination such as 'mod+k' (Command+K on macOS, Control+K elsewhere), 'shift+?' or 'escape'. Skips plain keys while the reader types in a field, and returns aria-keyshortcuts and Kbd keys for the hint.
components.summary: Keyboard shortcuts with platform-aware mod keys.

props.name: keys
props.description: One or more combinations: 'mod+k', 'ctrl+shift+p', '/', 'escape'.

props.name: callback
props.description: Called when a combination matches.

props.name: options.enabled
props.description: When and where to listen.

props.name: target
props.description: When and where to listen.

props.name: event
props.description: When and where to listen.

props.name: options.preventDefault
props.description: Stop the browser default for a matched shortcut.

props.name: options.enableInInputs / allowRepeat
props.description: Also fire in text fields, and on held-key repeats.

returns.name: kbdKeys
returns.description: Keys for Kbd, e.g. 'command,k' on macOS and 'ctrl,k' elsewhere.

components.accessibility: Every shortcut needs a visible control that does the same thing. Put aria-keyshortcuts on that control and show the keys with Kbd. Avoid single-key shortcuts unless they can be turned off (WCAG 2.1.4).
notes: `parseHotkey`, `matchHotkey`, `toAriaKeyShortcuts` and `toKbdKeys` are exported for custom handling.

stories.name: Single-key shortcuts that can be turned off

components.name: useHover
components.title: Hooks/Interaction/useHover
components.description: Tracks pointer hover through onPointerEnter and onPointerLeave. Touch pointers are ignored so a tap does not leave an element stuck in its hover state.
components.summary: Pointer hover state with props to spread, ignoring touch.

props.name: options.disabled
props.description: Stop tracking and clear the state.

props.name: options.onHoverChange
props.description: Called when hover starts or ends.

returns.name: isHovered
returns.description: Whether a mouse or pen is over the element.

components.accessibility: Hover is an enhancement. Anything revealed on hover must also appear on focus (track :focus-within or onFocus) and be reachable on touch.
notes: Use CSS :hover for purely visual effects; use the hook when hover changes behaviour, such as pausing a carousel.

components.name: useMousePosition
components.title: Hooks/Interaction/useMousePosition
components.description: Uses pointermove so mouse and pen work together. Updates at most once per animation frame, and cancels pending work when disabled or unmounted. Attach ref to measure local coordinates against an element's bounding rectangle.
components.summary: Track viewport, page and optional element-relative pointer coordinates.

props.name: options.enabled
props.description: Attach tracking listeners; disabling retains the last reading.

returns.name: x / y / pageX / pageY
returns.description: Viewport and document coordinates; null before the first move.

returns.name: elementX / elementY / isInside
returns.description: Coordinates relative to the bounding rectangle and whether the pointer is inside.

components.accessibility: Pointer readouts are supplementary. Keep every action available to keyboard and touch users; do not announce each move.
notes: Touch updates occur only while a pointer is moving. Scrolling alone does not refresh the last sample.
For an animated cursor use the existing Pointer component.
components.usage:
import { useMousePosition } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { ref, elementX, elementY, isInside } = useMousePosition();

components.name: useOnClickOutside
components.title: Hooks/Interaction/useOnClickOutside
components.description: Listens for pointerdown on the document and calls the handler when the target is outside every ref, for custom panels and inline editors. Pass several refs, such as a trigger and its panel.
components.summary: Run a callback when a press lands outside one or more elements.

props.name: ref
props.description: Element or elements that count as inside.

props.name: handler
props.description: Called on an outside press.

props.name: options
props.description: Event name ('pointerdown', 'mousedown', 'click', 'focusin'…) or options.

returns.name: (nothing)
returns.description: The listener lives as long as the component.

components.accessibility: An outside click is a pointer shortcut. Also close on Escape and return focus to the trigger, so keyboard users can dismiss the panel.
notes: Popover, Dialog, Select and menus already dismiss themselves.
components.usage:
import { useOnClickOutside } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

useOnClickOutside([triggerRef, panelRef], () => setOpen(false), { enabled: open });

components.name: useScrollLock
components.title: Hooks/Interaction/useScrollLock
components.description: Sets overflow hidden on the body while locked and pads it by the scrollbar width so content does not shift. Locks from several components nest; the last release restores the page.
components.summary: Lock page scrolling while a custom overlay is open.

props.name: locked
props.description: Whether scrolling is locked.

returns.name: (nothing)
returns.description: The lock is released on unlock or unmount.

components.accessibility: Lock scrolling together with a focus trap, so neither the pointer nor the keyboard reaches the page behind the overlay.
notes: Dialog, Sheet and Drawer lock scrolling themselves.
`lockScroll()` returns a release function for non-React code.

components.name: useCollapsibleSections
components.title: Hooks/Layout/useCollapsibleSections
components.description: Coordinates individual and bulk disclosure for settings pages, filter sidebars, FAQs and inspectors. The initial expansion is read once; onChange receives the expanded ids after each change. The pure reducer is exported too.
components.summary: Expanded state for several sections, with expand all and collapse all.

props.name: config.sections
props.description: Every section id.

props.name: config.initialExpanded
props.description: Sections open at first, or all of them.

props.name: expandAll
props.description: Sections open at first, or all of them.

props.name: config.onChange
props.description: Called after each change.

components.accessibility: Render each section with Collapsible or Accordion so triggers expose aria-expanded. Disable "Expand all" when everything is open rather than hiding it, so the controls do not move.
notes: `collapsibleSectionsReducer`, `createCollapsibleSectionsState` and `areAllSectionsExpanded` are exported.
components.usage:
import { useCollapsibleSections } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const sections = useCollapsibleSections({ sections: ['profile', 'billing', 'privacy'], initialExpanded: ['profile'] });

stories.name: Settings with expand and collapse all

components.name: useElementSize
components.title: Hooks/Layout/useElementSize
components.description: Measures the border box and follows resizes, for container-driven layouts, truncation and drawing at real pixel sizes. Returns a callback ref and the size; onResize receives each size without a render.
components.summary: An element's size, kept current with a ResizeObserver.

props.name: options.initialSize
props.description: Size on the server and before the first measurement.

props.name: options.onResize
props.description: Called with each measured size.

props.name: options.round
props.description: Round to whole pixels.

components.accessibility: Size-driven layouts must still reflow at 400% zoom and keep reading order; prefer CSS container queries when only styles change.
notes: Charts measure themselves; use this for your own canvases and layouts.

components.name: useInView
components.title: Hooks/Layout/useInView
components.description: For lazy sections, "load more" sentinels, reading progress and reveal effects. With once, it stops observing after the element is first seen.
components.summary: Whether an element is in the viewport, from an IntersectionObserver.

props.name: options.root
props.description: IntersectionObserver options.

props.name: rootMargin
props.description: IntersectionObserver options.

props.name: threshold
props.description: IntersectionObserver options.

props.name: options.once
props.description: Stop after the first time the element is in view.

props.name: options.initialInView
props.description: Value on the server and without IntersectionObserver.

props.name: options.onChange
props.description: Called on each change.

components.accessibility: Never hide content until it scrolls into view for readers without JavaScript or with reduced motion; keep "load more" available as a real button too.
notes: Set initialInView to true for content that must render without JavaScript.

stories.name: Load a section when it is reached

components.name: useScrollPosition
components.title: Hooks/Layout/useScrollPosition
components.description: Follows window scrolling, or the element in targetRef, with a passive listener. 0 during server rendering.
components.summary: The vertical scroll offset of the page or a scroll container.

props.name: options.targetRef
props.description: Scroll container to follow instead of the window.

components.accessibility: A back-to-top control revealed by scrolling should stay in the tab order (hidden with inert or visibility, not just opacity) and move focus sensibly.
notes: Updates on every scroll event; throttle derived work with useThrottleCallback.

stories.name: Reading progress in a scroll container

components.name: useBoolean
components.title: Hooks/State/useBoolean
components.description: Keeps on/off state without disclosure-specific ARIA. Values and functional updates are normalized to booleans; the initial value is also the server value.
components.summary: Generic boolean state with stable toggle, enable and disable actions.

props.name: initialValue
props.description: Initial on/off value.

returns.name: setValue / setTrue / setFalse / toggle
returns.description: Set directly or through an updater, enable, disable, or invert the value.

components.accessibility: Use aria-pressed on toggle buttons or checked on switches. Use useDisclosure for a control that reveals a region.
notes: Covers the boolean useToggle use case with one API.
components.usage:
import { useBoolean } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { value, toggle, setTrue, setFalse } = useBoolean(false);

components.name: useControllableState
components.title: Hooks/State/useControllableState
components.description: The component owns the state until its host passes value; then the host accepts, refuses or replaces each change offered through onChange. The setter takes a value or an updater and skips unchanged values. DataTable uses it.
components.summary: State that works controlled or uncontrolled, like native inputs.

props.name: options.value
props.description: Controlled value; undefined means uncontrolled.

props.name: options.defaultValue
props.description: Initial value when uncontrolled.

props.name: options.onChange
props.description: Called with each change.

components.accessibility: Controlled components must still reflect every change visibly and to assistive technology (checked, expanded, selected), even when the host refuses it.
notes: Decide once: switching between controlled and uncontrolled during a component life is not supported.

stories.name: Controlled, with the host refusing changes

components.name: useCountdown
components.title: Hooks/State/useCountdown
components.description: Composes useInterval with count state. Changing the interval restarts the timer interval; reset stops it and restores the current countStart. Counts represent ticks, not elapsed wall-clock time.
components.summary: A pausable countdown or count-up that stops at its target.

props.name: options.countStart
props.description: Starting value and terminal value.

props.name: countStop
props.description: Starting value and terminal value.

props.name: options.intervalMs
props.description: Positive milliseconds per tick; invalid values stop the timer.

props.name: options.isIncrement
props.description: Count up toward the target instead of down.

returns.name: count / isRunning
returns.description: Current count and whether the timer is advancing.

returns.name: start / stop / reset
returns.description: Start or resume, pause, or stop and reset.

components.accessibility: Keep pause and reset controls available. Avoid announcing every tick; announce completion separately.
notes: Timers can be throttled in background tabs. Use an application deadline for time-critical expiry.
Starting at or beyond the target does not run.
components.usage:
import { useCountdown } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { count, isRunning, start, stop, reset } = useCountdown({ countStart: 30 });

components.name: useCounter
components.title: Hooks/State/useCounter
components.description: Functional updates compose within one event. Reset returns to the current initialValue argument. The hook imposes no product-specific bounds.
components.summary: A number with increment, decrement, set and reset actions.

props.name: initialValue
props.description: Initial and reset value, also used on the server.

returns.name: increment / decrement / reset / setCount
returns.description: Change by one, reset, or assign a number or functional update.

components.accessibility: Give increment and decrement buttons meaningful names; announce changes only when useful.
components.usage:
import { useCounter } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

const { count, increment, decrement, reset } = useCounter(1);

components.name: useDebounceCallback
components.title: Hooks/State/useDebounceCallback
components.description: Runs the latest callback once, delay ms after the last call, with the latest arguments: autosave, search requests and resize work. Pending work is cancelled on unmount.
components.summary: A debounced function with cancel and flush.

props.name: callback
props.description: The work to run.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds after the last call.

returns.name: debounced.cancel / flush / isPending
returns.description: Drop pending work, run it now, or check for it.

components.accessibility: For autosave, show and announce the saved state once the debounced save finishes, and flush on blur so work is not lost.
notes: `createDebouncer(callback, delay)` is exported for non-React code.

components.name: useDebounceValue
components.title: Hooks/State/useDebounceValue
components.description: Delays a fast-changing value, such as a search query, until it has been still for the delay, so filtering and requests do not run on every keystroke.
components.summary: A value that updates only after it stops changing.

props.name: value
props.description: The live value.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds of stillness before updating.

components.accessibility: Announce result counts after the debounced update, not per keystroke, so screen readers are not flooded.
notes: Use useDebounceCallback when you need cancel or flush.

components.name: useDisclosure
components.title: Hooks/State/useDisclosure
components.description: Open state for dialogs, menus, drawers and custom disclosures, controlled or uncontrolled, with getTriggerProps for a custom trigger.
components.summary: Open, close and toggle state for overlays and disclosures.

props.name: options.open / defaultOpen
props.description: Controlled or initial state.

props.name: options.onOpenChange
props.description: Called with each change.

props.name: options.id
props.description: Id of the controlled region, added as aria-controls by getTriggerProps.

returns.name: getTriggerProps(props)
returns.description: Spread on a custom trigger button.

components.accessibility: A custom trigger must be a button with aria-expanded and, when the region is in the page, aria-controls; getTriggerProps adds both.
notes: Gaudi overlays take open and onOpenChange directly: pass them through.

components.name: useEventCallback
components.title: Hooks/State/useEventCallback
components.description: Pass handlers to effects, subscriptions and memoised children without re-running them when an inline callback changes. Call it from events and effects, not during render.
components.summary: A stable function that always calls the latest callback.

props.name: callback
props.description: The latest implementation.

returns.name: stableCallback
returns.description: Same identity for the component lifetime.

components.accessibility: No direct accessibility impact; it keeps listeners stable so focus and announcements are not reset by re-subscriptions.
notes: Do not call the returned function during render.

components.name: useInterval
components.title: Hooks/State/useInterval
components.description: Calls the callback every delay ms. Pass null to pause; the callback can read fresh state without restarting the interval.
components.summary: setInterval that can pause and always runs the latest callback.

props.name: callback
props.description: Called on each tick.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds between ticks; null or false pauses.

components.accessibility: Content that moves or updates automatically for more than five seconds needs a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2); pass null while paused.
notes: Pause in hidden tabs with usePageVisibility.
components.usage:
import { useInterval } from '@gaudi/design-system/hooks';

useInterval(() => setSeconds((s) => s + 1), running ? 1000 : null);

components.name: useIsomorphicLayoutEffect

components.readme:
# AeroShards

Asymmetric, folded shards tumble through a broad stream with perspective depth and pearl reflections. RGB edge separation follows the camera position. Hold the pointer to gather the stream, then release to unfurl it.

```jsx
import { AeroShards } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/AeroShards';

<AeroShards height={500} paused={paused} />
```

- `paused` (boolean, default false): Freeze the current frame. Reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers also stop animation.
- `speed` (number, default 1): Playback multiplier from 0 to 5. Zero freezes time.
- `intensity` (number, default 1): Visibility of the shards, clamped to 0–2. Zero shows only the background color.
- `scale` (number, default 1): Spatial scale from 0.25 to 4. Larger values produce larger details.
- `colors` (string[], default Gaudi theme colors): Up to three CSS colors. Omit to follow the current Gaudi theme.
- `background` (string, default var(--ds-color-surface)): CSS color behind the effect, also used by the static fallback.
- `interactive` (boolean, default true): The pointer repels nearby shards. Press and hold to gather a rotating cloud; release to unfurl. Input stops while paused.
- `height` (number | string, default 360): Container height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096; width fills the available container.
- `children` (ReactNode, default —): Accessible foreground content layered above the decorative canvas.
- `className / style / ref` (DOM props, default —): Applied to the outer div. Standard DOM attributes and handlers are forwarded.

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Foreground children remain readable and interactive. Provide a pause control for continuous motion, and place text on a contrasting surface. Reduced motion displays a still frame; unavailable WebGL uses a static color fallback.

A bounded mesh of 1,280 independently positioned shards uses four non-coplanar triangular faces per shard. Size, depth, shape and roll vary independently. Holding gathers the same particles into individual circulating orbits; release restores their stream trajectories without resetting time. Narrow containers crop the same world span instead of concentrating the entire particle count into a phone-sized field.

The private renderer shares Gaudi’s canvas lifecycle, uses depth testing for overlapping facets, and releases its mesh, shaders, texture and depth framebuffer on unmount or context replacement. This is an original approximation of the rendered reference; alternate upstream materials, formations and presets are not included.

Visual idea inspired by [AeroShards](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/aero-shards) from [React Bits](https://reactbits.dev). Independently implemented for Gaudi from the rendered visual reference; no React Bits source code, shaders or assets are included.

components.readme:
# Aurora (Borealis)

Theme-aware Aurora light curtains, with a Soft Aurora variant that forms a narrow glowing ribbon.

```jsx
import Borealis from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/Borealis';

<Borealis variant="soft" height={500}>{content}</Borealis>

// A band across the top of a page: no fill, faint behind the text column, faded top and bottom.
<Borealis height={560} transparent mask="text" />
```

Existing root, layout barrel and `@gaudi/design-system/layout/Borealis` imports remain supported. Direct children and the ref stay on the outer page wrapper. Without a height, the wrapper grows with content and fills at least the viewport; the decoration is capped at 48rem.

## Contract

- `variant` ("aurora" | "soft", default `aurora`): Top-lit curtains or a soft horizontal ribbon. Unknown values fall back to aurora.
- `amplitude` (number, default `1`): Height variation of the light, clamped to 0–2.
- `blend` (number, default `0.5`): Softness of the glow, clamped to 0–1.
- `fadeEdges` (boolean, default `true`): Fade the decorative layer into the page at its lower edge.
- `paused` (boolean, default `false`): Freeze the current frame. Reduced motion, offscreen containers and hidden tabs also stop animation.
- `speed` (number, default `1`): Animation speed multiplier, clamped to 0–5. Zero holds a static frame.
- `intensity` (number, default `1`): Effect strength, clamped to 0–2. Zero reveals the background color.
- `scale` (number, default `1`): Spatial scale of the effect, clamped to 0.25–4.
- `colors` (string[], default `Gaudi theme tokens`): Up to three CSS colors. Omitted colors inherit the current Gaudi palette.
- `background` (string, default `var(--ds-color-surface)`): CSS color behind the effect and its static fallback.
- `transparent` (boolean, default `false`): Drop the decoration's background fill so masked or faded areas reveal the page behind. The light itself still blends towards `background`.
- `mask` (`'bottom'` | `'edges'` | `'text'` | `'none'` | string, default `fadeEdges`): Canvas fade. `bottom` melts into the page below, `edges` fades in at the top and out at the bottom, `text` also stays faint behind leading-edge text and follows writing direction. Any other string is a CSS `mask-image` whose layers intersect. Replaces the `fadeEdges` fade when set; `none` removes both.
- `height` (number | string, default `content / viewport`): Optional fixed height in pixels or CSS length. Without it, the existing page wrapper grows with content and fills at least the viewport; decoration is capped at 48rem.
- `children` (ReactNode, default `—`): Optional semantic content layered above the decorative canvas.
- `className / style / ref / DOM props` (DOM props, default `—`): Forwarded to the outer container.

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep important content in children and provide a pause control for continuous animation. Reduced motion renders a static frame; unsupported WebGL retains the styled container and content.

## Visual references

Inspired by [React Bits Aurora](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/aurora) and [Soft Aurora](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/soft-aurora) (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently authored for Gaudi; no upstream source, shaders or assets are included.

components.readme:
# CRTWarp

Cellular plasma islands split and reconnect through broad stepped phosphor contours, curved scanlines, and analog grain.

```jsx
import { CRTWarp } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/CRTWarp';

<CRTWarp height={360} speed={1} intensity={1} interactive />
```

Two displaced fields drift independently to form irregular islands that merge and separate. Several nested brightness bands preserve dark space between saturated cores; separated phosphor channels and a continuous halo soften the coarse contours. Signal cells use CSS pixels, and barrel curvature bends both the field and its fine scanlines. Grain covers the whole signal, including dark areas. Pointer motion locally bends the field when `interactive` is enabled. The supplied palette remains visible without washing every core toward white.

## Contract

- `paused=false` freezes the current frame when enabled. `speed=1` accepts 0–5; zero stops time.
- `intensity=1` accepts 0–2. `scale=1` accepts 0.25–4. Invalid numbers use safe defaults.
- `colors` optionally supplies up to three CSS colors; defaults come from the current Gaudi theme. `background` defaults to `var(--ds-color-surface)`.
- `interactive=false` enables pointer response when set. Content and controls retain their normal pointer behavior.
- `height=360` accepts pixels or a CSS length; numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. The canvas fills its container with a device pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and a drawing buffer of approximately two million pixels at most.
- `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and DOM attributes belong to the outer container. Children render above the canvas.

The shared renderer pauses for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and releases its observers, animation frame and WebGL resources on unmount. Server output is deterministic. A static styled background remains available when WebGL fails.

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep meaningful text and controls in semantic children. Provide a pause control for continuous motion and maintain text contrast when layering content over the effect.

## Visual reference

Inspired by the visual idea of [React Bits CRT Warp](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/crt-warp) (MIT + Commons Clause). This is an independent Gaudi implementation; no upstream component source, shader or asset is redistributed.

## Contract

- `scale` (number, default `1`): Spatial scale of the effect, clamped to 0.25–4.
- `colors` (string[], default `Gaudi theme tokens`): The first CSS color supplies the tint; omitted colors inherit Gaudi theme tokens.
- `background` (string, default `var(--ds-color-surface)`): CSS color behind the effect and its static fallback.

# GradientWaves

Broad, softly lit swells roll toward a hazy horizon, with atmospheric depth and subtle pointer parallax.

```jsx
import { GradientWaves } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/GradientWaves';

<GradientWaves height={360} speed={1} intensity={1} interactive />
```

The shader traces a continuous height field with broad foreground swells. Surface lighting and distance haze soften receding crests; pointer movement subtly shifts the viewpoint.

## Contract

- `paused=false` freezes the current frame when enabled. `speed=1` accepts 0–5; zero stops time.
- `intensity=1` accepts 0–2. `scale=1` accepts 0.25–4. Invalid numbers use safe defaults.
- `colors` optionally supplies up to three CSS colors; defaults come from the current Gaudi theme. `background` defaults to `var(--ds-color-surface)`.
- `interactive=false` enables pointer response when set. Content and controls retain their normal pointer behavior.
- `height=360` accepts pixels or a CSS length; numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. The canvas fills its container with a device pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and a drawing buffer of approximately two million pixels at most.
- `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and DOM attributes belong to the outer container. Children render above the canvas.

The shared renderer pauses for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and releases its observers, animation frame and WebGL resources on unmount. Server output is deterministic. A static styled background remains available when WebGL fails.

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep meaningful text and controls in semantic children. Provide a pause control for continuous motion and maintain text contrast when layering content over the effect.

## Visual reference

Inspired by the visual idea of [React Bits Gradient Waves](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/gradient-waves) (MIT + Commons Clause). This is an independent Gaudi implementation; no upstream component source, shader or asset is redistributed.

<LightPillar height={360} paused />

- `children` (ReactNode, default —): Optional content rendered above the decorative canvas. Keep text and controls on a contrasting surface.
- `className / style / ref` (DOM props, default —): Applied to the outer div along with other DOM props and pointer handlers.

components.readme:
# LiquidEther

Colored dye follows pointer movement, curls through a retained velocity field, and gradually dissipates.

```jsx
import { LiquidEther } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/LiquidEther';

<LiquidEther height={360} speed={1} intensity={1} interactive />
```

A bounded velocity and dye simulation retains, transports, and dissipates each plume. Pointer movement adds dye and momentum; an autonomous drifting source runs when the pointer is absent. Pausing and zero-delta redraws preserve the field, and a seeded plume provides a deterministic reduced-motion still.

## Contract

- `paused=false` freezes the current frame when enabled. `speed=1` accepts 0–5; zero stops time.
- `intensity=1` accepts 0–2. `scale=1` accepts 0.25–4. Invalid numbers use safe defaults.
- `colors` optionally supplies up to three CSS colors; defaults come from the current Gaudi theme. `background` defaults to `var(--ds-color-surface)`.
- `interactive=true` injects dye along pointer movement; set it to false for autonomous motion only. Content and controls retain their normal pointer behavior.
- `height=360` accepts pixels or a CSS length; numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. The canvas fills its container with a device pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and a drawing buffer of approximately two million pixels at most.
- `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and DOM attributes belong to the outer container. Children render above the canvas.

The shared renderer pauses for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and releases its observers, animation frame and WebGL resources on unmount. Server output is deterministic. A static styled background remains available when WebGL fails.

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep meaningful text and controls in semantic children. Provide a pause control for continuous motion and maintain text contrast when layering content over the effect.

## Visual reference

Inspired by the visual idea of [React Bits Liquid Ether](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/liquid-ether) (MIT + Commons Clause). This is an independent Gaudi implementation; no upstream component source, shader or asset is redistributed.

# ParticleSea

A rolling sea of fine points seen in perspective; crests catch the light and glitter.

```jsx
import { ParticleSea } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/ParticleSea';

<ParticleSea height={500} waveHeight={1.2} colors={['var(--ds-color-warning)']} />
```

Points are spaced evenly across the water, so they shrink and crowd towards the horizon. Only crests are lit, and each point twinkles on its own phase. Points too small to resolve fade out instead of shimmering. Change `waveHeight` or `speed` to give different content its own sea.

## Contract

- `waveHeight` (number, default `1`): Swell height, clamped to 0–2. Higher seas light more crests.
- `density` (number, default `1`): Points per unit of water, clamped to 0.25–2.
- `horizon` (number, default `0.75`): Horizon position from the bottom of the container, clamped to 0.3–1. The area above it shows the background.
- `paused` (boolean, default `false`): Freeze the current frame. Reduced motion, offscreen containers and hidden tabs also stop animation.
- `speed` (number, default `1`): Animation speed multiplier, clamped to 0–5. Zero holds a static frame.
- `intensity` (number, default `1`): Brightness of the lit points, clamped to 0–2. Zero reveals the background color.
- `scale` (number, default `1`): Spatial scale of the sea, clamped to 0.25–4.
- `colors` (string[], default `Gaudi theme tokens`): Up to three CSS colors for the points. Omitted colors inherit the current Gaudi palette.
- `background` (string, default `var(--ds-color-surface)`): CSS color behind the effect and its static fallback.
- `interactive` (boolean, default `false`): Lift the sea under the pointer without capturing clicks or scrolling.
- `height` (number | string, default `360`): Container height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096; width fills the available container.
- `children` (ReactNode, default `—`): Optional semantic content layered above the decorative canvas.
- `className / style / ref / DOM props` (DOM props, default `—`): Forwarded to the outer container.

The shared renderer caps drawing at 30fps, device pixel ratio at 1.5, and its buffer at approximately two million pixels. It stops for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and cleans up its GPU resources on unmount. A static fallback preserves the content if WebGL is unavailable.

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep important content in children and provide a pause control for continuous animation. Reduced motion renders a static frame; unsupported WebGL retains the styled container and content.

components.readme:
# Plasma

Translucent plasma folds flow across the surface, with soft illuminated edges.

```jsx
import { Plasma } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/Plasma';

<Plasma height={500} paused={false} />
```

The flowing field uses broad folds with narrow illuminated rims. Pointer interaction adds subtle parallax.

## Contract

- `direction` ("forward" | "reverse", default `forward`): Direction of the flowing folds.
- `turbulence` (number, default `1`): Fold distortion, clamped to 0–2.
- `paused` (boolean, default `false`): Freeze the current frame. Reduced motion, offscreen containers and hidden tabs also stop animation.
- `speed` (number, default `1`): Animation speed multiplier, clamped to 0–5. Zero holds a static frame.
- `intensity` (number, default `1`): Effect strength, clamped to 0–2. Zero reveals the background color.
- `scale` (number, default `1`): Spatial scale of the effect, clamped to 0.25–4.
- `colors` (string[], default `Gaudi theme tokens`): Up to three CSS colors. Omitted colors inherit the current Gaudi palette.
- `background` (string, default `var(--ds-color-surface)`): CSS color behind the effect and its static fallback.
- `interactive` (boolean, default `false`): Let pointer position influence the effect without capturing clicks or scrolling.
- `height` (number | string, default `360`): Container height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096; width fills the available container.
- `children` (ReactNode, default `—`): Optional semantic content layered above the decorative canvas.
- `className / style / ref / DOM props` (DOM props, default `—`): Forwarded to the outer container.

The shared renderer caps drawing at 30fps, device pixel ratio at 1.5, and its buffer at approximately two million pixels. It stops for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and cleans up its GPU resources on unmount. A static fallback preserves the content if WebGL is unavailable.

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep important content in children and provide a pause control for continuous animation. Reduced motion renders a static frame; unsupported WebGL retains the styled container and content.

## Visual reference

Inspired by [React Bits Plasma](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/plasma) (MIT + Commons Clause). This is an independent Gaudi implementation; no upstream source, shaders or assets are redistributed.

# ShapeWaves

Ten-pixel cells cycle through triangle, circle and square bands, with optional text carved out of the field.

```jsx
import { ShapeWaves } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/ShapeWaves';

<ShapeWaves height={500} paused={paused} />
```

- `text` (string, default ''): Optional text cut out of the decorative canvas and exposed once to assistive technology. Foreground children remain unmasked.
- `textSize` (number, default 0.6): Cutout height relative to the surface, clamped to 0.1–1. Long text shrinks to fit.
- `cellSize` (number, default 10): Grid pitch in CSS pixels, clamped to 4–40.
- `dotSize` (number, default 0.75): Glyph size as a fraction of a cell, clamped to 0.1–0.95.
- `paused` (boolean, default false): Freeze the current frame. Reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers also stop animation.
- `speed` (number, default 1): Playback multiplier from 0 to 5. Zero freezes time.
- `intensity` (number, default 1): Visibility of the geometric marks, clamped to 0–2. Zero shows only the background color.
- `scale` (number, default 1): Spatial scale from 0.25 to 4. Larger values produce larger details.
- `colors` (string[], default Gaudi theme colors): Up to three CSS colors. Omit to follow the current Gaudi theme.
- `background` (string, default var(--ds-color-surface)): CSS color behind the effect, also used by the static fallback.
- `interactive` (boolean, default true): Moving the pointer leaves fading light; clicking sends a spreading ripple. Input stops while motion is paused.
- `height` (number | string, default 360): Container height in pixels or a CSS length. Numeric values are clamped to 1–4096; width fills the available container.
- `children` (ReactNode, default —): Accessible foreground content layered above the decorative canvas.
- `className / style / ref` (DOM props, default —): Applied to the outer div. Standard DOM attributes and handlers are forwarded.

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Foreground children remain readable and interactive. Provide a pause control for continuous motion, and place text on a contrasting surface. Reduced motion displays a still frame; unavailable WebGL uses a static color fallback.

Scale changes wave size while cellSize controls glyph density. Dark bands are triangles, middle bands circles and bright bands squares.

components.readme:
# WebThreads

Six luminous strands fan outward from one bright central pinch, with soft glow around each thread.

```jsx
import { WebThreads } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/WebThreads';

<WebThreads height={360} speed={1} intensity={1} interactive />
```

Six curves meet at one compact luminous knot and fan broadly toward the edges. Pointer movement adds a local light and a subtle horizontal drift; scale changes the curve frequency.

## Contract

- `paused=false` freezes the current frame when enabled. `speed=1` accepts 0–5; zero stops time.
- `intensity=1` accepts 0–2. `scale=1` accepts 0.25–4. Invalid numbers use safe defaults.
- `colors` optionally supplies up to three CSS colors; defaults come from the current Gaudi theme. `background` defaults to `var(--ds-color-surface)`.
- `interactive=false` enables pointer response when set. Content and controls retain their normal pointer behavior.
- `height=360` accepts pixels or a CSS length; numeric values are clamped to 1–4096. The canvas fills its container with a device pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and a drawing buffer of approximately two million pixels at most.
- `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and DOM attributes belong to the outer container. Children render above the canvas.

The shared renderer pauses for reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers, and releases its observers, animation frame and WebGL resources on unmount. Server output is deterministic. A static styled background remains available when WebGL fails.

## Accessibility

The canvas is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Keep meaningful text and controls in semantic children. Provide a pause control for continuous motion and maintain text contrast when layering content over the effect.

## Visual reference

Inspired by the visual idea of [React Bits Web Threads](https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/web-threads) (MIT + Commons Clause). This is an independent Gaudi implementation; no upstream component source, shader or asset is redistributed.

- `duration` (number, default 1200): Reveal duration in milliseconds, clamped to 100–10000.
- `direction` (start | end | center, default "start"): Order in which the original letters are revealed.
- `trigger` (view | hover, default "view"): Begin on entering view, or wait for hover/focus. Hover and focus can replay either mode.
- `characterSet` (string, default "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"): Glyphs used for the decorative character rendering. Empty input uses a safe fallback.
- `paused` (boolean, default false): Stop nonessential motion. System reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers also stop it.
- `className / style / ref` (DOM props, default —): Applied to the outer span. Typography is inherited.
