components.readme:
# GlyphInspector

Inspect animated letter outlines with a gliding frame, floating square particles, measurement guides and a live readout. Hover to take control; drag and release a letter to return it to its slot.

```jsx
import { GlyphInspector } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/GlyphInspector';

<GlyphInspector text="Gaudi" paused activeIndex={2} />
```

- `text` (string, default "Gaudi"): Text to display. Keep it short enough for the chosen font size.
- `autoplay` (boolean, default true): Step the inspector through the letters while no letter is hovered or held.
- `draggable` (boolean, default true): Allow decorative letters to be lifted a short distance; release returns them to their slot. Does not change the text.
- `readout` (boolean, default true): Show the inspected character, its code point and its measured size (or drag offset) below the frame.
- `guides` (boolean, default true): Draw faint horizontal guides along the top and bottom of the inspected letter across the line.
- `interval` (number, default 900): Milliseconds between automatic steps, clamped to 200–10000 before applying tempo.
- `outline` (dashed | dotted | solid, default "dashed"): Stroke style of the inspected letter outline.
- `accent` (string, default "currentColor"): Color of the frame, guides and readout.
- `particles` (number, default 12): Number of drifting square particles around the frame, rounded and clamped to 0–40. Set 0 to hide them.
- `tempo` (number, default 1): Speed multiplier for automatic inspection, outline tracing and particles, clamped to 0.25–3.
- `reveal` (letter | area | none, default "letter"): Outline the inspected letter, softly reveal nearby letter outlines around the pointer, or keep all letters filled.
- `radius` (number, default 120): Area reveal radius in CSS pixels, clamped to 20–400. Only used with reveal="area".
- `paused` (boolean, default false): Stop motion and dragging while keeping the inspector visible at `activeIndex`, even with `autoplay={false}`. System reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers also stop motion.
- `activeIndex` (number, default 0): Zero-based character index to inspect when paused. Counts Unicode code points, including spaces. Out-of-range, non-integer or non-finite values fall back to 0. Empty text shows no inspector. Ignored while running.
- `className / style / ref` (DOM props, default —): Applied to the outer span. Typography is inherited.

The complete text is exposed once; decorative letters are hidden from assistive technology. Hover and drag do not change the text. Reduced motion removes animated inspection and dragging; an explicitly paused inspector remains visible without motion. Provide a pause control for continuous autoplay.

Typography is inherited and shrinks to fit the available width. The component reserves space for its particles, readout and bounded drag movement.

Visual idea inspired by [Tech Text](https://reactbits.dev/text-animations/tech-text) from [React Bits](https://reactbits.dev) (MIT + Commons Clause). Independently implemented for Gaudi; no React Bits code or assets are included.

# PhraseCycle

```jsx
import { PhraseCycle } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/PhraseCycle';

<PhraseCycle texts={["Create", "Explore"]} />
```

- `interval` (number, default 2200): Milliseconds between phrase changes, clamped to 700–30000. Each transition uses the focal motion duration (560 ms).
- `direction` (up | down, default "up"): Direction of the vertical transition.
- `paused` (boolean, default false): Stop nonessential motion. System reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers also stop it.
- `className / style / ref` (DOM props, default —): Applied to the outer span. Typography is inherited.

All phrases are exposed once as stable text, without a live region. Reduced motion shows the first phrase. Pausing keeps the current phrase visible. Provide a pause control for continuous cycling.

components.description: A formatted value whose digits spin into place on slot-machine reels, landing left to right.

props.name: value
props.description: The value to show, already formatted. Digits become reels; every other character stays fixed.

props.name: duration
props.description: Milliseconds the first reel takes to land, clamped to 0–4000.

props.name: stagger
props.description: Milliseconds between consecutive reels landing, left to right, clamped to 0–400.

props.name: paused
props.description: Swap values without motion. System reduced motion, hidden tabs and offscreen containers do the same.

props.name: className / style / ref
props.description: Applied to the outer span. Typography is inherited.

components.readme:
# ReelText

A formatted value whose digits spin into place on slot-machine reels. Use it for figures that change in place, such as a metric switching period; it is how `StatCard` animates its value with `valueMotion='reel'`.

```jsx
import { ReelText } from '@gaudi/design-system/animations/ReelText';

<ReelText value='$31,904' />
```

Pass the value already formatted. Each digit is a 0–9 reel that rolls to its digit with a fast start and a soft landing (`--ds-motion-ease-out`); reels land left to right, `stagger` milliseconds apart, the first after `duration`. Separators, currency signs and letters stay fixed, and characters are matched from the end, so `999` → `1,000` spins only digits. The first paint rolls up from zero.

The root is one image with the whole value as its accessible name; the reels are hidden from assistive technology. Reduced motion, `paused`, hidden tabs and offscreen containers swap the value without motion.

Motion inspired by Arc's Slot text.

components.readme:
# Chart (MDX)

The MDX adapter for the Charts collection. Authors write `<Chart type=… />` in an article, or any chart by name from the MDX component map, and get the same framed, accessible chart an application renders from `@gaudi/design-system/charts`.

[Open the docs](http://localhost:6007/?path=/docs/mdx-chart--docs) for the Playground and an article that renders a chart inside its prose.

## In an article

```mdx
Search still brings in most readers, and the newsletter has grown every month.

<Chart
  type='line'
  title='Readers by channel'
  ariaLabel='Monthly readers by channel'
  data={[{ label: 'Jan', search: 1840 }, { label: 'Feb', search: 2110 }]}
  yKey='search'
/>

<DonutChart title='Essays by topic' data={[{ label: 'Data', value: 42 }, { label: 'Engineering', value: 28 }]} />
```

The blog loads the adapter on demand with `dynamic(() => import('@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Chart'))`; `MDXComponents` from `@gaudi/design-system/mdx` also maps every chart by name.

## Types

`type` picks the chart; every other prop goes to it. Each type has its own page under **Charts** with detailed examples.

| `type` | Chart |
| --- | --- |
| `bar`, `line`, `area`, `composed`, `range`, `sparkline` | BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart, ComposedChart, RangeChart, Sparkline |
| `waterfall`, `funnel`, `sankey` | WaterfallChart, FunnelChart, SankeyChart |
| `pie`, `donut`, `bar-list`, `treemap` | PieChart, DonutChart, StackedBarList, TreemapChart |
| `histogram`, `box-plot`, `scatter`, `bubble` | HistogramChart, BoxPlotChart, ScatterChart, BubbleChart |
| `gauge`, `radial`, `radar`, `heatmap` | GaugeChart, RadialBarChart, RadarChart, HeatmapChart |

Keyboard reading, the data table, the loading, empty, invalid and error states, and locale formatting come from the chart's frame; see `Charts/ChartFrame`.

See [source notices](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

components.name: Citation
components.title: MDX/Citation
components.description: Citation documents the blog citation authoring flow and the Gaudi runtime components that hydrate generated citation links.
components.overview: Use citations in three places. Authors put BibTeX files in the blog, list those files in post frontmatter, and cite keys directly in prose with Pandoc-style brackets. The blog MDX pipeline runs rehypeSimpleCitations, which converts those text markers into numbered anchors plus a generated References section. Gaudi does not parse BibTeX or rewrite MDX; it only provides the runtime CitationPopover and CitationTracker behavior for the generated markup.
components.accessibility: Generated citation links are real anchors with readable labels. Popovers open on hover or focus, grouped references remain individually reachable, and CitationTracker keeps bibliography back-links pointed at the most recent citation instance.
notes: The authoring API is markdown citation syntax, not a React component API.

`rehypeSimpleCitations` is the blog rehype plugin. It loads BibTeX through `citation-js`, assigns first-use numbers, supports grouped citations, emits citation anchors, and appends the References list.
`CitationPopover` binds to generated anchors marked with `data-citation-popover` and reads the generated citation keys, numbers, and reference text from data attributes.
`CitationTracker` updates bibliography back-links so a reference points back to the most recent citation instance the reader used.
dos: Add BibTeX files to `data/meta/bibliography` in the blog repo.
List the BibTeX files in post frontmatter with `bibliography: ['meta/bibliography/references.bib', 'meta/bibliography/kg.bib']`.
Cite one source with `[@HusseinYC18]` and grouped sources with `[@HusseinYC18; @WangJSWYCY19; @YangXJWHW20]`.
Let `rehypeSimpleCitations` generate numbered anchors, popover data attributes, and the References section.
Use `CitationPopover` and `CitationTracker` only as runtime hydration for the generated citation markup.
donts: Do not hand-write `<sup>`, `citation-link` classes, `data-citation-*` attributes, or References markup in MDX.
Do not import `CitationPopover` or `CitationTracker` inside individual MDX posts.
Do not use `CitationPopover` as a manual popover for arbitrary text; it expects generated citation anchors.
consumerResponsibilities: Keep BibTeX source files in the blog, usually under `data/meta/bibliography`. They do not belong in the design-system package.
Register `rehypeSimpleCitations` in the blog MDX/content pipeline so citation text is transformed before React renders the article.
Mount `CitationTracker` once in the app layout and mount `CitationPopover` near the rendered article content.
Keep citation keys in MDX prose exactly matched to the BibTeX ids in the bibliography files.
components.usage:
---
title: 'An Introduction to Knowledge Graphs'
bibliography: ['meta/bibliography/references.bib', 'meta/bibliography/kg.bib']
---

A heterogeneous graph [@HusseinYC18; @WangJSWYCY19; @YangXJWHW20] assigns types to nodes and edges.

The same source can be cited again later [@HusseinYC18].

<!-- Do not hand-write citation anchors, popover data attributes, or references markup. -->

components.name: Footnote
components.title: MDX/Footnote
components.description: Footnote hydrates generated markdown footnote references with hover and focus popover previews.
components.overview: Authors do not write a React component for each footnote. They write standard markdown footnote syntax in the post. The blog MDX pipeline extracts the definitions, enhances the generated footnote reference anchors with `data-footnote-*` attributes, and may visually collapse the bottom notes section. Gaudi only owns the small client runtime that reads those generated attributes and shows the preview popover on hover or keyboard focus.
components.accessibility: Generated footnote references are real anchors, so readers can still jump to the notes list. `Footnote` adds hover and focus previews without replacing the underlying link or removing the accessible footnote relationship.
notes: `Footnote` listens for `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`, `focusin`, and `focusout` on generated links marked with `data-footnote-popover="true"`.
The popover body is read from generated `data-footnote-content`, so the plugin must sanitize and serialize the note content before runtime.
The component positions the popover next to the reference and flips left when it would overflow the viewport.
The visible footnotes list remains the source of truth; the popover is a reading convenience.
dos: Write standard markdown footnotes with `[^id]` references and `[^id]: note text` definitions.
Let `remarkFootnoteData` extract note content and let `rehypeFootnotePopoverV2` attach popover data to generated reference links.
Use `Footnote` as a page-level runtime binder after the article has rendered.
Keep footnote copy short enough for a compact popover; long supporting material belongs in the visible footnotes section.
donts: Do not hand-write `data-footnote-*` attributes in article MDX.
Do not use `<Footnote />` as an inline MDX component or wrapper around footnote text.
Do not hide the underlying footnote references without preserving anchor navigation and focus behavior.
consumerResponsibilities: Enable markdown footnotes in the blog MDX pipeline with `remarkGfm`.
Run `remarkFootnoteData` before rehype so footnote definitions are available on `file.data.footnotes`.
Run `rehypeFootnotePopoverV2` after footnotes are converted to HTML so reference anchors receive `data-footnote-popover`, `data-footnote-number`, and `data-footnote-content`.
Mount `Footnote` once near the rendered MDX article, not inside the MDX document itself.
components.usage:
Inline prose can use a normal markdown footnote reference.[^model-note]

[^model-note]: This explanatory note can include links, emphasis, and short supporting context.

<!-- Runtime wiring lives outside the post:
app layout/page shell: <MDXLayoutRenderer ... />
article runtime: <Footnote />
-->

<!-- The blog pipeline generates anchors with data-footnote-popover, data-footnote-number, and data-footnote-content. -->

notes: `remarkLinks` converts external `http` and `https` markdown links into `Preview` MDX text elements with `url` and optional `title` attributes.
`rehypeInternalLinks` converts matching internal blog anchors like `/blog/category/slug` into `Preview internal` elements after markdown has become HAST.
External previews call the configured endpoint; without one nothing is fetched. Unavailable URLs render a red fallback link instead of breaking article content.
Internal previews skip remote fetching and can use local metadata supplied by the app or generated pipeline.

What each link shows (repository stars and language, video channel and duration, article author and date, post author and counts, Wikipedia excerpts) is decided by `normalizeLinkPreview` in Core/LinkPreview; the adapter only keeps the pipeline props. Images the payload lacks come from the app's `resolveImage`.
The endpoint resolves from the `endpoint` prop, then `SiteConfigProvider preview={{ endpoint }}`; with neither, links render from `previewData` or as plain links without fetching.
dos: Write normal markdown links such as `[assaf.website](https://assaf.website)` in MDX posts.
Use direct `<Preview />` only in React pages, custom layouts, or deterministic docs examples with `previewData`.
Use `internal` for local blog links that should render internal metadata without remote preview fetching.
Provide `title` when the source text is not enough or when deterministic rendering matters.
donts: Do not rewrite ordinary article links by hand when markdown syntax can express the link.
Do not rely on the hover card as the only place a title or destination appears.
Do not fetch external preview metadata inside the design-system package; the consuming app owns the API route.
consumerResponsibilities: Register `remarkLinks` in the blog remark pipeline so external markdown links become `Preview` MDX elements.
Register `rehypeInternalLinks` in the blog rehype pipeline so internal blog anchors become `Preview internal` elements after markdown has become HTML.

Expose a preview route (the blog uses `/api/preview`) for external metadata fetching, caching, and failure handling, and configure it with `SiteConfigProvider preview={{ endpoint }}` (or `LayoutContainer preview`). There is no default endpoint.
Configure `preview.resolveImage` (a function or a template map) for derived images such as video thumbnails, repository cards or page screenshots; Gaudi ships no image services.
Keep `Preview` in the `MDXComponents` map so generated MDX JSX can resolve at render time.
recovery: Preserve the original destination link while preview metadata loads or fails, so navigation never depends on the enrichment API.
Name the unavailable preview and keep the supplied title visible; a failed hover card must not become an empty interaction.

components.readme:
# Preview (MDX)

The `<Preview>` element the blog's markdown pipeline generates for links (`remarkLinks` for external links, `rehypeInternalLinks` for internal ones). It is a thin adapter over the Core [LinkPreview](../../core/LinkPreview/README.md): rendering, kinds and the normaliser live there.

```jsx
import { Preview } from '@gaudi/design-system/mdx';

<Preview url='https://assaf.website' title='assaf.website' previewData={payload} />
```

Props: `url`, `title`, `internal`, `previewData`, `showImage`, `defaultOpen`, `timeout`, `variant`, `orientation`, `endpoint`, `resolveImage`, `onLoad`, `onError`, `fallback`, `className`.

## No built-in network access

Gaudi loads nothing on its own. The adapter fetches metadata only from an endpoint the app configures, and shows images only from the payload or the app's `resolveImage`. Without either, links render from `previewData` or as plain links. Stories pass static `previewData`.

## What the blog must add (2026-10-02)

The blog relied on two defaults that were removed: the implicit `/api/preview` endpoint and the Microlink screenshot fallback for pages without an Open Graph image (plus the YouTube thumbnail and GitHub Open Graph card derived from the URL). Pass them once through the layout (or `SiteConfigProvider`):

```jsx
// Plain data, so it can be passed from the server LayoutContainer.
const preview = {
  endpoint: '/api/preview',
  resolveImage: {
    video: 'https://img.youtube.com/vi/{videoId}/maxresdefault.jpg',
    repository: 'https://opengraph.githubassets.com/1/{owner}/{repo}',
    wikipedia: null, // Wikipedia shows its excerpt instead
    default: 'https://api.microlink.io/?url={url}&screenshot=true&meta=false&embed=screenshot.url'
  }
};

<LayoutContainer preview={preview} …>   // or <SiteConfigProvider preview={preview}>
```

`resolveImage` may also be a function `({ kind, url, host, data, videoId, repository }) => string | null`, but a function cannot cross from a server component to the client provider, so the template map is the simplest fit for the blog's server `LayoutContainer`. See the [LinkPreview images notes](../../core/LinkPreview/README.md#images).

components.readme:
# Table

This Gaudi owner includes **table**, with shared primitives and article framing.

Import the documented composition from `@gaudi/design-system/mdx/Table`. Existing convenience names are preserved; compound roots use explicit aliases where needed.

[Open the first example](http://localhost:6007/?path=/story/mdx-table--basic) for the complete JSX and public imports. The Storybook catalogue lists every variant and use case under this owner.

Provide visible labels for controls, preserve heading order, and connect controlled values to application state. The examples exercise keyboard and accessibility behavior; application networking and persistence remain consumer responsibilities.

See [reconciliation and compatibility details](../../../../README.md#component-catalogue) and [source notices](../../../../README.md#third-party-notices).

## Shared headers and density

`TableRoot` is the unframed primitive; the default `Table` adds article scrolling, sticky columns and framing. Both accept `density='compact' | 'normal' | 'comfortable'` (default `normal`). Density changes spacing only. `TableHeadPrimitive` (or article `TableHeaderCell`) preserves label casing and uses the same 14px, medium-weight style as DataTable and DataGrid. Its `variant='muted'` default uses the muted surface; `'plain'` uses the surface colour.

Use the supplied row and cell parts, including in MDX mappings. `TableRoot` accepts `containerProps` for the scrolling wrapper, such as `role`, `tabIndex`, and `aria-label`. `TableCellPrimitive as='th' scope='row'` creates a body row header without applying column-header styling. The Header consistency story compares all four implementations and checks their computed styles and sorting.

components.readme:
# Post A semantic list entry for the blog. Storybook's **Blocks → Blog → Post lists** shows image cards, featured and recent articles, horizontal rows, and a compact archive using the same component and article data as the blog pages. ```jsx import Post from '@gaudi/design-system/post/Post'; import { PostReadingTime } from '@gaudi/design-system/post/PostHeader';
    } footer={} />
``` `frontMatter` contains the supplied `title`, `href`, `date`, `subtitle`, `draft`, and `category` (`{ label, href }` or an unlinked string). `locale` controls date formatting; `titleAs` defaults to `h3`; `titleVariant` defaults to `index-list-title` and accepts a shared Typography variant. Applications prepare routes and content. `Post` does not infer a destination or estimate reading time. `layout` defaults to `list`, preserving the existing text index. `stacked` puts optional media above the summary. `horizontal` puts media beside the text when the list item is at least 36rem wide and stacks it below that width. `media` and `footer` accept composed content; `className` and standard list-item props pass to the outer `li`. Place entries inside a list. Use a heading level appropriate to the surrounding section and keep the title link descriptive. Cover artwork that repeats the title's purpose can use empty alt text; meaningful illustrations need a useful description. Keep unrelated buttons and category links outside the title link. Layouts in the examples use shared styles and do not duplicate post metadata rendering.

components.readme:
# Footer

One footer owner for blog and marketing pages. Import from `@gaudi/design-system/layout/Footer`.

- `standard` places navigation beside the shared `NewsletterForm`.
- `editorial` places a brand and social links beside grouped navigation.
- `centered` centers the brand, a flat list of links, social links, and copyright.
- `compact` puts the brand, flat navigation, and social links in a row when the container permits.

Supply `sections` as `{ title, links: [{ href, label }] }[]`, `socialLinks` as `{ kind, href }[]`, and `copyrightName` as a name or author object. Content and destinations belong to the host. Empty navigation and social groups are omitted. The simple variants flatten the supplied navigation groups.

`brandTitle` accepts a React node, including `GaudiBrand`; `brandDescription` supplies the supporting text. `className` and native footer attributes pass through to the landmark. Each instance generates a unique accessible heading.

`newsletterProps` goes to `NewsletterForm`. An endpoint is required to enable subscriptions; the examples use local sample responses and never subscribe an address. Custom form classes merge with the footer defaults.

The footer responds to its container, so it can be used in page layouts and inset regions. The host owns the outer width and horizontal gutters. Keep each page's footer outside its main landmark.

components.readme:
# NewsletterForm One subscription form for footer embeds and **Blocks → Marketing → Newsletter** sections. The public import remains `@gaudi/design-system/layout/NewsletterForm`. ```jsx import NewsletterForm from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/NewsletterForm';

Unsubscribe whenever you like.

 ``` The host endpoint receives a POST with `{ email }`. A successful HTTP response without an `error` value confirms the subscription. Failed requests preserve the address for retry; pending and successful forms prevent duplicate submission. Endpoint changes and unmounts abort pending work. Without an endpoint, signup is disabled and an unavailable message is shown. `title` and `description` accept content or `null`. `headingAs` defaults to `h3`; `titleVariant` optionally selects a shared Typography variant. Omit it to retain the compact heading used by existing embeds. `children` follows submission feedback. `classNames` accepts `root`, `header`, `body`, `title`, `description`, `form`, `input`, `action`, `button`, and `message`. The EmailInput owns single-address validation and caret behavior. Feedback uses an alert for errors and a status for success. All examples share this implementation; section layout styles and local sample endpoints stay in the story fixtures. The response control switches between success, error, and unavailable and resets the example. Demo addresses are never sent to a subscription service.

props.name: background

components.accessibility: Renders only a hidden, aria-hidden marker and affects decorative layers only: the background and scroll edges are aria-hidden, so no content, landmark or focus order changes.
components.readme:
# PageChrome

Turns off parts of [LayoutContainer](../LayoutContainer/LayoutContainer.js)'s site chrome for the page that renders it.

```jsx
import PageChrome from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/PageChrome';

// An About page with its own header background.
<PageChrome background={ false } />

// An article that reads sharp to the bottom of the window.
<PageChrome scrollEdges={ false } />
```

- `background` (boolean, default `true`): `false` hides the layout background: the `background` slot, or the default Borealis. Backgrounds the page renders itself are unaffected.
- `scrollEdges` (boolean, default `true`): `false` hides the page-level [ScrollEdges](../../core/ScrollArea/README.md) (those without a `targetRef`); scroll areas keep their own edges.

PageChrome renders a hidden marker that `PageChrome.css` (part of `@gaudi/design-system/styles.css`) matches with `:has()`. It needs no client JavaScript, works in server components, and the server HTML is already correct, so the chrome never flashes in. Unmounting the marker, for example on client navigation to another page, restores the chrome.

components.readme:
# PageHeader The introduction at the top of a page or section: an optional eyebrow, a title, a description and an actions slot. Server-safe, so it renders in server components. ```jsx import PageHeader from '@gaudi/design-system/layout/PageHeader'; // A list heading that stays visible while the list scrolls.
42 posts } /> {list}
``` ## Contract - `title` (ReactNode): the heading text. `titleAs` (default `h1`) sets the element and `titleVariant` (default `title-md`) the Typography style. - `titleId` (string): an ID on the heading for `aria-labelledby`. - `eyebrow`, `description` (ReactNode): optional label above and supporting text below the title. - `actions` (ReactNode): controls or meta beside the title; they wrap below it on narrow screens. - `divider` (boolean, default `false`): a bottom border in the `border` token. - `sticky` (boolean, default `false`): `sticky top-0` on the `background` token with the same border, for headers that stay visible while the content below scrolls. - `children`: extra content below the description, such as filters. - `className`, `classNames` (`root`, `eyebrow`, `title`, `description`, `actions`): style overrides. ## Accessibility Keep one `h1` per page and use `titleAs='h2'` for section headers. A sticky header covers content scrolled beneath it, so keep it compact; label the region it introduces with `aria-labelledby` pointing at `titleId`.
